author: aliasunder
body:
## What

Adds `reviews.auto_review.auto_incremental_review: false` to `.coderabbit.yaml`.

## Why

CodeRabbit re-runs an incremental review on every push to an open PR. Each
re-review reposts/edits its summary comment, which carries a large hidden
`<!-- internal state -->` blob that grows with PR history. For sessions
subscribed to PR activity, that full comment body is delivered on every
commit — heavy and noisy, and getting worse as PRs accumulate commits.

The three keys already in the file (`poem`, `sequence_diagrams`,
`review_status`) only trim small visible sections; they don't touch the
blob. `auto_incremental_review: false` is the lever that actually stops the
per-commit reposting.

## Behavior after merge

- CodeRabbit reviews **once** when a PR opens, then stays quiet through
  subsequent commits.
- Trigger a fresh pass manually with `@coderabbitai review` (or
  `@coderabbitai full review` for a from-scratch pass).

Takes effect repo-wide once on `main`, since CodeRabbit reads
`.coderabbit.yaml` from the base branch.

author: alphatownsman
body:
## What
`user_post_list` (and the identical `profile_posts_data`) paginated a user's posts with `WHERE author_id = %s ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT %s`. With only the implicit `author_id` FK index, Postgres can scan the primary-key index backwards filtering by `author_id`, exceeding the gunicorn 60s worker timeout for accounts whose newest post is far from the global max id — surfacing as `SystemExit: 1` worker aborts (EGGPLANT-1E7).

This **supersedes #1630** (which added a `(author, -id)` index). Instead of new schema, it changes the sort to `(-published, -pk)`. The planner can no longer pick the pathological backward primary-key scan, so it uses the existing `author_id` index and sorts the small per-author result set. It also matches `get_recent_posts`' declared `-published` ordering and shows federated posts in authored-time order — better UX.

## Pagination correctness
The cursor token stays a single post pk (no template change). `get_recent_posts(before_pk=...)` resolves that pk to its `published` time and filters on the full `(published, pk)` tuple:

```
published < boundary OR (published = boundary AND pk < before_pk)
```

which is exactly lexicographic-descending `(published, pk)`. So keyset paging is correct even when pk order disagrees with published order (federated posts) or two posts share a published time. If the cursor post was deleted between requests it falls back to `pk__lt` (forward progress guaranteed; self-corrects on reload).

## Test
New `test_get_recent_posts_keyset_follows_published_not_pk` proves the pk-order ≠ published-order case plus the same-timestamp pk tiebreak. Full `test_user_post_list.py` (9) and `test_n_plus_one.py` (65) pass, verified with the index **absent**.

## Sentry issue resolved
EGGPLANT-1E7

Supersedes #1630.

## 🗒️ Description / Motivation

- Implements stateless inclusion-proof verification for `BinaryMerkleTree`.
- Allows proofs to be verified using only the expected root, leaf data, and proof.

## What Changed

- Implemented `ProofVerifier<H>` for `BinaryMerkleTree<H>`.
- Added the `BinaryMerkleTree::verify()` convenience method.
- Hashes leaf pre-images using `H::hash()`.
- Reconstructs roots iteratively using sibling hashes and `ProofSide`.
- Added support for trivial single-leaf proofs.
- Added structural validation for:
  - Empty leaf data.
  - Zero leaf counts.
  - Out-of-range leaf indices.
  - Incorrect proof-path lengths.
  - Inconsistent sibling sides.

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees

- Valid proofs with correct leaf data return `true`.
- Incorrect leaf data returns `false`.
- Tampered sibling hashes return `false`.
- Proofs checked against another tree's root return `false`.
- Malformed proofs return `false` without panicking.
- Verification does not access or require a tree instance.

## Tests Added / Run

Added tests covering:

- Successful proof verification.
- Incorrect leaf data.
- Tampered sibling hashes.

Este PR simplifica el flujo principal del proyecto para dejar una experiencia mucho más clara de entrenamiento, validación y evaluación del modelo `foundation`.

También organiza mejor la configuración, el almacenamiento local de artefactos y la operación diaria mediante `Makefile`, dejando una base más limpia para seguir agregando escenarios en el futuro.

- se simplifica el flujo público de entrenamiento a un solo camino principal
- se deja `basic` como escenario activo inicial
- se reemplaza `configs/training_profiles.toml` por una configuración dividida en:
  - `configs/base.toml`
  - `configs/scenarios/basic.toml`
- se retiran del flujo público comandos que generaban confusión:
  - `sweep`
  - `list-scenarios`
  - `list-profiles`

Se mejora `Makefile` para centralizar operación diaria del proyecto:

- setup de entorno virtual
- instalación de dependencias
- validación completa
- entrenamiento
- entrenamiento desde cero
- reanudación desde último checkpoint
- evaluación visual

Se implementa una estructura local más limpia para artefactos de entrenamiento:

author: rileyr
body:
TLS siblings of the tcp fast-path knobs (the market-data gateway handoff request). The handle resolves to the underlying socket fd, so `set_nodelay` / SO_TIMESTAMPNS reuse the plain-tcp primitives and `recv_stamped_into` is `recv_into` + a kernel-timestamp capture (`last_recv_{kernel,user}_ns()`).

**The wrinkle, resolved without touching the BIO:** the kernel SCM_TIMESTAMPNS stamp rides the *socket* recvmsg, but `SSL_read` sits in front. Rather than swap OpenSSL's BIO for a recvmsg one (which would touch every TLS read — risky + CI-unverifiable), `SSL_read` does its ordinary socket read (kernel records the stamp since SO_TIMESTAMPNS is on) and the last segment's stamp is pulled with `SIOCGSTAMPNS` afterward. `user_ns` = CLOCK_REALTIME at `SSL_read` return; `kernel_ns` = 0 when the path delivered none (needs RX-timestamping hardware — same env limitation as the tcp recv_stamped).

**Validated against a live host** (example.com:443): handshake + send + recv_stamped decrypt the 828-byte response (the path doesn't break TLS) and capture the userspace stamp. The CI test proves the surface compiles + links (loopback TLS is blocked by mandatory SSL_VERIFY_PEER); the real per-record probe is `#[ignore]`.

author: vishbay
body:
## Problem

`cram sync` (the post-commit hook) rewrote `ARCHITECTURE.md` via the LLM on **every commit**. Because the context model is non-deterministic (Haiku), this produced spurious prose churn even when nothing structural changed — `ARCHITECTURE.md` showed as modified after every commit.

## Fix

Embed a `sha256` fingerprint of the repo structure inside `ARCHITECTURE.md` as an HTML comment (`<!-- cram:structure-hash … -->`). On sync, if the stored hash matches the current structure, skip the LLM rewrite entirely. SYMBOLS.md (deterministic) still refreshes every sync.

The marker travels **with the committed file**, so after a teammate pulls, their matching structure also skips the regen — no churn for them either. When structure actually changes (files added/removed/moved), the rewrite runs and the hash updates.

This keeps `ARCHITECTURE.md` a shared, committed artifact (rejected the alternative of gitignoring it, which would remove it for everyone and undercut the context layer).

## Verification

- New tests: embeds hash after regen, skips regen + leaves file byte-identical when structure unchanged, regens when structure changes.
- Full suite: 569 passed, 1 skipped.
- Confirmed live: second `cram sync` prints "Repo structure unchanged — skipping ARCHITECTURE.md regen." and makes no model call.

author: irichard00
body:
## What

Replaces the app-held **Fernet** master key with **AWS KMS** for at-rest encryption of BYOK provider keys.

Why: the Fernet design kept a single symmetric master key in app config (SSM/env) that is pulled into process memory to decrypt. Anyone who can read that key (SSM read, env/memory dump, a DB dump + the key) can decrypt **every** user's provider credential **offline, forever, with no trace**. With KMS:
- the plaintext key material **never leaves KMS** (HSM-backed),
- every Decrypt is **audited in CloudTrail**,
- access is **revocable** (key policy / IAM) and rate-limitable — a kill switch.

BYOK keys are well under KMS's 4KB Encrypt limit, so we call **Encrypt/Decrypt directly** (no envelope/data-key). `UserLLMConfig.api_key_encrypted` (BinaryField) stores the raw `CiphertextBlob` — **no schema change**.

## Backward compatibility

None needed — the assistant/BYOK feature is **unreleased**, so there is no stored Fernet ciphertext to migrate. Fernet is removed outright (no dual-read).

## Config

- `ASSISTANT_KMS_KEY_ID` — CMK id / ARN / alias (unset → assistant reports not-configured, BYOK disabled)
- `AWS_REGION` — KMS client region
- `ASSISTANT_KMS_ENDPOINT_URL` — optional endpoint override (e.g. LocalStack) for local / self-hosted setups without a real AWS account

`crypto.py` keeps the same public surface (`is_configured` / `encrypt` / `decrypt` / `rotate`), so the 3 call sites are unchanged.

## Tests

`crypto.py` is exercised with an in-memory **fake KMS** (no AWS in CI). The shared `fernet_key` fixture is renamed `kms_crypto` across the assistant + loop contract suites. Full assistant + loop suites pass locally (**100 passed**).

## Follow-up (infra, separate)

Cloud envs need a CMK + `ASSISTANT_KMS_KEY_ID` SSM param + `kms:Encrypt`/`kms:Decrypt` granted to the EC2 instance role, and the deploy bootstrap's required-keys updated (`ASSISTANT_ENCRYPTION_KEY` → `ASSISTANT_KMS_KEY_ID`). Being applied to test alongside this.

Closes #59

  ## What
  A paginated **Library** of the user's past research jobs. Each row shows the topic, date, source
  count, and overall confidence, links straight to the report (or live progress view), and can be
  deleted with an inline confirmation. Backed by `GET /api/research` and `DELETE /api/research/{job_id}`.

  ## Backend
  - `GET /api/research` — paginated list (`limit` 1–50, `offset`), newest-first, scoped to the caller.
    follow-up children survive as standalone briefs.
  - `JobRepository.list_jobs` and `JobRepository.delete_job`.

  ## Frontend
  - `/history` route — `HistoryPage` with infinite-scroll pagination (`useResearchHistory`).
  - Per row: topic, date, source count, confidence, a follow-up badge + parent link, and click-through
    to the report (completed) or progress view (in flight).
  - Delete with inline confirmation (`useDeleteResearch`), invalidating the list query on success.

  ## Testing
  - Backend: unit tests for list pagination/param clamping and delete (`204` / `404` / owner-scoping);
    integration tests for `list_jobs` joins + ordering and `delete_job` cascade + tenant scoping.
  - Frontend: `HistoryPage` (loading / empty / rows / pagination / delete-confirm) and the
    `useResearchHistory` + `useDeleteResearch` hooks.

The daemon now authenticates local UDS connections by **kernel peer-cred** (desktop-assistant#407) and the `adelie-mint` minter is retired. `client-common` dropped the `minter` module and the `minter_socket` / `minter_ttl_seconds` config fields, so this client stops setting them — the local UDS handshake is now **tokenless** (the `ConnectionConfig` defaults cover it).

author: brynne8
body:
## Problem

PR #1808 changed the Base URL input `disabled` condition from:

```tsx
(isCodexType && (authMode === 'official' || authMode === 'auth-json'))
```

to just:

```tsx
isCodexType
```

This unconditionally disables the Base URL field for **all** Codex channels, including third-party ones. Third-party Codex channels require a custom Base URL by definition — without it, the third-party option is functionally useless.

Additionally, `handleResponsesTransportChange` would overwrite a third-party channel's custom endpoint when the user switches the Responses transport protocol.

## Fix

1. **Base URL `disabled` condition**: Changed `isCodexType` to `(isCodexType && authMode !== 'third-party')`, restoring the ability for third-party Codex channels to edit their Base URL.

2. **Transport switch protection**: Added an early return in `handleResponsesTransportChange` when `isCodexType && authMode === 'third-party'`, preventing the official default URL from overwriting the user's custom endpoint on protocol switch.

## Testing

- Official Codex: Base URL remains disabled (auto-controlled by protocol)
- Auth-JSON Codex: Base URL remains disabled
- Third-party Codex: Base URL is now editable ✅
- Switching Responses transport on third-party Codex: preserves custom URL ✅

Fixes regression from #1808

## チケットへのリンク / 変更の理由 関連Issue: vektor-inc/vk-all-in-one-expansion-unit#874 管理画面の設定ページ（3カラムレイアウト = `column_3`）の左サイドナビが、WordPress 管理画面の注意文・警告文（`.notice` 等）が表示されると下に押し下げられ、ナビ下部が画面外に見切れて操作できなくなる不具合の修正です。 不具合の実体は ExUnit 本体ではなく、ExUnit が同梱する共有ライブラリ vk-admin にあるため、本リポジトリで修正します（このライブラリを同梱する他プラグインの設定画面にも同じ修正が反映されます）。 @kurudrive 数年前のものかつ意見待ちとなっていなかったので作業してしまいましたが、もし対応すること自体に何かありましたらご連絡ください。 ## 真因 WordPress コア（`wp-admin/js/common.js`）は、管理通知（admin notice）を `.wp-header-end` の直後へ移動します。`.wp-header-end` が無い場合は `.wrap` 内で最初に見つかった見出し（`h1` / `h2`）の直後へ挿入します。 `column_3` レイアウトはページに `.wp-header-end` も `h1` も持たず、DOM 上の最初の見出しが左サイドバー内の `

` になります。そのため通知がサイドバー内（タイトルとナビの間）に差し込まれ、ナビが通知の高さ分だけ下に押し下げられて画面外に出てしまいます。`column_2` は先頭に `h1` があるため通知は `h1` 直後に出て正常です。バグは `column_3` 固有でした。 ## どういう変更をしたか？ * `src/VkAdmin.php` の `admin_page_frame()` 内、全レイアウト共通の位置（`.adminLayout` の直前・`column_2` / `column_3` の分岐の外側）に、WordPress 標準の非表示マーカー `
` を 1 つ追加。 * これにより通知は常にページ最上部（メイン領域・`.adminLayout` の直前）に表示され、サイドバー内には入らなくなります。ナビは押し下げられず最初から見えるようになります（#874 解決）。 * `.wp-header-end` は WordPress 管理画面コアの CSS で非表示のため、見た目の追加要素は出ません。 変更ファイル: * `src/VkAdmin.php`（非表示マーカー + 説明コメントを追加） * `README.md`（changelog 1 行・既存エントリが英語のため英語・バージョン番号なし） ※ 旧アプローチ（左サイドナビ `.adminMain_sub_inner` の内部スクロール化）は「スクロールすれば届く」止まりで #874 の「見えない」を解消しきれないため取り下げ、暫定対応で触れていた scss / コンパイル済み css / README の暫定 changelog 行は `origin/main` 相当に戻しました。PR は「通知の表示位置の根本修正」という単一目的の差分になっています。 ## 既存ユーザーへの影響 * `column_3`: 通知がサイドバー外（ページ最上部・メイン領域）に出るようになり、ナビが見切れなくなります。データ・オプション・保存値には一切触れていません（マークアップ 1 行の追加のみ）。 * `column_2`: `.wp-header-end` は `h1` の直後に位置するため、通知の表示位置は従来（`h1` 直後）と同一です。回帰はありません。 ## 実装者の確認事項 実装者はレビュワーに回す前に以下の事を確認してチェックをつけてください。 - [x] 複数の意図の変更 （ 機能の不具合修正 + 別の機能追加など ） を含んでいないか？ → 通知の表示位置の根本修正のみ。暫定の内部スクロール CSS は revert 済み - [x] Files changed (変更ファイル)の内容は目視で確認したか？ → `git diff origin/main` で PHP のマーカー追加・README +1 行のみ、scss / css は origin/main と完全一致（差分なし）を確認済み - [x] 本当にちゃんと確認をしたか？ → はい ## プログラムの変更の場合 テストを書かないのは普通ではありません。書けるテストは極力書くようにしてください。 - [ ] 書けそうなテストは書いたか？ → マークアップ（非表示マーカー）1 行の追加で、表示位置はブラウザ（WordPress コアの JS / CSS）依存のため単体テストになじまない。視覚確認で担保する ## 変更内容について何を確認したか、どういう方法で確認をしたかなど * `php -l src/VkAdmin.php` で構文エラーがないことを確認 * `git diff origin/main` で、正味の差分が PHP のマーカー追加と README の changelog 1 行のみ、scss / css は origin/main と差分ゼロであることを確認 * WordPress コア `wp-admin/js/common.js` の admin notice 移動ロジック（`.wp-header-end` 直後へ挿入、無ければ `.wrap h1, .wrap h2` の先頭直後へ挿入）を一次ソースで確認 ## 確認スクリーンショット（Before / After） ExUnit メイン設定画面（`column_3`）に高さのあるダミー通知を表示させて確認したものです（ローカル実機）。 **Before（修正前）— 通知が左サイドバー内に入り、ナビが押し下げられて見切れる** ![before](https://github.com/vektor-inc/review-assets/blob/main/vk-admin/pr-18/before-main-setting-firstview.png?raw=true) **After（修正後）— 通知がページ上部（メイン領域）に出て、左サイドナビが最初から全項目見える** ![after](https://github.com/vektor-inc/review-assets/blob/main/vk-admin/pr-18/after-main-setting-firstview.png?raw=true)
フルページ版（クリックで展開） Before: ![before-full](https://github.com/vektor-inc/review-assets/blob/main/vk-admin/pr-18/before-main-setting.png?raw=true) After: ![after-full](https://github.com/vektor-inc/review-assets/blob/main/vk-admin/pr-18/after-main-setting.png?raw=true)

テスト通知

author: ehelbig1
body:
## What

Retires the global-`DELETE` shared-state test pattern. `setup_test_context()` began every test with a cascade of **unscoped** `DELETE FROM …` against a *shared* database (`organization_members`, `organizations`, `api_keys`, `users`, `workflows`, …), so two tests running concurrently deleted each other's rows mid-flight — surfacing as flaky FK violations / missing `api_keys`. The mitigation was a `db-shared-state` nextest group pinning 7 binaries to `max-threads = 1`, plus `--test-threads=1` in `test-integration.sh`. It also left a footgun: any new binary using the harness silently reintroduced the flake.

## How — template-database-per-test

The originally-sketched schema-per-test approach was ruled out by the **240-migration** count (re-migrating per test is far too slow). Instead each test now gets its own database via a fast `CREATE DATABASE <unique> TEMPLATE <migrated-db>` file-copy clone, dropped on scope-exit:

- **`controller/tests/common`** — `isolated_db_pool()` + a `TestDb` Drop guard that `DROP DATABASE … WITH (FORCE)`s on a dedicated OS thread (Drop is sync but we're inside the test runtime, so a runtime-in-runtime would panic). Create retries the transient *"source database is being accessed by other users"* race under concurrency. The global `DELETE` block is gone.
- **`integration_mcp_tests`** — converted to the shared helper (2 call sites), dropping its own `init_pool` + `DELETE` cleanup, so nothing writes to the `talos_ctl` template anymore.
- **`.config/nextest.toml`** — removed the now-obsolete `db-shared-state` group; those binaries run fully parallel.
- **`scripts/test-integration.sh`** — dropped `--test-threads=1` for the isolated binaries (kept only for `env_vars`, which mutates the global `DATABASE_URL` process env).
- **`scripts/lint-structural.sh`** — new **check 43**: no `init_pool()` in `controller/tests` outside `env_vars` (prevents reintroducing a shared-DB harness). CLAUDE.md list + count updated (42 → 43).

## Verification

- ✅ Harness **compiles** — `api_key_tests` + the converted `integration_mcp_tests` build clean.
- ✅ **Isolation mechanism proven end-to-end** against a live Postgres via a standalone replica of the helper: 8 concurrent tests each saw exactly their own row; the Drop teardown left **zero** leftover databases.
- ✅ SQL mechanics (concurrent `TEMPLATE` clone + `DROP … FORCE`) proven via `psql`; structural lints + `cargo fmt` green.
- ⚠️ **Not run in the authoring sandbox:** the full converted suite against the real 240-migration schema (needs a pgvector image + `sqlx-cli`; Docker was unavailable). The `quality.yml` integration job exercises it on this PR — that's the gate that confirms the converted tests *pass* (vs. just compile).

author: dkaukov
body:
## Summary

Adds BLE KISS support to the firmware.

This lets APRS apps connect to kv4p over Bluetooth Low Energy instead of USB or Bluetooth Classic.

It follows the de-facto BLE KISS API standard:
https://github.com/hessu/aprs-specs/blob/master/BLE-KISS-API.md

So it should be compatible with apps that already support BLE KISS, including the ones listed in that spec.

## Changes

* Adds BLE KISS GATT service.
* Adds TX/RX BLE characteristics.
* Handles KISS data over BLE.
* Splits outgoing data based on BLE MTU.
* Tracks BLE connection and notify subscription state.
* Sends the normal kv4p `HELLO` once the BLE client is ready.
* Adds BLE as another protocol transport next to USB and Bluetooth Classic.

author: verifiedcoder
body:
`WellKnownTypeHandler.ConvertAny`/`WriteAnyJson` treated `Any.value` as UTF-8 JSON text in both directions. Per the protobuf spec, `value` must hold the binary protobuf of the embedded message, resolved by `@type` — so an `Any` payload from a real server rendered as `@type` plus JSON-ish text, and outgoing `Any` values were wire-incompatible with conformant servers.

Adds `AnyTypeResolver`, which indexes the transitive `FileDescriptor` closure of the message being processed plus the built-in well-known types, and resolves an `Any` `type_url` to its `MessageDescriptor`. The `Any` (de)serialization moves onto `SimpleDynamicMessage` (where the containing descriptor — hence the closure — is in hand):

- **JSON → wire:** resolve `@type`, build the embedded message (regular messages inline their fields; special well-known types use the `{"@type":..,"value":..}` form), serialize to binary into `Any.value`. An unresolvable `@type` is a clear error rather than silent JSON bytes.
- **wire → JSON:** resolve `@type`, decode the binary value, inline the fields (or emit the special-form value). Unresolvable types fall back to `{"@type":..,"@error":"type not found","value":"<base64>"}` (upstream-grpcurl style) so nothing is lost.

The dead static `ConvertAny`/`WriteAnyJson` and their JSON-text-based tests are removed. New `AnyWireFormatTests` cover, against real protobuf descriptors: binary-not-text output, full round-trip of a resolvable type, the base64 fallback, an unresolvable-input error, and well-known-type-inside-Any in both directions. Coverage is unit-level (the `SimpleDynamicMessage` round-trip is the same `ToByteArray`/`MergeFrom` path used on the wire); the shared `test.proto`/protoset fixtures are intentionally left untouched.

**Verified:** 986/986 tests, ValidationRunner 10/10, conformance 634/634 (re-run locally on the rebased base).

PR 4 of 5 (stacked; rebased onto main after #8 merged). Core-only, disjoint from earlier PRs.

author: hedone21
body:
Add the argus-chat binary: a multi-turn chat server exposing an OpenAI-compatible HTTP API (POST /v1/chat/completions, streaming + non-streaming; GET /v1/models; /health), backed by the existing ChatSession. --interactive runs a local stdin REPL instead.

- Wire the resilience manager into the chat decode loop for all three KV modes (Standard/KIVI/Offload): throttle/suspend/target-TBT control directives + per-token tick/heartbeat, mirroring the standard happy path (build_standard_loop). Standard sets the heartbeat KV handle, KIVI sets the KIVI handle; manager-driven eviction stays inert (chat manages its own eviction out-of-loop).
- ChatSampler reads a shared, per-request SamplingConfig so temperature/ top_p apply to every generated token (not just the first); TokenSampler gains a reset() hook so the stateless server clears the repetition ring between requests.
- Streaming via a DecodeEnd ChatStreamStage + a UTF-8-safe incremental detokenizer, written as Server-Sent Events directly to the connection.
- ChatTemplate gains render_user / render_assistant / assistant_header to replay a full OpenAI messages[] history (stateless per request).
- Hyphenate the argus-* binary family (argus-cli/-bench/-eval/-chat) via explicit [[bin]] + autobins=false; update CI, scripts, and docs to match.

tiny_http (blocking, no async runtime) is the only new dependency; the engine decode loop is not Send and is serialized on a single thread.

## Summary

Builds the reusable **AttributeTooltip** the spike ([#528](https://github.com/ginderjeremiah/GameServer/issues/528)) calls for and adopts it in combat, replacing the bare native `title=` on the active-effect chips. Area **D** of the spike. Both prerequisites — [#529](https://github.com/ginderjeremiah/GameServer/issues/529) (metadata) and [#531](https://github.com/ginderjeremiah/GameServer/issues/531) (icons) — have landed, so this consumes the real attribute type/description/icon data.

## What's here

**Reusable foundation**
- `components/tooltip/AttributeTooltip.svelte` — built on the shared tooltip chrome (`TooltipShell`/`TooltipTitle`/`TooltipSection`) and driven by the global tooltip store, mirroring the item/skill/reward tooltips. Content: attribute **icon + name + type** (Primary/Secondary/Status) **+ description**, from `staticData.attributes`. In the effect-chip context it also shows the effect's **direction / magnitude / duration**, reusing the `skill-effect-display` helpers so the wording/direction match the chips and the skill tooltip's "On hit" lines. Degrades gracefully (name falls back to the enum name; type/description drop out) when the reference data is unavailable.
- `components/tooltip/attribute-tooltip.svelte.ts` — `createAttributeTooltip()` registers the panel with the tooltip store and returns the reactive `attributeId`/`effect` state plus an imperative controller; `setAttributeTooltip`/`getAttributeTooltip` publish that controller down a screen via context (mirroring the reward-tooltip controller) so nested attribute surfaces don't have to thread hover handlers.
- `TooltipTitle` gains an optional `leading` snippet (for the attribute icon) — additive, so every existing tooltip renders identically.
- `attributeTypeName()` maps `EAttributeType` to its display label.

**Adoption**
- `ActiveEffectChips.svelte` — native `title=` replaced with the rich tooltip (with the effect's magnitude/direction/duration).
- Reused on the other attribute surfaces where a hover explanation helps: the **breakdown rail rows**, the **point-buy steppers** (guided + theory), and the **skill scaling chips**.

## How it addresses the issue

Delivers the component, the combat adoption (the issue's mandatory item), and the named reuse surfaces, all behind one reusable controller so future attribute surfaces can drop it in instead of a bare `title=`.

## Test plan

- **New** `AttributeTooltip.test.ts` — content assembly: icon / name / type / description present; the effect detail (signed magnitude, buff/debuff, duration) present in the chip context, including the harmful-attribute and lowered-beneficial debuff cases; core vs. neutral accent; graceful degradation with no reference data.
- **New** `attributeTypeName` cases in `attribute-display.test.ts`.
- **Updated** `ActiveEffectChips.test.ts` — hovers a chip and asserts the tooltip opens for the chip's attribute with the effect detail, then hides on leave (end-to-end controller wiring).
- `npm run lint` (eslint + svelte-check) clean — 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- Full `vitest` suite green — 1746 passed.

## Notes / follow-ups
- Static hover-trigger elements (chips, the steppers' name row, the scaling chips) carry `<!-- svelte-ignore a11y_no_static_element_interactions -->`, matching the existing house convention (`ZoneNav`). The breakdown rail rows are real `<button>`s, so they additionally get keyboard focus/blur support for free.
- Accent hues for Secondary/Status attributes remain deferred (spike decision 6); their tooltips use the neutral accent as today.

Closes #532

Additive only: `journal.user_scope` and `oauth_auth_codes.token_ttl_secs` are added via `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`. The imported data is untouched (lands as global/`user_scope IS NULL`); claim it later with the bulk-reassign tool.

- Tags **v0.5.0** + retags `hive-rust` as **:0.5.0 / :release / :latest**.

Portainer pull-and-redeploy (no `.env` change needed). Smoke-check the container reports 0.5.0; the connector then gets correct `https://` metadata and you can add it + control its session lifetime.

author: keno
body:
__julia_personality mapped the EXCEPTION_EXECUTE_HANDLER filter result to the non-standard mingw-w64 `ExceptionExecuteHandler` EXCEPTION_DISPOSITION value. That value was always undefined behavior and newer mingw-w64 has removed it, breaking the build under the GCC 16 Windows toolchain ('ExceptionExecuteHandler' undeclared in src/win32_ucontext.c). Fixes #61733.

The branch was dead anyway: jl_exception_handler (our UnhandledExceptionFilter, src/signals-win.c) only ever returns EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_EXECUTION or EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH, never EXCEPTION_EXECUTE_HANDLER. Drop the case; any non-continue-execution result now maps to ExceptionContinueSearch (unchanged behavior).

피드에 **전체공개 / 회원공개 / 비공개** 3단계 공개 범위 + 접근 제어. (DF·공유는 후속 PR)

- `Feed.published(Boolean)` → **`visibility(String)`** 마이그레이션. 기존 데이터 변환: 공개→`public`, 초안→`private`.

author: furbytm
body:
### Description of Change(s)


This PR adds all fixes inside [UpdateCommand.swift](https://github.com/wabiverse/SwiftUSD/blob/49ff8739755fb07654225f392cecf35a49b1d540/Sources/OpenUSD/Commands/UpdateCommand.swift) needed to build against past, present, and future versions of OpenUSD - including the latest changes on OpenUSD's `dev` branch. Rather than making the usual one-off manual edits across the OpenUSD codebase, the goal here is to keep the `openusd update` command robust (and contained) across OpenUSD source changes, so new fixes land as patches there rather than as scattered manual diffs that get deleted for every fresh clone of OpenUSD:
```sh
git clone https://github.com/wabiverse/SwiftUSD.git
cd SwiftUSD

# swift with openusd v26.05
# freshly clones openusd from the v26.05 release and makes all the
# required changes to work cleanly with swift across Android, Linux,
# and all Apple platforms (Windows support is a WIP).
swift package --disable-sandbox plugin openusd update v26.05
swift build
```
> you can also pass `--allow-writing-to-package-directory` and `--allow-network-connections all` to stop getting prompted for permissions every time you run this command.

or if you prefer to build the latest in-development branch of OpenUSD (latest changes from `dev`):
```sh
git clone https://github.com/wabiverse/SwiftUSD.git
cd SwiftUSD

# swift with the very latest changes from the openusd 'dev' branch, freshly clones
# openusd from the 'dev' branch and makes all the required changes to work cleanly
# with swift across Android, Linux, and all Apple platforms (Windows support is a WIP),
# 'openusd update' is built to be robust across all openusd source code changes
# (past, present, and future).
swift package --disable-sandbox plugin openusd update
swift build
```
> you can also pass `--allow-writing-to-package-directory` and `--allow-network-connections all` to stop getting prompted for permissions every time you run this command.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> All of this is quite hopeful for when SwiftPM compile-time plugins finally support feeding C/C++ code to the Swift compiler, because once that happens, we can remove all OpenUSD C/C++ code from the SwiftUSD package and leave only our pure Swift layer ([`Sources/PixarUSD`](https://github.com/wabiverse/SwiftUSD/blob/49ff8739755fb07654225f392cecf35a49b1d540/Sources/PixarUSD), and [`Sources/UsdView`](https://github.com/wabiverse/SwiftUSD/blob/49ff8739755fb07654225f392cecf35a49b1d540/Sources/UsdView)), aside from the small subset of C++ Overlay code we're using in ([`Sources/USDOverlays`](https://github.com/wabiverse/SwiftUSD/blob/49ff8739755fb07654225f392cecf35a49b1d540/Sources/USDOverlays)) (a modified version) from [apple/SwiftUsd](https://github.com/apple/SwiftUsd).
> > [C codegen is now supported in Swift v6.3, we are just awaiting C++ codegen support](https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-package-manager/pull/9730/changes#diff-6c949b8eec7699e488b612683a06ef9373d31476e27f3705fc45dcc2b0ad2619R268-R274).

> _While this does already perform some **CMake**-semantics translation for parts of OpenUSD's **CMake** build system into SwiftPM, I think there's room to go further toward a more general **CMake** → **SwiftPM** transpiler - one that translates `add_library`/`target_link_libraries` (or at least the OpenUSD-specific variants) down the line._

* Clones upstream OpenUSD, walks all of `pxr/base|exec|imaging|usd|usdImaging|usdValidation/` (plus `plugin/` subdirs) and maps every library to its SwiftPM target name.
* Splits each lib into `Sources/<Target>/` (sources) and `Sources/<Target>/include/<Target>/` (headers), rewriting every `#include "pxr/..."` to `#include "<Target>/..."`.
* Applies appropriate Swift ARC semantics for reference to pointer types, graphics interfaces, and other types across OpenUSD automatically.
* Revises some OpenUSD enums and types for syntically clean Swift APIs, while preserving the existing OpenUSD C++ code, so that there are no underlying differences in how these types are currently compiled in C++.
* Resolves **CMake** `configure_file()` `.in` templates (`@VAR@` substitution).
* Generates per-target umbrella headers (`Tf.h`, `Gf.h`, etc.) automatically from whatever headers land.
* Preserves special vendored subdirectory layouts so cross-includes still resolve: Pegtl's `internal//contrib/`, Tf's `pxr<Vendor>/` (tsl robin-map etc.), Gf's `nc/` (nanocolor), Js's `rapidjson/`, and UsdExecImaging's `pxr/exec`.
* Handles case-insensitive-filesystem collisions (`tf.h` vs `Tf.h`), umbrella-include collisions, `x`-macro fragment headers (in Sdf).
* Wraps Python-only sources in `#if PXR_PYTHON_SUPPORT_ENABLED` by scraping `CMakeLists.txt` for `PYTHON_*_CLASSES/HEADERS/PYMODULE_CPPFILES`.
* Skips `*Test_*` files (in `PXR_BUILD_TESTS`).
* Patches in Metal/ObjC for (ARC `retain`/`release` guards, Metal type shims), `opensubdiv`/`materialx` includes, `plugInfo.json` templates, `.usda` defined schemas, `.glslfx` shaders, and platform-guarded sources.
* Nukes stale generated files first so renamed/deleted upstream files don't linger as undefined behavior zombies, while preserving hand-maintained edits as overrides on top of the upstream code.

So basically it's grown into a full "upstream-to-SwiftPM transpiler/patch pipeline" for the entire OpenUSD tree, every weird edge case we've hit has a corresponding fixit in the `UpdateCommand.swift` file so future `openusd update vXX.XX` runs will reproduce the fix automatically rather than needing manual surgery again (and again).

author: a-jay85
body:
## Summary

Three roster-transaction write paths trusted a POST-supplied team name as the acting team. Each was already login-gated upstream, but none bound the action to the *session owner's* team — so any logged-in user could act as any team by changing a hidden form field. This PR derives the acting team from the authenticated session at each write site and discards the POST team value.

| ID | Hole | Fix |
|----|------|-----|
| D-06 | FA offer deletion (`FreeAgencyController::deleteOffer()` read `$_POST['teamname']`) | Derive from session, drop POST value |
| D-07 | FA offer submission (`FreeAgencyProcessor::processOfferSubmission()` read `$postData['teamname']`) | New `$verifiedTeamName` param; controller derives from session |
| D-08 | Waiver add/drop (`WaiversController::processWaiverSubmission()` read `$postData['Team_Name']`) | Derive in `executeWaiverOperation()`, pass to private method |

All three sites include a guard that rejects null / Free-Agents acting team before any processor call (the `tid=0` write prevention pattern from PR #1073).

## Changes

- `FreeAgencyController.php`: D-06 + D-07 derive-and-guard edits in `deleteOffer()` and `processOffer()`
- `FreeAgencyProcessor.php`: D-07 new `$verifiedTeamName` param; stop reading POST team
- `FreeAgencyProcessorInterface.php`: D-07 interface signature + docblock updated
- `WaiversController.php`: D-08 derive in `executeWaiverOperation()` + private `processWaiverSubmission()` signature/guard
- `FreeAgencyProcessorTest.php`: new D-07 IDOR negative/positive PHPUnit rows + update ~9 existing call sites with the new arg
- `tests/e2e/flows/free-agency-submission.spec.ts`: IDOR coverage for D-06/D-07
- `tests/e2e/flows/waivers-submission.spec.ts`: IDOR coverage for D-08

## Manual Testing

14. Does the session-team ownership binding preserve every legitimate FA-offer and waiver workflow and any commissioner/admin path — no team locked out of an action it should still have, no legit path silently broken? *(requires reviewer walkthrough — a human judges the authz negative-proof; machine gates cannot validate this)*

author: dgershman
body:
Closes #508

## Summary

Replaces the edge-triggered "needs refine" machinery shipped in #507 (1-day-old) with a stateless rule that derives the answer from the PR snapshot on every poll. Motivated by [shell-crm#202](https://github.com/radiusmethod/shell-crm/pull/202): even with #507 deployed, that PR sat in `CHANGES_REQUESTED` for 30+ minutes without Crow re-prompting after a restart — the bookkeeping that #507 added carried its own failure modes (poll loop starvation, missing persistence, dedup map drift after restart).

**The rule:** emit `.changesRequested` when ALL of:
1. PR is OPEN and `reviewDecision == CHANGES_REQUESTED`
2. `lastChangesRequestedAt` (max `submittedAt` across CHANGES_REQUESTED reviews) > `lastSubstantiveCommitAt` (max `committedDate` across commits with `parents.totalCount < 2` AND whose subject doesn't start with `Merge branch|remote-tracking|pull request`)
3. Managed terminal is idle (readiness == `.agentLaunched`, agent activity == `.idle`)
4. `AutoRespondSettings.respondToChangesRequested` is on
5. PR has been observed at least once this Crow process (first-observation skip)
6. 7 minutes have elapsed since the last dispatch for this PR (cooldown)

Anti-loop is **automatic**: any real (non-merge, non-rebase) commit advances `lastSubstantiveCommitAt` past `lastChangesRequestedAt` and the rule stops firing on the next poll. No `headShaAtEmit` snapshot needed. The GitHub "Update branch" button produces a merge commit that's filtered out upstream, so it can't trick the rule.

Restart-safe by construction: a fresh Crow process re-derives the truth on the next successful poll. The 7-min cooldown is in-memory only; worst case after restart is one duplicate prompt before the cooldown re-arms.

## Decisions made

- **Same-PR deletion, not follow-up.** The diff is easier to reason about as one atomic swap, and reverting is a single-SHA revert. Listed all deleted symbols below.
- **Cooldown of 7 min** (middle of the ticket's 5–10 min range). 7 min sits comfortably between "long enough that an agent thinking through a hard finding isn't interrupted" and "short enough that a true stall surfaces within ~3 poll cycles."
- **Tree-equals-parents check skipped** (the ticket called it optional). The merge-message + parent-count filter catches every shape I observed in the wild; the tree check would add an extra API call per PR for marginal coverage.
- **GraphQL query bumped `latestReviews(first: 5)` → `first: 20`** and added `commits(last: 30)` with `oid`, `messageHeadline`, `committedDate`, `parents.totalCount`. Per-PR cost is small; the stateless rule needs both timestamps every poll.
- **No transitions() emission for `.changesRequested`.** The pure `PRStatus.transitions(…)` function now only emits `.checksFailing`. `.changesRequested` lives entirely in `IssueTracker.applyPRStatuses` (the stateless dispatch path).

## Symbols deleted

- `PersistedIssueTrackerState` (CrowPersistence)
- `StoreData.issueTrackerState` field (decode-tolerant — existing stores ignore the key, no migration needed)
- `EmittedTransitionMeta` (CrowCore)
- `PRStatusTransition.dedupeKey`, `.latestReviewID`, `.isReFire` fields
- `PRStatus.latestReviewID` field
- `PRRecord.latestReviewID` field (replaced with `lastChangesRequestedAt`, `lastSubstantiveCommitAt`)
- `IssueTracker.emittedTransitionMeta` map
- `IssueTracker.hydratePersistedState()`, `persistTrackerState()`
- `IssueTracker.reFireStalledChangesRequested(now:)`
- `IssueTracker.shouldReFireStalledChangesRequested(meta:…)` predicate
- `IssueTracker.stalledRefireQuietWindow`, `maxStalledRefires` constants
- `IssueTracker.parseSessionID(fromDedupKey:)`, `parseKind(fromDedupKey:)` helpers
- `AppDelegate` re-fire notification skip block

## New code

- `PRStatus.needsRefine(status:terminalIdle:)` — pure rule in CrowCore. ~12 lines.
- `IssueTracker.seenPRs: Set<String>` (PR URL keyed; first-observation skip)
- `IssueTracker.lastRefineDispatchAt: [String: Date]` (PR URL keyed; cooldown)
- `IssueTracker.needsRefineCooldown` constant (7 min)
- `IssueTracker.isManagedTerminalIdle(sessionID:)` helper
- `GitHubCodeBackend.isMergeCommitMessage(_:)` helper (merge-prefix detection, shared with tests)
- `PRRecord.lastChangesRequestedAt`, `.lastSubstantiveCommitAt` fields
- `PRStatus.lastChangesRequestedAt`, `.lastSubstantiveCommitAt` fields

## Acceptance tests

All four ticket scenarios are automated:

| # | Scenario | Test |
|---|----------|------|
| 1 | Round-N stall fires on idle poll (after first-observation skip) | `IssueTrackerNeedsRefineTests.roundNStallFiresOnSecondPoll` |
| 2 | Merge-from-main does NOT reset the rule | `IssueTrackerNeedsRefineTests.mergeFromMainDoesNotFlipTheRule` + `BackendsTests.testParseMonitoredPRsLastSubstantiveCommitExcludesMergesAndRebases` |
| 3 | Real fix flips the rule off | `IssueTrackerNeedsRefineTests.realFixStopsTheRule` + `PRStatusNeedsRefineTests.doesNotFireWhenCommitIsNewerThanReview` |
| 4 | Restart-safe: skip → fire → cooldown blocks → cooldown elapses → fire again | `IssueTrackerNeedsRefineTests.restartFreshTrackerSkipsThenFiresThenCoolsDown` |

Plus defense-in-depth tests for the busy-agent, pre-launch-terminal, opt-out, missing-timestamp, closed-PR, and merge-message-shape gates. Total new/rewritten: 23 tests across 3 suites.

## Deliberate-break verifications

Each guard is pinned by a test that flips loudly when the guard is removed:

- **Remove cooldown** → `restartFreshTrackerSkipsThenFiresThenCoolsDown` poll 3 count would go from 1 to 2.
- **Remove first-observation-skip** → `roundNStallFiresOnSecondPoll` poll 1 count would go from 0 to 1.
- **Remove merge-commit filter** → `testParseMonitoredPRsLastSubstantiveCommitExcludesMergesAndRebases` would observe `lastSubstantiveCommitAt == 2026-06-07` instead of `2026-06-01`.

I read each assertion to confirm the inversion would fail loudly rather than mechanically running them (the assertions themselves are the forcing function).

## Test plan

- [x] `swift test --package-path Packages/CrowCore` — 273 tests pass (includes new `PRStatus.needsRefine (CROW-508)` suite)
- [x] `swift test --package-path Packages/CrowPersistence` — 30 tests pass (includes new "decoder ignores legacy issueTrackerState blob" coverage)
- [x] `swift test --package-path Packages/CrowProvider` — 49 tests pass (includes new commit-parsing + merge-filter tests)
- [x] `swift test` (root) — 219 tests pass (includes new `IssueTracker stateless needsRefine (CROW-508)` suite)
- [x] `swift build --arch arm64` clean
- [ ] Manual smoke: attach a `CHANGES_REQUESTED` PR with no agent push since the review → Crow re-prompts on the second poll, then waits 7 min before re-prompting.
- [ ] Manual cap check: rebase via "Update branch" → `lastSubstantiveCommitAt` does NOT advance, Crow keeps prompting on the next poll.
- [ ] Manual anti-loop check: agent pushes a real fix → `lastSubstantiveCommitAt` advances, Crow stops prompting on the next poll.

author: herbachino1776
body:
### Motivation
- The third-person Neckman view placed the character too close to camera and caused visible jitter during movement/turning, making the prototype unplayable.
- The goal is to frame Neckman as a lower-middle, over-shoulder third-person player, reduce avatar scale, and eliminate avatar/camera jitter without changing gameplay systems or attack/sword behavior.

### Description
- Camera: expanded and re-framed defaults in `ThirdPersonCameraController` with tuned values `cameraDistance: 6.1`, `cameraHeight: 3.0`, `cameraLookAtHeight: 1.42`, `cameraSideOffset: 0.22`, `cameraSmoothing: 0.18`, added `cameraPitch: -8°`, and clamped `minCameraDistance: 2.35` / `maxCameraDistance: 7.25`; collision probe minimum updated to `2.35`; camera follow target is now smoothed (`smoothedLookAt`) and the smoothing alpha formula was adjusted for frame-rate stability. (`src/game/player/ThirdPersonCameraController.js`)
- Avatar scale and presentation: reduced `avatarScale` from `1` to `0.78`, kept existing `avatarPositionOffset`/`groundOffset` to preserve grounded feet, and softened turn smoothing (`turnSmoothing: 10`) to make yaw interpolation smoother. (`src/game/player/ThirdPersonNeckmanPlayerAvatar.js`)
- Jitter/root-motion fixes: added `removeRootMotionTracks` to strip root-position tracks from loaded animation clips where possible and added `neutralizeRootMotion()` to re-center animation roots after mixer updates; ensured the avatar visual root follows the authoritative `PlayerController.position` and yaw, and applied smooth yaw interpolation to avoid snapping. Root motion neutralization is active. (`src/game/player/ThirdPersonNeckmanPlayerAvatar.js`)
- Attack / sword preservation: weapon model and attachment remain unchanged and still attach to `arm_right_hand`; sword visibility continues to follow equipment state and `playAttack` logic is preserved. (`src/game/player/ThirdPersonNeckmanPlayerAvatar.js`)
- Documentation: updated `docs/architecture/THIRD_PERSON_NECKMAN_PLAYER_PROTOTYPE.md` with the tuned camera defaults, avatar scale notes, jitter root-cause and fix, update order, and known limitations.
- Small implementation notes: smoothing and clamp logic updated in camera distance resolver so the view cannot collapse into an extreme close-up except when forced by collision/min-distance rules; no gameplay systems (movement, combat, HUD, equipment, dungeon) were redesigned.

### Testing
- Ran `npm run build` which runs `tsc -b && vite build` and produced a successful build (Vite build completed and assets emitted). (Succeeded)
- Ran `npm run validate:integrity` which completed with zero integrity errors and reported existing warnings (Succeeded, warnings observed). 
- Ran `npm run validate:bgt` which executed and completed (Succeeded).
- Performed static checks: `node --check src/game/player/ThirdPersonCameraController.js` and `node --check src/game/player/ThirdPersonNeckmanPlayerAvatar.js` (Succeeded), and `git diff --check` (no issues).
- Verified `vite.config.ts` still sets Vite base to `/Dread_Stone_Black/` and that no GitHub Pages workflows were altered (Confirmed).
- Note: attempted `npm.cmd` Windows-style commands were unavailable in this environment and were skipped; equivalent `npm` invocations were used instead.

Known limitations
- Camera collision remains a simple walkable-space probe fallback; very tight spaces may still push camera to the configured minimum distance.
- Attack visuals are still the repurposed Neckman punch animation with the sword attached (prototype behavior retained).
- Animation blending and per-clip polishing were not changed beyond root-motion removal; per-clip polish may be required later.

body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Update | Change | OpenSSF |
|---|---|---|---|
| [jdx/mise](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise) | patch | `2026.6.9` → `2026.6.10` | [![OpenSSF Scorecard](https://api.securityscorecards.dev/projects/github.com/jdx/mise/badge)](https://securityscorecards.dev/viewer/?uri=github.com/jdx/mise) |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>jdx/mise (jdx/mise)</summary>

### [`v2026.6.10`](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/releases/tag/v2026.6.10): : Env defaults, Unix 7z, and stale-PATH fixes

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/compare/vfox-v2026.6.9...vfox-v2026.6.10)

A focused release that adds a `default` shorthand for env vars, brings `.7z` archive support to Unix, and cleans up several long-standing PATH and shim edge cases on Linux, macOS, Windows, and WSL.

#### Added

- **env:** New `{ default = "fallback" }` shorthand for `[env]` (and config/task `[vars]`). The default applies only when the variable is unset or empty; existing non-empty values from the process env or earlier config are preserved. Mixing `default` with `value`, `required`, or `age` now fails with a clear message ([#​10441](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/pull/10441) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx)).

  ```toml
  [env]
  EDITOR = { default = "vim" }       # only used if $EDITOR is unset/empty
  PORT   = { default = "3000" }
  ```

- **backend:** `.7z` archives now extract on Unix as well as Windows, and `strip_components` probing works cross-platform. Migrated from the unmaintained `sevenz-rust` to `sevenz-rust2`, and tightened extraction to reject directory traversal and absolute paths ([#​10434](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/pull/10434) by [@​risu729](https://redirect.github.com/risu729)).

#### Fixed

- **env:** When `env_shell_expand` is enabled, `${VAR:-default}` now follows POSIX semantics: empty strings are treated as missing (fallback applies), `${VAR-default}` only substitutes when the variable is unset, and fallback text is recursively expanded (e.g. `${NONEXISTENT:-$OTHER}`). Braced parsing is also stricter — unterminated `${…` stays literal and `}` inside `$(…)` no longer closes the brace ([#​10445](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/pull/10445) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx), fixes [#​10444](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/10444)).
- **env:** `mise x` / `run` / `env` now strip mise-managed install directories from the inherited PATH when composing the child environment. Stale entries carried in from a frozen env snapshot (IDE terminals, CI wrappers, AI-agent harnesses) no longer sit ahead of the freshly injected bin dir, so subshells, `#!/usr/bin/env` shebangs, and package-manager workers all resolve the requested tool version ([#​10422](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/pull/10422) by [@​JamBalaya56562](https://redirect.github.com/JamBalaya56562), addresses [#​10345](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/10345)).
- **vfox:** Plugin install hooks that shell out via Lua `os.execute` now run under the same sanitized `mise_env` as `cmd.exec`. Combined with new resolution of `tools = true` env *values* during install, this fixes setups like gcloud depending on python where a single `mise install` previously left `CLOUDSDK_PYTHON` pointing at a nonexistent path ([#​10432](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/pull/10432) by [@​JamBalaya56562](https://redirect.github.com/JamBalaya56562), fixes [#​10282](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/10282)).
- **shims:** Windows extensionless bash shims now detect WSL (`WSL_DISTRO_NAME` / `WSL_INTEROP` / `WSLInterop`), drop their own dir from PATH, and `exec` the tool directly. This breaks the infinite `mise x` loop that happened when the Windows shims dir was exposed at `/mnt/c/...` inside WSL, and gives a clean `<tool>: not found` when no Linux tool is installed. `file`-mode shims are now also flagged version-stale so a normal reshim regenerates them on upgrade ([#​10421](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/pull/10421) by [@​JamBalaya56562](https://redirect.github.com/JamBalaya56562), addresses [#​10299](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/10299)).
- **file:** `make_symlink` on Unix now creates the link at a unique temp name in the destination dir and atomically `rename(2)`s it into place. This eliminates the noisy `failed to ln -sf … File exists (os error 17)` warnings that surfaced when several mise processes (shell `hook-env`, direnv, editor integrations) raced on the same tracked-config link, e.g. when spawning a new git worktree ([#​10414](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/pull/10414) by [@​JamBalaya56562](https://redirect.github.com/JamBalaya56562), fixes [#​10292](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/issues/10292)).
- **task:** On Windows, script-task lookup now prefers Windows-native variants (e.g. `.ps1`) over their extensionless siblings, and extensionless takeover only applies when the match is unambiguous and stays within the same config family ([#​10443](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/pull/10443) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx)).

#### Changed

- **deps:** Replaced the unmaintained `number_prefix` (RUSTSEC-2025-0119) and stale `humansize` crates with `bytesize`. Size strings in generated `tool-stub` comments and `mise cache prune` output now use native `bytesize` IEC formatting — e.g. `821.69 KiB` becomes `821.7 KiB` and `2.15 MiB` becomes `2.2 MiB` ([#​10438](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise/pull/10438) by [@​risu729](https://redirect.github.com/risu729)).

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/jdx/mise/compare/v2026.6.9...v2026.6.10>

body:
## 根因（不是猜，是 path-dep 契约）

`sandbox` 拆分后，跨目录 path 依赖写死了绝对布局：

| 来源 | path | 镜像内必须存在 |
|------|------|----------------|
| `http-gateway-rs` | `../../../sandbox/crates/*` | `/sandbox/crates/*` |
| `claw-sandbox-client` | `../../../rust/crates/gateway-solve-turn` | `/rust/crates/gateway-solve-turn` |

worker 镜像虽只 `cargo build -p rusty-claude-cli`，但 cargo 会解析整个 workspace → 加载 `http-gateway-rs` → 加载 `claw-sandbox-client` → 再回指 `/rust/crates/...`。

## 两次失败分别缺什么

- `release-v1.6.1`：worker Dockerfile 未 `COPY sandbox/`（PR #54 只补了一半）
- `release-v1.6.2`：补了 sandbox，但 rust 仍在 `/build` 而非 `/rust`（`claw-sandbox-client` 找不到 `/rust/crates/...`）

`Containerfile.gateway-rs` 早已是 `WORKDIR /rust` + 双树 COPY；worker 应对齐。

## 本 PR

1. `Containerfile.gateway-worker` builder 与 gateway-rs 同布局（`/rust` + `/sandbox`）
2. 新增 `deploy/stack/lib/verify-image-rust-layout.sh`：构建前校验两份 Containerfile
3. CI `claw-code-image` + pre-push 跑该校验，避免再靠 buildx 撞出来

## Test plan
- [ ] `bash deploy/stack/lib/verify-image-rust-layout.sh`
- [ ] 合并后打 `release-v1.6.3`，确认 worker job 绿

**勿用** `release-v1.6.1` / `release-v1.6.2` 部署。

💡 What: Wrapped Hero, Features, Testimonials, Pricing, CTA, and Footer components in React.memo().

🎯 Why: In the landing page builder, any update to a single section's data (e.g., Hero title) triggers a full re-render of all other sections because they all consume parts of a centralized state object in the parent component.

📊 Impact: Reduces re-renders of non-edited sections by 100% after initial load. Total re-renders during typical editing sessions are reduced by ~83%, making the real-time editor significantly more responsive on lower-end devices or with more complex sections.

🔬 Measurement: Verified using a custom Playwright script that monitors 'RENDER: [Component]' console logs during sidebar interactions. 
- Before: All 6 sections re-rendered 6 times for 3 keystrokes (due to React 19 double-rendering in dev).
- After: Only the section being edited (e.g., Hero) re-renders, others stay at 0 after initial load.

author: dhoulb
body:
## Summary

Adds search across the docs site in **three places**, all built on one shared ranking helper over the same `tree.json` payload, so behaviour stays consistent across surfaces.

Closes #164

## Shared ranking helper — `searchTree`

`modules/util/tree.ts` (next to `TreeElement`):

```ts
function searchTree(scope: TreeElement, query: string, options?: SearchTreeOptions): TreeElement[]
```

- Tokenises the query with `getWords` so `"quoted phrases"` match literally and stack with bare words; each token scores independently.
- Ranks case-insensitively, summing per token: `name` exact → `startsWith` → `includes` → `title` → `description` → `content`. Score tiers are separated by orders of magnitude so a **name match always beats a content-only match**.
- `filter` is a `Query` over each candidate's props (e.g. `{ kind: "method" }`, `{ source: "…" }`) — no hard-coded `kind` option.
- Empty query returns the (filtered) candidates in tree order — useful for filter-only / "show everything" listings. `limit` defaults to `20`.

## Surface 1 — Sidebar (`TreeSidebar`)

Search-as-you-type input above the menu. A non-empty query swaps the tree menu for a flat ranked list (cap 20); empty falls through to the normal menu. Adds an **"All elements"** link to the index page. The sidebar flattens the tree locally so results carry a canonical `path` for their hrefs.

## Surface 2 — `DocumentationPage` in-page filter

Above the card listing: a search input, a **"This {kind} only"** scope toggle, and a row of **kind chips**.

- **Checked (default):** scope is this page's `children`.
- **Unchecked:** scope is the whole tree (cards can come from anywhere).
- Chips narrow by `kind` via `searchTree`'s `filter` (exclusive — one at a time).
- Idle (empty query, no chip) → the normal grouped listing, unchanged.

## Surface 3 — `TreeIndexPage` (`/all`)

A new page listing every element in one flat, searchable view (search input + kind chips + flat card listing). Empty query lists everything (cap 100); non-empty ranks and caps at 20. Shipped as a synthetic `tree-index` node injected at build time and routed via `TreeRouterMapping`, so it renders statically and routes for free.

## Shared chip component

`DocumentationKindChips` — the colour-coded kind-chip row reused by Surfaces 2 and 3.

## Incidental fix

`Input.module.css` imported a `Shades.module.css` that was removed in an earlier refactor. It was latent until now (the docs tree never pulled in form inputs); pulling `TextInput`/`CheckboxInput` into the docs broke the build, so the stale `@import` is removed.

## Notes / decisions

- **Chips are exclusive** (single active kind), per the issue's "decide while building".
- **Index routing**: chosen the dedicated `/all` route (injected tree node) over root-merge, since both static rendering and routing are already driven off the flattened tree.
- `content` is already present in `tree.json` (2209 nodes), so no separate `search.json` was needed.
- The sidebar search input is not yet `position: sticky` (would require a new CSS module on a composition component); functional otherwise.

## Testing

- `bun run test` — lint, types, and 1133 unit tests pass (added 9 `searchTree` ranking tests).
- `bun run docs:build` — builds 2407 pages; verified `/all` renders, the sidebar search + "All elements" link render, and a class page shows the "This class only" toggle and chips.

author: ricksinclair
body:
## Summary
Bakes the **graph-first-recall** discipline into Engram itself, so every user's agent gets it — not just one person's private config.

`new-project`'s generated repo `CLAUDE.md` previously said only *"Consult it before substantive work."* That reads as a task-*start* step. This rewrites the **Knowledge graph** section to make the graph the **primary source of truth for recall**:

> **Query the graph FIRST** for any question about work done, decisions made, or *why* something is the way it is — before answering from memory or searching elsewhere (`resume` / `context` / `search`). Treat **Notion as the secondary lane**: follow the `Source` references the graph surfaces rather than searching it blind.

Also folds in the end-of-work sync reminder (consistent with the graph-sync trigger change).

## Why
The graph is the cross-session resume layer; an agent that only checks it "when asked" defeats the purpose. This makes consulting it the unprompted default for recall, with Notion reached *through* the graph's provenance rather than searched blind.

## Notes
- Synced from the canonical template via `sync-engram.sh`; leak gate clean; diff is the one section only.
- `npm test` — 22/22 pass (assertions cover name/URL/IDs, unaffected).

author: goospel
body:
## 무엇을

A3(#353)가 깐 드래그를 **"빈 칸 이동만"에서 드래그 모델 완성**으로 풍부화합니다. 사용자 결정 = **점유 칸 스왑 + 캔버스 밖 드롭=거두기**(핀치·팬·part-sway는 후속 제외).

## 왜

A3 첫 PR은 점유 칸 드롭을 "무효 복귀"로 두고 자리 바꾸기·거두기를 후속으로 미뤘는데, 끌어서 자리를 바꾸고 밖으로 빼 거두는 것이 드래그의 자연스러운 완성입니다(현 무효 복귀는 답답).

## 어떻게

- **드롭 결정 로직을 순수 함수 `resolveDrop(source, target, placements)`로 추출** — 상태 변경(`this.placements` 대입)과 결정을 분리해 하니스가 결정만 단독 단언. `applyDrop`은 결과 맵을 적용만(+`justPlaced` pop).
- **4가지 결정**:
  - 빈 칸 이동(기존 동작 보존)
  - **셀 → 점유칸 = 스왑**(출발칸 ↔ target 교환, 둘 다 "한 식물 한 번" 유지)
  - **팔레트 → 점유칸 = 교체**(점유자 거둠 + 같은 식물 중복 떼기 — 기존 탭 교체와 정합)
  - **밖(-1) = 거두기**(셀 소스만 `fromCell` 제거, 팔레트 소스는 무변경) + 제자리(`target===fromCell`) 무변경
- **오발 방지(R2)**: `closestCellIndex`의 셀 크기 비례 마진(`outOfBoundsMargin=1.0`)이 "확실히 밖"일 때만 -1(갭·근접은 안 거둠) + 셀 소스를 밖으로 끌 때 캔버스에 `.drag-removing` 붉은 점선 톤 경고.
- **저장 계약 불변·백엔드 0**(A3 계승): 스왑/거두기/이동 다 `placements` 맵 조작일 뿐 `save` payload는 여전히 `{axis,code,cell}` → 위조 표면·Flyway 무변경, 격자 스냅 유지로 B 전환 트리거(자유 픽셀 `x,y`) 회피 지속.

## TDD (RED → GREEN, 실제 실행)

- **RED**: `resolveDrop` 미구현 → `.preview/a3-pure.test.mjs`가 garden.html `@a3-pure-core` 마커 블록을 추출 실행하다 `Export 'resolveDrop' is not defined`로 실패 확인.
- **GREEN**: 마커 블록에 `resolveDrop`+`removeSamePlant` 추가 → **28 passed, 0 failed**(빈칸이동·셀스왑·팔레트교체·밖거두기·제자리·입력 불변 + 기존 `closestCellIndex`/`clampScale` 회귀 가드).
- **회귀 가드**: `./gradlew test` 전체 **BUILD SUCCESSFUL**(`.java` 무변경).
- ⚠️ 멀티터치·`setPointerCapture` 실기기 차이는 헤드리스 한계 → 실 브라우저 수동 시각 게이트로 남김(계획 §4.3).

> 참고: A3 세션이 만든 `a3-pure.test.mjs`가 `.gitignore`(`.preview/`)라 커밋되지 않아 로컬에 없었습니다. `@a3-pure-core` 마커 블록이 단일 출처이므로 하니스를 재생성해 RED→GREEN 절차는 동일하게 지켰습니다.

## 변경 파일

- `src/main/resources/templates/garden.html` — 순수 함수 2개(`resolveDrop`/`removeSamePlant`) + `applyDrop` 리팩터 + 거두기 힌트 `:class` 바인딩
- `src/main/resources/static/css/app.css` — `.drag-removing` 거두기 경고 톤
- `claude-docs/changelog.md` · `plan.md` — A3 후속 출하 반영

## 후속

핀치 줌·팬·part-sway(모션)는 후속 PR로 분리.

author: thedavidmeister
body:
## Summary

A scoped adversarial-mutation-test coverage pass over `src/lib/LibDataContract.sol` (the SSTORE2-style data-contract write / read / readSlice paths). **Test-only — `src/` is byte-for-byte unchanged** (verified `git diff src/` empty). The pass mutated each load-bearing line, ran the suite, and added discriminating tests only for behaviors that survived or were covered solely by fuzz luck.

No anchoring issue exists (the only open issue, #1, is an EIP-3540 research item and is out of scope for coverage hardening), so this is standalone.

## Group hardened: `LibDataContract` write/read/readSlice boundaries

The existing suite is a strong set of fuzz round-trips, so most mutants were already killed. The gaps were **edge inputs the `bytes`/`uint16` fuzzer effectively never generates** — empty data, the max valid length, and exact-end slices — which left several boundary mutants alive or killed only when the fuzzer happened to land on the edge.

## Mutation matrix

| # | Mutation | Pre-existing coverage | Action |
|---|----------|----------------------|--------|
| 1 | `DataTooLarge` `>=` → `>` | killed by `testContractCreationCodeDataTooLargeRevert` | already covered |
| 2 | prefix length `+1` → `+0` | killed by fuzz only | **+** `testRoundLargestData`, `testReadSkipsPrefixExactly` pin deterministically |
| 3 | `shl(232,…)` → `shl(233,…)` | killed by fuzz | already covered |
| 4 | readSlice `size < end` → `<=` | killed by `testSameReads` (fuzz) | **+** `testReadSliceExactEndBoundary` (deterministic) |
| 5 | read `extcodecopy` offset `1` → `0` | killed by fuzz | **+** `testReadSkipsPrefixExactly`, `testRoundLargestData` (deterministic) |
| 6 | readSlice offset `+1` → `+0` | killed by fuzz | already covered |
| 7 | readSlice `end = offset+length` → `+0` | killed by `testRoundSliceError` (fuzz) | already covered |
| 8 | readSlice copy `offset` → `start` | killed by fuzz | already covered |
| 9 | `PREFIX_BYTES_LENGTH` `13` → `12` | killed by fuzz | already covered |
| 10 | read `size == 0` → `size == 1` | **SURVIVED** except on fuzz-generated empty bytes | **+** `testReadEmptyData`, `testReadZeroCodeReverts` pin both sides of the size guard |
| 11 | `DataTooLarge` guard `max` → `max-1` (tighten accepted side) | **SURVIVED** (existing revert test only checks the rejected side) | **+** `testContractCreationCodeLargestAccepted`, `testRoundLargestData` pin the accepted boundary |

Every new test was confirmed to **pass clean and fail under its target mutation**, then the source was restored.

## New tests

- `testReadEmptyData` / `testReadZeroCodeReverts` — writing empty data yields a 1-byte container (just the `0x00` prefix) that `read`s back empty **without reverting**, while a no-code address reverts `ReadError`. Pins the `read` size guard to exactly zero.
- `testRoundLargestData` — round-trips at the largest valid length (`type(uint16).max - 1`), exercising the full 2-byte length field (`shl(232, data.length + 1)`) and the prefix copy offset at maximum width, plus a slice of the final byte.
- `testContractCreationCodeLargestAccepted` / `testContractCreationCodeSmallestRejected` — pin both sides of the GTE `DataTooLarge` boundary (the existing revert test only covered the rejected side).
- `testReadSliceExactEndBoundary` — a slice ending exactly at the data end is valid; one byte past reverts `ReadError`.
- `testReadSkipsPrefixExactly` — a non-zero leading data byte appears at index 0 of `read`/`readSlice`, pinning the skip-one-byte offset.

## Verification

- `forge build` clean
- `forge fmt --check` clean
- `forge test`: 13 passed, 0 failed (6 original + 7 new)
- `git diff src/` empty (source untouched)

## Remaining gaps / not done

- [ ] Issue #1 (EIP-3540 / EOF) is **not** addressed — research item, explicitly out of scope.
- [ ] Multiple contracts deployed from the *same* memory container / overlapping-allocation reuse is exercised by the fuzz garbage-injection test but has no dedicated deterministic case.
- [ ] `read` on a contract whose first byte is non-zero (i.e. NOT produced by this lib) is documented as caller responsibility (`MUST have a leading byte that can be safely ignored`) and intentionally not guarded; left as-is.
- [ ] No gas-regression / snapshot assertions added beyond the existing `testSameReads` relative-cost check.

author: twodragon0
body:
## Problem

Dependabot #220 (bump docker group: alpine 3.20→3.24, nginx 1.27→1.31-alpine) is **digest-pin compliant** but fails to merge — it turns 4 required checks red (Lint gate, Run Security Scan, Security Scan Gate, dashboard-regression-check).

Root cause is **not** Dependabot — it's a version-brittle `Dockerfile`. The prowler cleanup step hardcodes `/install/lib/python3.12/site-packages`. alpine 3.24's base image ships **Python 3.14**, so that path no longer exists and the unguarded `sed -i` fails:

```
sed: /install/lib/python3.12/site-packages/prowler/__main__.py: No such file or directory
```
→ `process "...prowler..." did not complete successfully: exit code: 1` → build fails.

## Fix

- Resolve site-packages dynamically (no hardcoded minor version):
  ```dockerfile
  SITE="$(find /install/lib -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'python3.*' | sort | head -n1)/site-packages"
  ```
- Reference `"${SITE}"` for every `rm -rf` strip path and for `MAIN`.
- Guard the provider-import patch with `[ -f "$MAIN" ]` (warn-and-skip instead of hard-fail if prowler's entrypoint ever moves).

Behavior-preserving on the current base: same strip list, same `sed` pattern.

## Verification (local `docker buildx`, `--target builder`)

| Base | Python | Build | Notes |
|------|--------|-------|-------|
| alpine 3.20 | 3.12 | ✅ PASS | no regression (current `main`) |
| alpine 3.24 | 3.14 | ✅ PASS | was failing on #220 |

Post-build checks on the 3.24 image:
- `prowler --help` exits 0; `import prowler.providers.aws` OK
- Unused providers (azure/gcp/llm/m365/…) stripped; only `aws`, `common` remain — same as before

## Follow-up

Once merged, Dependabot will rebase #220 against this `main`; its Docker build then passes and it can merge (or be closed in favor of a combined bump).

#### What's new

##### Features

Config validation now handles the full lifecycle of bundled skill and agent names — including names that have been removed in past releases. Previously, listing a no-longer-bundled name in `disabled_skills` or `disabled_agents` would fail validation and prevent plugin load, effectively bricking setups that had disabled something Systematic later cleaned up.

v2.32.0 introduces a removed-names mechanism with three coordinated layers:

- **Schema acceptance**: The JSON Schema generator now includes the removed-names list in the enum for `disabled_skills` and `disabled_agents`, so editors and runtime stay in sync. While the list ships empty today, the schema will reflect any future additions without requiring editor configuration updates.
- **Validation acceptance**: Removed names are accepted during config validation alongside current bundled names, maintaining the strict rejection of genuinely-unknown names.
- **Load-time cleanup**: After validation, removed names are silently dropped from the effective disabled lists and a per-load `[systematic]` warning identifies each stale entry. Raw config is preserved for merge precedence; the dedup is stateless per load.

A content-integrity gate enforces that removed names never overlap current bundled names, preventing accidental misclassification as a name moves from active to removed.

author: cbrightly
body:
## Bug
When an SDES camera's `webrtcResp` (answer) arrives **after** the bridge has started, the bridge sends a *late* USE-CANDIDATE. That path nominated **only the one socket** that received the first BindingReq (usually audio) and set `sent=True` — so the **video ICE pair was never nominated**. Result: the session establishes, audio/control flow, but the camera **never sends video RTP** (0 video bytes).

## Fix
Mirror the early (answer-in-time) path: nominate **both** the audio and video sockets for each candidate.

## Validation
Live on a real SDES camera (A001064, late-answer scenario):
- **Before:** late answer → no video RTP at all → 0 bytes.
- **After:** `late USE-CANDIDATE sent (audio+video)` → `first video RTP pt=96` → ffmpeg records steadily to **5.5 MB** (H.264) end-to-end.
- ruff clean; `pytest tests/ -q` → 112 passed.

> Note: separately discovered that SDES recording requires the official app to be **closed** (the camera serves a single media viewer); and that **H.265 (pt=97)** sessions still don't record because the ffmpeg SDP lists `96 97` and binds H.264 — that codec fix is tracked next, plus go2rtc as the durable path.

body:
## What

Calibrates `.github/dependabot.yml` so scheduled **version updates** run only for code that stays in L0; apps departing to their own repos are **security-only**.

| Ecosystem | Directory | Mode |
|---|---|---|
| pip (toolkit) | `/` | version updates |
| docker | `edge/errors` | version updates |
| github-actions | `/` | version updates |
| npm | `apps/web/*` | security-only (`limit: 0`) |
| gomod | `apps/api/src` | security-only (`limit: 0`) |
| docker | `apps/web`, `apps/api` | security-only (`limit: 0`) |

## Why

The initial full-coverage config (#618) opened a 14-PR burst on merge, much of it on apps slated to graduate to their own repos (WEB-002b kubelab.live, PUB-001 kubelab-cli, mlorente.dev). Managing versions on departing code is churn on the single self-hosted runner for little value.

`open-pull-requests-limit: 0` disables version-update PRs while **security updates keep flowing** and the **Astro-major ignore stays active**. The docker block is split so `edge/errors` (a durable edge service) keeps version updates while app images do not.

Aligns the live config with `docs/runbooks/dependency-updates.md` (#633).

author: jrcheshire
body:
## Summary

  Adds a Lagrangian-bias tracer and a lightcone galaxy-catalog generator, making the
  forward-only mocks faithful for injected local f_NL and for radially-evolving samples.

  ## Lagrangian-bias tracer (`mbody/bias.py`, `mbody/cosmology.py`)
  - `lagrangian_bias_field` (+ `tidal_sq` shear, `laplacian_field`) — a 2nd-order
    Lagrangian bias expansion (b1, b2, b_s2, ∇²δ) with an **explicit** b_phi term, applied
    to the initial field and advected as per-particle CIC weights.
  - Setting b_phi directly (separate-universe definition) removes the through-PM dilution of
    the emergent Eulerian-b2 tracer: `dlnP_g/df_NL` recovers the linear Dalal value (~1.0 at
    low k) instead of ~0.25.
  - Coefficients may be per-cell fields, so the bias can evolve along the line of sight.
  - `cosmology.comoving_distance(z)`.

  ## Lightcone galaxy catalogs (`mbody/catalog.py`)
  - `sample_from_field` (+ `_counts_from_delta` refactor): Poisson-sample a precomputed
    tracer overdensity (the seam the weighted-paint field uses).
  - `lightcone_catalog`: an onion multi-snapshot lightcone with continuous radial
    b1(r)/b_phi(r) and per-shell growth — reproduces D(z(r)) where a single-redshift
    snapshot is off by up to ~74% in radial clustering amplitude.
  - Plus lean float32 / streaming placement (`place_galaxies_chunked`, `sample_to_parquet`)
    and observer-centered radial selection (`radial_nbar_field`).

  ## Validation
  - `scripts/probe_lagrangian_bias.py` — gate 1 (linear b_phi = Dalal kernel), gate 2
    (through-PM, no dilution), gate 3 (resolution stability).
  - `scripts/probe_lagrangian_lightcone.py`, `scripts/probe_lightcone_catalog.py` — growth
    profile, geometry, and per-shell b(r)/b_phi(r) recovery.
  - New tests in `tests/test_lagrangian_bias.py` and `tests/test_catalog.py`; full suite
    **203 passing**, format/lint clean.

body:
…bootstrap)

Extend doc-lint beyond doc-vs-doc linting to also serve stale-docs and code-first repos, via a manifest `mode` (default doc-first, unchanged):

- doc-first  — concerns over authored docs (original behavior, identical)
- reconcile  — authored docs + a static code map → concerns plus a documentation↔code drift scanner that flags where docs and code disagree
- code-first — an ONBOARDING mode, not a lint mode: `doc-lint bootstrap` deterministically (no LLM) scaffolds evidence-named as-built docs plus a documentation gap inventory from a static scan. lint/reconcile/assemble redirect to bootstrap. (Linting docs synthesized from code is circular — "is X documented?" collapses into "is X implemented?" — so it is not done; multi-model design consensus.)

Core additions:
- code-scan.ts: language-agnostic static code map (tree, deps, routes, models, external calls, env vars) with a first-class coverage model; `scan` command
- drift scanner: DriftFinding type, template, prompt/parser, reconcile command, --mode/--code/--no-drift; the code map is injected only into code-aware concerns so implementation facts can't falsely satisfy a doc-gap concern
- bootstrap.ts + command: deterministic scaffolds (architecture-as-built, functional-surface, operations-surface, doc-todos gap inventory) with a path-traversal guard; works with or without a manifest
- code signals (detectSignalsFromCode) + code-first init fallback
- manifest mode/code fields with mode-aware validation (doc-first byte-identical)
- 7 new concerns incl. code-vs-doc parity (endpoint-parity, dependency-drift, schema-doc-parity) and doc-vs-doc (data-model-ownership, config-surface- documentation, public-contract-versioning, background-job-observability)

author: an9xyz
body:
## What

Refines the management-console authorization model along the read/write boundary and gives the frontend a single source of truth for what the current operator may do.

### 1. `common` — reading system settings requires superAdmin (`f0431ca`)
System-setting reads expose secrets (masked) and effective config; tightened from admin to **superAdmin**, matching the existing write/update gate. No change to the masked-secret behaviour.

### 2. `opanalytics` — dashboard reads allow admin, ETL trigger stays superAdmin (`fd1e09f`)
The 6 read-only dashboard endpoints (overview / trend / spaces / space-channels / channel-members / global direct-chats) now accept **admin** — they are read-only analytics. The single state-changing endpoint, `POST /v1/manager/dashboard/etl/run`, **remains superAdmin**. This splits "look at the dashboard" (admin) from "kick off an ETL run" (superAdmin).

### 3. `user` — new `GET /v1/manager/me` identity + capability map (`7858a25`)
Returns `{uid, name, role, capabilities}` so the console can render/hide controls from one call instead of probing endpoints. The capability map is a pure function of role; auth/role resolution is unchanged, and it surfaces no per-reason detail (anti-enumeration preserved).

## Why
The previous gating treated read and write uniformly per module. These changes make the boundary consistent: secret-bearing reads and state-changing actions require superAdmin, while pure analytics reads are available to admin. `/me` removes the frontend's need to infer capabilities by trial.

## Testing
Full integration suites for all three touched modules pass against **MySQL 8 + Redis** (WuKongIM not required — IM-token calls are logged-only and non-fatal):

| Module | Result |
|---|---|
| `modules/user` | ok, 0 failures |
| `modules/common` | ok, 0 failures |
| `modules/opanalytics` | ok, 0 failures |

Includes new regression tests: `TestManagerSystemSetting*` (read requires superAdmin), `TestOpanalyticsDashboardReadAdminTriggerSuperAdmin` (read=admin, trigger=superAdmin), and `TestManagerCapabilities` (pure capability-map coverage).

> Note for local reproduction: use MySQL 8 (a `robot_legacy01` migration uses MySQL-8-only functional-index syntax) and create the test DB with `utf8mb4_general_ci` (the MySQL-8 default `utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci` triggers collation-mix errors in opanalytics joins). CI already uses these.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)
Frontend references `PUT /v1/manager/download/versions/{id}` which has no backend handler — tracked separately, pending a decision on whether to add the endpoint or drop the frontend call.

body:
## Summary

Adds a typed local action layer for PromptVault Lite.

This enables deterministic local action dispatch without DOM automation, MCP server exposure, cloud APIs, or LLM calls.

## Capabilities

- 10 typed local actions via `dispatch(..., input)`
- Manual schema validation without new dependencies
- Evidence log for action calls
- Developer-mode gate
- Write-approval gate for write actions
- Path-boundary enforcement for QA fixtures
- 6 new artifact hygiene categories
- 25 red tests for security and regression scenarios

## Security

- Action layer disabled by default
- Write actions require approval token
- `qa.load_fixture` blocks traversal, absolute paths and null bytes
- Evidence log avoids uncontrolled raw prompt leakage
- No network / no API / no LLM

## Verification

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm test` | 308 passed, 12 pre-existing QA failures (non-blocking, see note) |
| `pnpm lint` | PASS (0 errors, 0 warnings) |
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | PASS (0 errors) |
| `pnpm build` | PASS |
| `cargo test` | PASS (102 lib + 17 integration, 0 failures) |
| `cargo build` | PASS |

### Note on 12 pre-existing QA failures

The 12 failures are in `.opencode/corpus-qa/evaluation-corpus.test.ts` — an internal QA evaluation corpus. These are pre-existing scoring-calibration issues in the prompt evaluation engine (PR #88), NOT caused by #90. They do not block this PR.

## Known Limits

- Write approval currently uses `_approvalToken: approved` until UI dialog exists
- Evidence log is in-memory only
- `qa.load_fixture` works only with running dev server
- Action layer and appStore still contain parallel logic paths

## Follow-up candidates

- UI approval dialog for write actions
- Persist evidence log to disk
- Settings modal integration for developer mode
- Sandbox preview demo with screenshots

Closes #90
