author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary

First research iteration on **picks-theorem-oq-04** ("Shoelace formula and its
integrality bridge to Pick's theorem"). Build-free ORIENT under a dual-backend
blackout (Docker hangs; Aristotle MCP returns "Resource not found").

**Gap pinned.** The *triangle* shoelace and its integrality are already proven in
the gallery — `PicksTheoremOQ01.lean:70` (`shoelaceTriangle`), `PicksTheoremOQ01OQ01OQ01.lean:137`
(`twiceArea = |det| ∈ ℕ`), plus the partition-sum identity and `picks_additivity`.
The genuine OQ-04 content is the **general simple n-gon**:

1. `2·Area = |S|`, `S := Σ_i (x_i y_{i+1} − x_{i+1} y_i)`.
2. **Integrality bridge**: `S ∈ ℤ` by construction ⇒ `Area ∈ ½ℤ`, the exact
   denominator of Pick's `i + b/2 − 1` (`2·Area = 2i + b − 2 ∈ ℤ`).
3. **Lift engine**: `S = Σ cross2(v₀, v_i, v_{i+1})` (fan triangulation) — the
   algebraic, telescoping lift of the proven per-triangle determinant.

**Key observation for ACT**: integrality is *not* the hard part (definitional once
`shoelaceSum : List (ℤ×ℤ) → ℤ`); the Lean crux is the telescoping fan identity. No
primitive-decomposition geometry is needed — the route is purely algebraic (~120–200 LOC).

## Durable verification

`verify_shoelace_integrality.py` (exact integer arithmetic, no floats) checks:

| Claim | Result |
|-------|--------|
| (I) `S ∈ ℤ`, `2·Area = |S|` | ✅ |
| (II) fan bridge `S = Σ cross2` | ✅ |
| (III) n=3 reduces to `shoelaceTriangle` | ✅ |
| (IV) Pick `|S| = 2i + b − 2` (`i,b` counted independently) | ✅ |

8 fixtures (triangles, rectangle, L-shape, pentagon, collinear-edge quad, non-convex
zigzag hexagon) **+ 400 random convex lattice polygons** — all pass.

## Files
- `research/problems/picks-theorem-oq-04/verify_shoelace_integrality.py`
- `research/problems/picks-theorem-oq-04/knowledge.md`
- `research/problems/picks-theorem-oq-04/state.md`

No Lean changes (build-gated). Path-disjoint from the OQ01/OQ03 Pick family.

## Test plan

author: niktonikto717
body:
Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/102707
Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/108104

One unified set of `SYSTEM` commands to control the background activity of the streaming engines (`Kafka`, `RabbitMQ`, `NATS`, `S3Queue`/`AzureQueue`) and refreshable materialized views (RMV). Previously RMV had its own `SYSTEM ... VIEW` commands and the streaming engines had no per-table SQL control.

```sql
SYSTEM STOP    [db.]table | ALL BACKGROUND   -- abort the in-flight read AND block further cycles
SYSTEM START   [db.]table | ALL BACKGROUND   -- resume (undo STOP / PAUSE)
SYSTEM PAUSE   [db.]table | ALL BACKGROUND   -- block further cycles, let the running one finish
SYSTEM CANCEL  [db.]table | ALL BACKGROUND   -- abort the in-flight read only, keep scheduling
SYSTEM REFRESH [db.]table | ALL BACKGROUND   -- run exactly one out-of-order cycle
```

On an RMV the verbs are **aliases** of the existing `SYSTEM ... VIEW` commands. `ALL BACKGROUND` applies the verb to every such table at once.

## How the verbs behave

A **cycle** = read a block → insert into the dependent MVs → reach the engine's **commit point**. Each verb has 2 effects:

| verb | block future cycles? | abort in-flight cycle? | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `STOP` | yes | yes | `= PAUSE + CANCEL` |
| `PAUSE` | yes | no | running cycle still commits |
| `CANCEL` | no | yes | keeps scheduling |
| `START` | unblock | — | undo `STOP` / `PAUSE` |
| `REFRESH` | — | — | one extra out-of-order cycle |

The abort is best-effort: `STOP`/`CANCEL` are honored only while the source is still reading the block. Once the insert has started, the block runs to its commit point (mid-insert it acts like `PAUSE`), aborting it then would duplicate the already-inserted rows. `S3Queue`/`AzureQueue` are the exception: their source streams files straight into the insert (one fused pipeline, no buffered block to drop), so the abort cancels the pipeline. Files in progress are reprocessed, files already done stay done. Aborted data is redelivered later. Core NATS has no replay and drops it.

| Engine | Commit point | What `STOP`/`CANCEL` abort |
|---|---|---|
| Kafka v1/v2 | offset commit | the read (a running insert still commits) |
| RabbitMQ | AMQP ack | the read (a running insert still acks) |
| NATS (JetStream) | JetStream ack | the read (a running insert still acks) |
| NATS (core) | *none (at-most-once)* | the in-flight read, but it is lost (no replay) |
| S3Queue / AzureQueue | file marked `Processed` | the read and the insert (files reprocessed)\* |
| RMV | refresh committed | the in-progress refresh |

\* With deduplication off (non-default), the in-flight batch finishes and commits instead.

`REFRESH` runs immediately on a streaming table (even while stopped, then re-blocks). On a stopped RMV it defers until `START`, like `SYSTEM REFRESH VIEW`.

## Design notes

- **AST**: scope lives in the `Type` enum (5 basic verbs + 5 `*_ALL_BACKGROUND`). Basic verbs match in a fallback *after* the specific forms, so `STOP` can't shadow `STOP MERGES`/`STOP VIEW`. The new values push `Type` past the default `magic_enum` range, so `enum_range` is widened and the parser rejects the `UNKNOWN`/`END` sentinels. Otherwise `SYSTEM UNKNOWN`/`SYSTEM END` would parse into an AST whose formatting throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` instead of a syntax error.
- **Dispatch** (`InterpreterSystemQuery`): one place resolves the table and branches streaming vs. RMV-aliasing on the new `isStreamingStorage()` predicate. `isMessageQueue()` couldn't be reused, because it excludes `S3Queue`/`AzureQueue`. `ALL BACKGROUND` fans out over both lock sets, skipping tables the caller can't access.
- **Abort boundary**: only the read is abortable, not the insert. Aborting a half-inserted block would duplicate its rows, so a `STOP`/`CANCEL` mid-insert lets that block finish, keeping exactly-once.
- **Streaming mechanism**: one `StreamingBackgroundControl` per streaming table, shared by every engine, holds three signals:

  - `ActionBlocker`: blocks future cycles. `STOP`/`PAUSE` set it, `START` clears it.
  - `cancel_epoch`: a monotonic counter bumped by `STOP`/`CANCEL`. Each consumer snapshots it on start and aborts once it advances. So a stale `STOP` can't poison a later read and concurrent cycles can't cancel each other. It covers an in-flight direct `SELECT` too, so `STOP` halts a manual read, otherwise the `SELECT` would keep consuming after a `STOP`.
  - `refresh_epoch`: a monotonic counter bumped by `REFRESH`. Each worker runs one cycle when it advances, even while blocked.

  The signals and verb logic are shared. Each engine's source then drops the uncommitted work its own way, so it is redelivered or reprocessed: Kafka v1 rewinds to the last committed offset (in place, no group rebalance, so one `REFRESH` re-reads the backlog), Kafka v2 drops uncommitted Keeper offset guard, RabbitMQ requeues (`reject` with `AMQP::requeue`), NATS JetStream skips the ack, S3Queue/AzureQueue cancel the pipeline and reset in-flight files when deduplication is on (default), otherwise in-flight batch finishes to avoid duplicates.
- **NATS JetStream acks after the insert** (`ManualAck=true`): it used to ack on delivery, *before* the insert, so a `STOP`/`CANCEL` or failed insert had already acked the message and lost it. Acking after a successful insert makes NATS at-least-once: an aborted message stays unacked and is redelivered, like Kafka/RabbitMQ. Side effect: a direct `SELECT` no longer permanently consumes (opt in via `nats_commit_on_select`).
- **`nats_commit_on_select`** (default `false`): a direct `SELECT` on JetStream leaves read messages unacked (redelivered, not consumed). `true` consumes the rows it returns. No-op for core NATS.
- **RBAC**: a new `SYSTEM BACKGROUND` now parents existing `SYSTEM VIEWS` and a new `SYSTEM STREAMING ENGINES`. Privilege is resolved at runtime per engine (RMV → `SYSTEM VIEWS`, streaming → `SYSTEM STREAMING ENGINES`), and per table for `ALL BACKGROUND`, so it skips tables the caller lacks and never fails on access.

## Known limitations / out of scope

- **`ON CLUSTER`** is not supported (matching the `SYSTEM ... VIEW` aliases). Its `getRequiredAccessForDDLOnCluster` mapping is defensive only and, if ever enabled, must first be made engine-aware (`SYSTEM STREAMING ENGINES` for streaming tables).
- **Core NATS** `STOP`/`CANCEL` are lossy (no replay). JetStream is at-least-once.
- `FileLog`, `WindowView`, and an engine-agnostic `WAIT` are out of scope. `SYSTEM WAIT VIEW` stays RMV-only.

## Tests

- `04319_system_stop_all_background`: every verb (per-table + `ALL BACKGROUND`) + RBAC.
- `04320_parser_system_background_controls`: parser round-trip plus negatives: `ON CLUSTER` rejected, non-controllable tables error with `BAD_ARGUMENTS`, `SYSTEM UNKNOWN`/`SYSTEM END` rejected as syntax errors (not a formatter `LOGICAL_ERROR`).
- `test_storage_{kafka,rabbitmq,nats,s3_queue}/test_system_stop.py`: every verb per engine (incl. Kafka v2, `AzureQueue`, NATS JetStream). The in-flight boundary from both sides (`STOP` aborts a block held at the source, while a `STOP`/`CANCEL` during the insert commits/acks exactly once, or resets & reprocesses for `S3Queue`). `REFRESH`-runs-once. Live read-guard, no refresh-leak, no backlog. RBAC proves `SYSTEM STREAMING ENGINES` (not `SYSTEM VIEWS`) is required. A NATS-only test checks that `nats_commit_on_select` makes a direct `SELECT` consume the messages it reads only when enabled. `test_storage_nats/` returns from master only to host this file plus a minimal broker/TLS harness.

### Changelog category (leave one):
- New Feature

### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):

Added engine-agnostic `SYSTEM STOP`, `SYSTEM START`, `SYSTEM PAUSE`, `SYSTEM CANCEL`, and `SY

💡 What: Replaced direct DOM container appends within loops across render methods (`renderNeighborhoods`, `renderList`, `renderExploreIndex`, `renderCollectionDetail`) with `DocumentFragment` to batch appends into a single DOM insertion. 🎯 Why: Repeatedly appending items directly to active DOM nodes in loops triggers expensive O(N) reflows and layout thrashing, which is a critical performance bottleneck in vanilla JS list rendering. 📊 Impact: Substantially reduces redraw layout thrashing during list renders and data processing UI operations, keeping memory and UI updates tightly scoped. 🔬 Measurement: Observe overall smoother interactions or lower execution times on layout cycles in profiling when navigating collections and lists.

author: p4suta
body:
## What & why

Enables real package distribution on **crates.io**, **npm**, and **PyPI** (GitHub Releases for CLI/C-ABI binaries already ships). Cuts a patch release **v0.4.1** so every channel ships the same version.

## Changes

- **`build(release)`** — drop `publish = false` from the internal build-block crates (`aozora-spec/syntax/veb/scan/encoding/pipeline/render/proptest/cst/query/pandoc`) so the umbrella `aozora` + `aozora-cli` can publish (crates.io rejects deps on unpublished crates). Bump workspace `0.4.0 → 0.4.1`.
- **`ci(release)`** — rewrite `publish-crates.yml` to publish the whole workspace as an explicit **topological ladder**.
- **`docs(release)`** — rewrite the handbook's crates.io section (live, not deferred) + add npm/PyPI; reframe CLAUDE.md's single-front-door guarantee (internal crates are now on crates.io but carry no API-stability contract — depend on `aozora`).

## Key decisions (verified against cargo 1.95.0, not assumed)

- **Explicit ladder, not `cargo publish --workspace`** — on the pinned toolchain `--workspace` does not order interdependent members topologically on a first publish (packages `aozora-render` before `aozora-pipeline` and aborts). The ladder publishes leaves-first; cargo waits for index propagation between crates.
- **Internal dev-dependencies are path-only (no version)** — cargo checks *versioned* dev-deps against the registry at publish time. Left as-is, `aozora-proptest` (a dev-dep of nearly everything) and the `aozora-pipeline ↔ aozora-render` / `aozora ↔ aozora-cst/query` / `aozora ↔ aozora-corpus` dev-cycles would block the first publish. Path-only deps are stripped from the published manifest, removing the constraint.
- `aozora-proptest` gains `readme`/`keywords`/`categories` (clippy's `cargo` group requires them once a crate is publishable).

## Verified locally (Docker)

- `just build`, `just lint` (fmt / clippy / typos / strict-code / doc) ✅
- `cargo publish --dry-run` of all 4 leaf crates ✅
- Ladder order is topological + every internal dev-dep is path-only (validated via `cargo metadata`) ✅

Name availability confirmed free on all three registries (`aozora`/`aozora-*`, `aozora-wasm`, `aozora_py`).

## After merge

Tag `v0.4.1` (GitHub Release binaries), then run the manual publish workflows once with `dry_run=true`, then `dry_run=false`: `publish-npm.yml` → `publish-pypi.yml` → `publish-crates.yml`. Requires the `NPM_TOKEN` / `CARGO_TOKEN` secrets and the PyPI trusted publisher.

body:
## Summary

Comprehensive, defence-in-depth security hardening across the app and Azure infrastructure. Full rationale in `docs/architecture/security.md`.

### App layer (`proxy.ts` + `lib/security/*`, `lib/auth/*`)
- **CSP** with a per-request nonce (`script-src` nonce + `strict-dynamic`) wired through `app/layout.tsx`.
- **Security headers**: HSTS, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy`, `Permissions-Policy`; `x-powered-by` disabled.
- **Rate limiting**: auth (10/5min) + API (100/min), `429` + `Retry-After`.
- **Same-origin CSRF guard** for cookie-authenticated `/api/v1` routes.
- **Timing-safe auth**: always runs a bcrypt compare against a dummy hash for unknown users (email-enumeration defence).
- **Password 72-byte cap** to avoid bcrypt truncation collisions.

### Infrastructure (Bicep + CI)
- **Front Door WAF** (`infra/modules/wafPolicy.bicep`): OWASP DRS 2.1 + Bot Manager (Premium) + custom rate-limit rules. SKU-gated managed rules; default Premium.
- **Origin lockdown**: App Service denies inbound by default, allows only the `AzureFrontDoor.Backend` service tag; CI pins ingress to our Front Door via `X-Azure-FDID` so the WAF can't be bypassed.
- **Postgres** `require_secure_transport = ON`; sensitive CI deployment outputs masked.

### Docs & skills
- New `docs/architecture/security.md` (threat model, controls, cost tradeoff, residual risks).
- New `atomic-habit-security` skill; cross-referenced from architecture/walkthrough/forward-deploy skills, README, AGENTS.

Use of `set_ciphers()` should only occur when specialized requirements exist. Otherwise, the security of the TLS channel is lowered. At line 125, the legacy-server compatibility path calls `context.set_ciphers('DEFAULT')`. OpenSSL's `DEFAULT` cipher string is version-dependent and expands to include cryptographically weak primitives: SHA1-based MACs (e.g., AES128-SHA), RC4, 3DES/DES, EXPORT-grade ciphers, and anonymous/NULL key-exchange suites. author: nicolasalt
body:
## Summary

The Playwright/browser MCP failed to launch inside session containers after the non-root worker migration (SHI-145 / docs/150): every `browser_*` tool returned `EACCES: permission denied, mkdir '/opt/playwright-browsers/mcp-chrome-for-testing-<hash>'`, blocking browser tools and `present`-tab screenshot verification. This passes `--isolated` to the Playwright MCP so its browser profile lands in a writable temp dir instead of the read-only shared browser store.

## Rationale

**Root cause is the browser *profile* dir, not a browser download.** The reported diagnosis (build-vs-runtime browser revision drift) turned out to be wrong. The pre-installed `chromium-<rev>` binary *is* the Chrome-for-Testing build (`browsers.json` names it `chromium`, title "Chrome for Testing"), is correctly installed read-only per docs/150 §8, and is never re-downloaded at runtime. The failing `mkdir` is `@playwright/mcp`'s per-cwd **persistent browser profile** (user-data-dir), named `mcp-<channel>-<sha256(cwd)[0:7]>` — the `mcp-` prefix and cwd-hash suffix are the tell. playwright-core anchors that profile to its `registryDirectory`, which resolves to `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/playwright-browsers` — the §8 read-only, root-owned, shared store. As the unprivileged `shipit` user (uid 1000) the profile `mkdir` EACCESes. Before SHI-145 the worker ran as root, so the `mkdir` into the root-owned store silently succeeded — which is why this only surfaced after the non-root move.

**Why `--isolated` over the alternatives.** Isolated mode launches the browser with an ephemeral profile under `os.tmpdir()` (`/tmp`, always writable per the docs/150 writable-paths table) and never writes to `registryDirectory`, so §8's read-only shared browser store is preserved exactly as designed. We don't need a persistent profile: the MCP server is per-session and the browser only drives the live preview, so there is no cross-session cookie/login state worth keeping. Pinning the browser revision would do nothing — the binary was never the problem. `chown`-ing the store to `shipit` or repointing `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` into `/home/shipit` were rejected because both re-introduce a writable shared browser store, the very thing §8 removed. No Dockerfile change is needed — the read-only install stays as designed.

## Changes

- **`src/server/session/agents/playwright-mcp.ts`** — add `--isolated` to the shared Playwright MCP launch command (consumed by both the Claude and Codex adapters), with a comment explaining the non-root profile-dir EACCES and why isolated mode is the fix.
- **`src/server/session/agents/playwright-mcp.test.ts`** (new) — regression guard asserting `--isolated` (and the other load-bearing flags) stay in the launch command, so a future edit that drops it fails the build instead of re-breaking the browser on the non-root worker.
- **`docs/150-non-root-session-worker/plan.md`** — new §8.1 addendum documenting the regression and root cause; updated the writable-paths note, the "Browser tool regressions" risk, and the touchpoints list.
- **`docs/150-non-root-session-worker/checklist.md`** — entry under the activation-blocker fixes recording the bug + fix + verification.

## Test plan

- `npx vitest run src/server/session/agents/` — 237 pass (incl. the new `playwright-mcp.test.ts`).
- `npm run lint:dev` + `npm run typecheck` — clean.
- **Live reproduction (uid 1000, `/opt/playwright-browsers` at `755 root:root`, pinned `@playwright/mcp` 0.0.75):**
  - Old args → `browser_navigate` returns `EACCES … mkdir '/opt/playwright-browsers/mcp-chrome-for-testing-<hash>'` (exact live symptom).
  - With `--isolated` → `browser_navigate` returns a page snapshot, no EACCES.

Refs https://linear.app/shipit-ai/issue/SHI-31

author: batirko
body:
Phase 5 hardening sprint, `lifecycle_integrity` **L5** — PR **1 of 3** (audit #5/#6/#7). 5a = suppression matching; 5b = highlight re-anchoring; 5c = per-section conflict-identity dedupe. (L6, the `evaluator.ts` split, follows L5.)

## Problem
`anchorText` is stored on every observation (R3b) but never read for matching. Dismissal suppression keyed purely on `blockId:startOffset:endOffset`, so any edit that shifts offsets — or the ledger sweep anchoring the same conflict whole-block at `0:9999` — made a dismissed card **resurface**. "I dismissed this and it came back" is the fastest way to lose trust.

## Change — make `anchorText` load-bearing for suppression
- **`db.ts`:** `DismissalSuppression` gains `anchorText` / `conflictingAnchorText` / `conflictPairKey`. `DB_VERSION` 8 → 9 with a **no-backfill** migration — legacy suppressions keep the fields `undefined` and continue to offset-match.
- **`evaluator.ts`:** export `conflictPairKey` (single source of conflict identity); rewrite `isSpanSuppressed` to match span obs on `(blockId + normalizeText(anchorText))` and `contradiction`/`strategic_tension` on `conflictPairKey`, each with the offset `spanSignature` as fallback. **G1 flattery-resistant gate preserved byte-for-byte** (span-only for high-severity/contradiction/unsupported; category-wide otherwise).
- **`App.tsx`:** `handleDismissObservation` stores the new fields alongside `spanSignature`.

**Effect:** a dismissal holds when surrounding edits shift offsets, and a dismissed per-section contradiction also suppresses the sweep's whole-block re-emission of the same pair.

## Tests
`evaluator.test.ts` → "suppression matching by anchor text (L5a)": anchor holds across offset shift; does **not** hold in a different block; legacy (no `anchorText`) still offset-matches; contradiction pair-key suppresses the sweep re-emission. The two new-behavior tests **verified to fail under the original offset-only logic** (real regression guards); the fallback/different-block tests correctly pass either way.

## Verification
Lint clean · build emits `dist/` · **384 tests pass** (+4).

author: rishsriv
body:
Fixes #10.

## Problem

`sql --full --out file.json` silently truncates large result sets. The server returns a truncated `results` array (default cap 500 rows) alongside the **pre-truncation** `row_count` plus `truncated`/`note` fields. But the CLI's stdout stub dropped `truncated`/`note` and echoed the server's total `row_count`, so an agent reading only the stub — the documented, context-saving workflow — had no signal that the written file held a partial (and, with `ORDER BY`, non-random) slice. Sorts/aggregations then silently ran on incomplete data and the resulting analysis was wrong.

A secondary docs/behavior mismatch: SKILL.md claimed `--full` is capped at 5,000 rows server-side, but the real default is `--max-rows 500`.

## Changes

`scripts/factiq.py` (`emit`):
- Propagate `truncated` and `note` into the stdout stub.
- Add `written_rows` (rows actually written to `--out`) so a mismatch with the server's `row_count` is visible at a glance.
- Print the truncation note to **stderr** as a loud `WARNING`, since silent partial data is a correctness hazard.

`SKILL.md`:
- Reconcile the cap docs — `--full` returns up to `--max-rows` rows (default 500, raisable), not 5,000.

## Verification

Truncating query (default `--max-rows 500`, 800-row result):

```
WARNING: Result truncated to 500 of 800 rows. Narrow the query (date range, fewer series) to fetch the rest.
{
  "out": "/tmp/out10.json",
  "columns": ["series_id", "series_title"],
  "row_count": 800,
  "schema_name": "census",
  "truncated": true,
  "note": "Result truncated to 500 of 800 rows. ...",
  "written_rows": 500
}
```

Non-truncating query stays clean (no warning, no `truncated`/`note`, `written_rows == row_count`).

## What

One pure `resolveDispatchModel` classifier shared by the route-dispatch hook and `ax dispatches` (both the `--candidates` and `--economy` loops), applying **judgment-first** precedence so reviewer/design/audit work is never routed down — even when its description also matches a route-down class. Hardens the `efficient-dispatch` skill to state the directional **implementer→sonnet / reviewer→strong** rule front-and-center.

## Why

Claude Code hooks can't enforce the `Agent` dispatch tool (CC #39814/#40580/#24327/#34692) — the route-dispatch hook is advisory-only. The real lever is the cognitive layer: the orchestrating agent's discipline (the skill) + the code that classifies dispatches. Two surfaces independently decided "what tier does this dispatch want" and **disagreed on the judgment∩route-down cell**: the hook kept it strong (`decideVerdict` rule 0), but `ax dispatches` candidates/economy suggested routing it down and counted it as addressable overspend. This unifies them.

## Changes

- **`packages/hooks-sdk/src/resolve-dispatch-model.ts`** (new, pure, Effect-free) — `resolveDispatchModel(table, desc, agentType) → { tier, match, judgmentStrong, effectiveModel, reason }`. Reuses the existing `JUDGMENT_STRONG_RE` (no new regex).
- **route-dispatch hook** rewired to derive its classification from the helper — behavior provably identical (42 hook/verdict tests unchanged).
- **`ax dispatches` candidates + economy loops** both call the helper and exclude `tier === "judgment"` — judgment work leaves the routable base, overspend, and savings. Honest addressable overspend.
- **`efficient-dispatch` skill**: directional implementer→sonnet / reviewer→strong rule front-and-center (cites the ~\$130 inversion + memory `feedback-review-gets-strong-model`) + a workflow-author note (`ax routing show`; sandboxed `.claude/workflows/*.js` can't import ax; in-tree code calls `resolveDispatchModel`).

## Evidence

- `bun run typecheck`: **0 errors**. `bun scripts/check-no-node-fs.ts`: clean. hooks-sdk **164/164**, dispatch-analytics **53/53** pass.
- `ax hooks backtest route-dispatch --days=7`: 756 calls replayed, **0 would-block / 0 would-warn / 204 would-advise** (advisory-only, as designed).
- `ax dispatches --economy --days=7` before (main) → after (same window):

  | metric | before | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | routable | 177 | 166 (−11 judgment∩match excluded) |
  | ran_expensive | 124 | 123 |
  | ran_cheap | 44 | 34 |
  | overspend | \$717.02 | \$715.56 |
  | addressable | \$459.24 | \$458.66 |

  The dollar swing is small in this window (most excluded rows already ran cheap); the win is **correctness + consistency** — the lens no longer claims review/design/audit work is addressable overspend, and now agrees with the hook.

author: jamessoubry
body:
Closes #115

Replaces the narrow canonical fork bomb pattern with a structural match that catches any function name.

The new pattern detects the defining characteristic of a fork bomb: a shell function whose body contains a pipe into a backgrounded process (`| word &`). This catches `bomb(){ bomb|bomb& }` and `f(){ f|f& }` alongside the classic `:(){ :|:& }`.

The pattern uses `[\w:]+` (instead of `\w+`) so the colon-named canonical form is also covered, since `:` is not a word character in regex.

Legitimate functions with pipes but no background (`foo(){ echo hello | cat; }`) are not affected.

author: marcstraube
body:
## Summary

Adds an **optional transport fallback** to `WebSocketManager` for environments that block WebSocket (strict proxies, corporate firewalls). When WebSocket is unavailable or fails before its first open, the manager switches to a configured fallback — **Server-Sent Events** or **HTTP polling** — behind the *same* event-based API, so consumer code never branches on transport.

Closes #96.

## What changed

- Internal `Transport` interface with three implementations: `WebSocketTransport`, `SseTransport` (EventSource receive + `fetch` POST send), `PollingTransport` (`fetch` GET loop + POST send). The manager keeps the transport-agnostic concerns (state machine, reconnect backoff, message queue + flush, JSON parse/serialize, handler fan-out, selection).
- New config: `fallback` (`'polling' | 'sse' | 'none'`, default `'none'`), `fallbackUrl` (required when fallback is set), `fallbackSendUrl`, `pollInterval`.
- New `activeTransport` getter and `INVALID_CONFIG` error code.
- Binary and heartbeat stay WebSocket-only; SSE/polling are text channels.
- Documented the server contract each fallback expects (`documentation/websocket.md`).

## Selection behavior

Try WebSocket first. If WebSocket is unsupported, or errors/closes before its first open, switch to the fallback. Once WebSocket has connected at least once, later drops reconnect on WebSocket. After falling back, reconnects stay on the fallback transport.

## Test plan

- `pnpm run typecheck` · `pnpm run lint` (0 warnings) · `pnpm run format:check`
- `pnpm run test:coverage` — 4518 tests pass; coverage above thresholds (lines 99.94 / branches 96.91 / funcs 99.51)
- `pnpm run build` · `pnpm run lint:md` · `pnpm run lint:package` · `pnpm run size:check` (websocket 2.34 kB / 2.5 kB)

- #146 — automatic upgrade back to WebSocket while on a fallback (deferred)
- #147 — docs(websocket): fix pre-existing config/method drift

author: alexander-zimmermann
body:
## Was

Neuer Anomalie-Detektor `freezer_icing` in `detect_knx_join.py`, der **Verdampfer-Vereisung des Küchen-Gefrierschranks** früh erkennt.

Hintergrund: Bei Vereisung isoliert die Frostschicht den Verdampfer → schlechterer Wärmeübergang → der Verdichter läuft pro Zyklus länger. Über ein Jahr Daten bestätigt: bei gleicher **warmer** Küchentemperatur driftete der Median-Lauf von ~30 auf ~42 min, während er bei kalter Küche normal blieb — die klassische Vereisungs-Signatur. Bei Kälte fehlt die thermische Last, deshalb wertet der Detektor nur Warm-Läufe.

## Wie

- Sessionisiert Verdichter-Läufe (`>= 120 mA`) aus roh `knx` über ein 21-Tage-Fenster (gaps-and-islands).
- Nur Läufe, die bei **Küche ≥ 24 °C** starteten; Tür-/Abtau-Ausreißer (`> 180 min`) raus.
- **Median** dieser Warm-Läufe gegen eine **feste** Gesund-Baseline (30 min) — eine rollende Baseline würde den langsamen Drift mit-absorbieren und das Signal verschlucken.
- Stufen info/warning/critical = 38/45/55 min.
- Kanäle werden über den **stabilen `ga_catalog`-Namen** aufgelöst, nicht über hartcodierte GA (gleiche Konvention wie `fbh_cold`/`window_while_heating`) — eine in ETS umadressierte GA läuft automatisch weiter.
- Läuft unter dem bestehenden `detect-knx-join`-Cronjob (alle 15 min), tagesgebucket + idempotent. Im Winter still (Küche selten ≥ 24 °C).

## Verifikation

- `ruff check .`, `mypy src`, `pytest -q` (67) lokal grün.
- Detektor-SQL live gegen die TSDB smoke-getestet: 336 Warm-Läufe/21d, Median aktuell **42,2 min → `info`** (driftet über Baseline 30, noch unter Warnstufe — plausibel, der Schrank fängt gerade an zuzufrieren).
- Unit-Tests: Klassifikator-Schwellen + Monotonie-Invarianten (inkl. „Tür-Event-Floor > höchste Icing-Stufe").

## Offen / Folgeschritt

KNX-/Basalte-Zustellung: Es existiert bisher **keine** `anomaly.*` writer-rule für *irgendeinen* UC. Bis diese Zuordnung getroffen ist, landet `freezer_icing` in `mcp_anomalies` + auf NATS, schreibt aber noch auf keine KNX-GA. Schwellen nach dem Abtauen gegen die neue Gesund-Baseline gegenprüfen.

author: nh13
body:
Stacks on #131 (base: `docs/nh_settings-profiles`).

Adds the methylation-specific `-s 0` deviation to the **recommended profile**, alongside `-m 10`: skips Pass-2 re-seeding under `--meth` (redundant in the 3-letter bisulfite alphabet) for **~20% less alignment CPU** at near-neutral accuracy. **No code or default change** — the optimization is already reachable today via `-s 0`; this documents and recommends it. Default `--meth` keeps `-s 10`, so the `meth_oracle` parity test is untouched.

## Evidence
Validated on **~33M holodeck em-seq golden-truth reads**, 10 seeds each, across three references:

| reference | records | net recall Δ (`-s 0` − `-s 10`) | significance |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| single-contig chr22 | 16.9M | −22 (−0.0001%) | McNemar p = 0.87 |
| multi-contig (chr19–22 + ALT/decoy/HLA, 2,977 contigs) | 16.4M | −453 (−0.0028%) | McNemar p = 0.23 |

Placement is **within noise even in the hard cross-contig regime** — same flat curve as `-m 10`, and the sub-0.003% drift sits in the low-MAPQ cross-contig tail.

## Documented caveat
Removing Pass-2 shrinks the candidate set, so MAPQ trends upward (~95% of changed reads). The dominant high-confidence bin (MAPQ 50–60, ~84% of reads) stays **identically calibrated** (0.020% mis-placement either way); the small mid-MAPQ bins (~3% of reads) are modestly-to-~2× more error-prone at a given reported MAPQ. Negligible for methylation quantification; noted for callers that hard-filter on MAPQ in repetitive regions. This is also why it's recommended opt-in rather than defaulted.

## Perf
chr22, single thread, best-of-5: alignment user-CPU **−19.7%** (12.96s vs 16.14s), peak RSS **−6.5%**.

A selective-reseed fallback (skip Pass-2 globally, re-seed only low-confidence reads) was evaluated and rejected — in the multi-contig regime it would re-seed ~13% of reads yet recovers ≈ as many placements as it sacrifices.

Supersedes the default-flip approach in #129 (which would have silently changed every `--meth` user's output and required repinning the oracle test).

Draft to match #131 (pending mdbook render review).

author: vincelaird
body:
## What & why

`claimAll`'s `totals` already carries a **claim-leg** outcome breakdown (`claimedFresh / alreadyClaimed / recoveredAlreadyClaimed`) but nothing for the **settle leg** — which is the multi-wallet-**contended** one. When several wallets run a postgame sweep over the same speculation, at most one settle tx lands and the rest skip/recover, so the settle leg is exactly where "someone else already did it" happens.

This adds the symmetric settle-leg breakdown to `ClaimAllResult.totals`:

```ts
totals: {
  // ...existing...
  settledFresh: number;             // this run sent the settle tx
  alreadySettled: number;           // pre-flight read found it closed → skipped
  recoveredAlreadySettled: number;  // a concurrent settle won the race
}
```

It lets a repeated multi-wallet wrap-up classify the settle leg at the totals level — "I settled it this run" vs "a peer/prior run already had" — without walking `entries[].steps`. (Directly serves the idempotent-postgame goal these follow-ups came from.)

## Implementation

Pure aggregation — **no new on-chain work, no new RPC.** The settle outcomes already live in the canonical `steps[]` (`sent` / `skippedAlreadySettled` / `recoveredAlreadySettled`); the existing claim-leg aggregation loop is extended to count both legs in one pass:

```ts
if (s.name === 'claimPosition') { /* claimedFresh / alreadyClaimed / recoveredAlreadyClaimed */ }
else if (s.name === 'settleSpeculation') { /* settledFresh / alreadySettled / recoveredAlreadySettled */ }
```

**Counts only the sent/skipped/recovered outcomes** — a genuinely-`failed` settle is uncounted (it surfaces in `totals.failed` and the entry's `failed` step), so the three settle counters need **not** sum to the `pendingSettle` entry count. All zero on dry-run (no steps run).

## Additive + forward-compatible

- New fields flow through the CLI payload verbatim (`ClaimAllPayload.totals = ClaimAllResult['totals']`; payload sets `totals: result.totals`) — no CLI command change needed.
- Consumers that ignore unknown fields are unaffected (AGENT_ENVELOPE_SPEC §1/§2.4 forward-compat rule); no zod/wire validator re-checks `totals` (the claim-all envelope is emitted, never re-parsed by the SDK).
- Naming mirrors the claim leg (`settledFresh` ↔ `claimedFresh`); no collision with `totals.claimed` (entry count).

## Docs / tests / verification

- **AGENT_CONTRACT §9** claimAll row now documents both per-leg breakdowns + how to use them for multi-wallet classification. **CHANGELOG** `[Unreleased]` → Added.
- **Tests:** settle-leg totals assertions on the 3 single-entry settle cases (fresh / skipped / recovered), a dry-run all-six-zero assertion, a **new mixed multi-entry sweep** (one of each settle outcome — proves the counters sum across entries), and a CLI transform passthrough test (the settle-leg totals reach the agent payload).
- `yarn typecheck` clean; **sdk 777 passed / cli 792 passed / 0 failed.**
- Adversarial review of the diff caught one real doc bug — the settle-leg jsdoc originally claimed the breakdown "sums to ... the count of `pendingSettle` entries", which is false when a settle genuinely fails. Fixed the wording (and the parallel pre-existing claim-leg jsdoc imprecision). The computation itself was confirmed correct.

body:
This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to master, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## @compiled/react@0.21.3

### Patch Changes

- 55514fd: Fix `LibraryManagedAttributes` to restore React 18 compatibility and `defaultProps` stripping.

  1. `key` no longer accepted `null`, contradicting `React.Attributes` which defines `key?: Key | null | undefined`. This caused `TS2322` errors in React 18 codebases when passing a nullable key (e.g. `key={item?.id ?? null}`).

  2. Using `P` directly instead of `React.JSX.LibraryManagedAttributes<C, P>` broke `defaultProps` stripping for class components — props covered by `defaultProps` were no longer treated as optional at the call site (`TS2740`).

  The fix delegates to `React.JSX.LibraryManagedAttributes<C, P>` (which correctly strips `defaultProps`) and explicitly restores `key?: React.Key | null` to align with `React.Attributes`. This avoids the circular reference issue since `React.JSX.LibraryManagedAttributes` does not route through the global `JSX` namespace.

  Also fixes the `typecheck:react18` test which used `toMatchTypeOf` (which does not catch type narrowing regressions) — replaced with `toEqualTypeOf` on `Managed['key']`.

author: felixgeelhaar
body:
## Summary

Fixes the same false-positive cluster that caused 300K+ findings when scanning `microsoft/autogen` (commit `027ecf0`). Root cause: 10 secret-detection rules used bare character-class patterns like `[a-zA-Z0-9]{32}` without word boundaries (`\b`) or secretShape filtering.

When a vendor keyword (`fcm`, `elk`, `heap`, etc.) appears in an SVG file containing base64-encoded PNG image data, the keyword filter passes and the engine then matches *every possible 32-char substring* in the continuous base64 stream — producing 24,000+ findings per file.

The same issue was briefly noted in the LangGraph scan post (SEC-616, SEC-692, SEC-659) but was not fixed at the time. Fixed now.

## Changes

**`core/analyzers/secrets/rules.go`** — Add `\b` word boundaries and `secretShape: true, minEntropy: 3.5` to 10 rules:

| Rule | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| SEC-455 | `[a-z0-9]{32}` | `\b[a-z0-9]{32}\b` + secretShape |
| SEC-533 | `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{44}` | `\b[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{44}\b` + secretShape |
| SEC-569 | `[a-zA-Z0-9]{24}` | `\b[a-zA-Z0-9]{24}\b` + secretShape |
| SEC-590 | `[a-zA-Z0-9]{32}` | `\b[a-zA-Z0-9]{32}\b` + secretShape |
| SEC-616 | `[a-zA-Z0-9]{32}` | `\b[a-zA-Z0-9]{32}\b` + secretShape |
| SEC-659 | `[a-zA-Z0-9]{32}` | `\b[a-zA-Z0-9]{32}\b` + secretShape |
| SEC-661 | `[a-zA-Z0-9]{32}` | `\b[a-zA-Z0-9]{32}\b` + secretShape |
| SEC-664 | `[a-zA-Z0-9]{32}` | `\b[a-zA-Z0-9]{32}\b` + secretShape |
| SEC-692 | `[a-zA-Z0-9]{32}` | `\b[a-zA-Z0-9]{32}\b` + secretShape |
| SEC-697 | `[a-zA-Z0-9]{32}` | `\b[a-zA-Z0-9]{32}\b` + secretShape |

These rules now match SEC-574 and SEC-629 which already used `\b...\b` + secretShape.

**`core/analyzers/secrets/secrets_test.go`** — 2 new tests:
- `TestBroadPatternRules_NoSVGBase64FalsePositives`: confirms none of the 10 rules fire on simulated SVG base64 content containing the vendor keywords
- `TestBroadPatternRules_DetectRealCredential`: confirms the rules still fire on properly-shaped 32-char tokens in realistic config assignments

**`docs/scan-of-the-week-queue.txt`** — marks `microsoft/autogen` done.

--- PASS: TestBroadPatternRules_DetectRealCredential

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Both HTML files (`index.html` and `EcoApp`) were missing all browser-enforced security headers, and the CDN-loaded Chart.js script had no integrity verification — meaning a compromised CDN could inject arbitrary JS.

**Fixes applied:**

1. **Content Security Policy (CSP)** — `<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy">` added to both files, restricting `script-src`, `style-src`, `font-src`, and `img-src` to only the domains actually used (Google Fonts, jsDelivr CDN, `'self'`).

2. **Subresource Integrity (SRI)** — `integrity="sha384-..."` + `crossorigin="anonymous"` added to the Chart.js `<script>` tag in `EcoApp`. If the CDN serves a tampered file, the browser will reject it.

3. **Clickjacking / MIME-sniffing protection** — `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` meta tags added to both files.

4. **Referrer policy** — `strict-origin-when-cross-origin` prevents leaking full URLs to third-party origins.

5. **Debug logging removed** — `console.log('Initializing Live Monitor...')` deleted from `EcoApp`.

6. **`crossorigin="anonymous"`** added to Google Fonts `<link>` tags in both files for proper CORS handling.

author: immuhammadfurqan
body:
Fixes #4739

## Summary

- `_update_settings()` now calls `_disconnect()` then `_connect()` after applying the delta, so updated settings take effect immediately on the next connection
- Removed the `_warn_unhandled_updated_settings()` call since settings are now actually applied
- No `_do_reconnect()` override needed here — `TTSService` has no reconnect infrastructure, so a direct disconnect + connect is the appropriate pattern (consistent with other TTS services like `GradiumTTSService`)

## How it works

`_connect()` builds the query string fresh from `self._settings.voice`, `self._encoding`, and `self.sample_rate` on every call. After `super()._update_settings(delta)` stores the change, the reconnect submits the updated configuration to the SageMaker endpoint.

Unlike the STT counterpart (#4738), TTS has no VAD deferral concern, so the reconnect is immediate.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify that sending `TTSUpdateSettingsFrame` mid-session causes a reconnect and the new query string (e.g. different `voice`) is sent to the endpoint
- [ ] Verify no reconnect occurs when the settings delta produces no changes

author: janoskonig
body:
## Summary

Implements a dental status timeline feature that tracks the evolution of a patient's odontogram (tooth status) over time. When a tooth treatment is marked as completed, the system automatically:
1. Records the patient's baseline (initial) dental status if not already captured
2. Updates the live odontogram based on the treatment outcome
3. Creates a dated snapshot for audit and historical review

The timeline viewer displays four layers: baseline state → treatment plan (projected) → dated status snapshots → current state.

## Key Changes

- **New timeline component** (`DentalStatusTimeline.tsx`): Read-only viewer showing baseline, historical snapshots, treatment plan projection, and current odontogram state with tab-like navigation between timepoints.

- **Treatment outcome rules** (`lib/tooth-treatment-outcome.ts`): Pure functions that map clinical treatment codes (extraction, filling, root canal, etc.) to resulting tooth base states and flag clearing (caries, periapical, mobility). Handles legacy D-F-M status format and modern structured tooth objects.

- **Snapshot persistence** (`lib/dental-status-snapshots.ts`):
  - `applyCompletedTreatmentToDentalStatus`: Transactional function that ensures baseline capture, updates live odontogram, and creates dated snapshot when a treatment completes.
  - `getDentalStatusTimeline`: Assembles the four-layer timeline (baseline, snapshots, plan, current) for the viewer.

- **Database schema** (`database/migrations/056_dental_status_snapshots.sql`): New `dental_status_snapshots` table with unique constraint on one baseline per patient; indexed by patient and effective date.

- **API endpoint** (`app/api/patients/[id]/dental-status-timeline/route.ts`): GET endpoint returning the complete timeline structure.

- **Treatment completion flow** (`app/api/patients/[id]/tooth-treatments/[treatmentId]/route.ts`): PATCH handler now wraps the status update in a transaction, calls `applyCompletedTreatmentToDentalStatus` when transitioning to 'completed', and returns a `dentalStatusUpdated` flag.

- **UI integration** (`ToothTreatmentPanel.tsx`, `BetegvizsgalatSection.tsx`):
  - Added `onTreatmentCompleted` callback to `ToothTreatmentProvider` so the editable odontogram can sync when a treatment completes (prevents autosave from reverting the server's automatic update).
  - Added `notifyToothTreatmentsChanged()` event dispatch on add/complete/delete/episode actions to refresh dependent UI (e.g., tooth badges).
  - Filter out already-active treatment codes from the add picker (prevents 409 conflicts from duplicate active treatments).

- **Tests** (`__tests__/lib/tooth-treatment-outcome.test.ts`): Unit tests for outcome rule mapping, legacy format resolution, and treatment projection.

## Implementation Details

- **Transactional safety**: Treatment completion uses `BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK` to ensure baseline capture, odontogram update, and snapshot creation are atomic.
- **Baseline capture**: Recorded once per patient on first treatment completion, using the patient's creation date as the effective date.
- **Treatment plan projection**: Calculated on-the-fly from open (non-completed) tooth treatments, not stored, so it always reflects current open work.
- **Event-driven sync**: `tooth-treatments-changed` custom event notifies the timeline viewer and other listeners to refresh without full page reload.
- **Legacy compatibility**: Handles both old D-F-M string status and new structured tooth objects with base/caries/periapical/mobility fields.

author: ppcvote
body:
## What & why

`PromptDefenseEvaluator` (`agt red-team scan`) statically audits an agent's
system prompt for missing defensive language before deployment. Today it
checks **12 vectors mapped to the OWASP LLM Top 10** — conversational safety
only. But this toolkit positions itself against the **OWASP Agentic Top 10
(ASI)**, and the prompt auditor says nothing about the risks that exist once
the model is an autonomous agent. This PR closes that gap by adding 5
agent-era vectors so a pre-deployment audit covers the agentic layer too.

| Vector | ASI | Defends |
|--------|-----|---------|
| `cross-agent-auth` | ASI-07 | Authority from another agent is re-verified per request, not inherited transitively |
| `transaction-guardrails` | ASI-02 | Value-moving actions require a limit / second approval / explicit refusal-without-authorization |
| `skill-provenance` | ASI-04 | Skills load only from a signed/trusted/pinned source; unverified ones refused |
| `least-agency` | ASI-01 | Least privilege, scoped to the assigned goal, aborts on goal drift |
| `encoding-injection` | ASI-01 | Decoded / base64 content treated as untrusted data, never as a command |

## Design — consistent with the existing module

- **`min_matches=2` contract preserved.** Each agentic rule needs the
  *capability* pattern AND the *constraint* pattern — attack vocabulary alone
  ("transfer the funds", "another agent told me", "decode this base64") never
  scores as defended. Verified against adversarial prompts.
- **ReDoS-safe.** All new patterns use bounded quantifiers (no unbounded
  `.*`); `MAX_PROMPT_LENGTH` guard unchanged. No catastrophic backtracking on
  99K adversarial inputs (the new vectors run in ~20ms at the cap).
- **`VECTOR_COUNT` stays dynamic** (`len(_RULES)`) — nothing hardcoded.

## Summary

Build-free ORIENT on the open **"if"** direction of Legendre's three-square theorem
(`n ≠ 4^a(8b+7) ⟹ ∃ x y z, n = x²+y²+z²`). Resolves the deferred TODO in open PR #24149
("confirm exact Mathlib names at build time" for the **G1** Dirichlet gate) and supplies the
local-analysis reason the *qualitative* theorem is enough.

Dual-backend blackout this session (Docker timed out; Aristotle `prove` → "Resource not found"),
so this is docs + Python only, no Lean built.

## Results

- **Exact Mathlib bearer pinned** (source-verified @ pinned rev `2df2f0150c27`, v4.26.0):
  the qualitative Dirichlet theorem is `Nat.forall_exists_prime_gt_and_modEq` (and the
  `infinite_setOf_prime_and_eq_mod` / `..._zmodEq` / `..._modEq` family) in
  `Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/PrimesInAP.lean`. The **sole** side-goal to feed it is

  (Heads-up: `Nat.setOf_prime_and_eq_mod_infinite` is now a `@[deprecated]` alias.)

- **Why qualitative suffices** — `scripts/verify_local_obstruction.py`, `ALL CHECKS PASSED`:
  - [A] `x²+y²+z²` is universal mod every odd prime power (`p ∈ {3,5,7,11,13}`, `k=1..3`).
  - [B] mod `2^k` (`k=3..8`) the non-represented residues are exactly the excluded `4^a(8b+7)` classes.
  - [C] for `n=0..3000`, representable over ℤ ⇔ not excluded — no odd prime ever vetoes.
  So the only local obstruction is 2-adic, cleared by **one** AP-prime → qualitative Dirichlet.

## What's in the PR (new files only; path-disjoint from #24149)

- `G1-dirichlet-bearer.md` — bearer signatures, the coprimality side-condition, local-obstruction
  argument, recommended ACT order. Does **not** touch `knowledge.md` / `state.md` / #24149's script.
- `scripts/verify_local_obstruction.py` — reproducible exact-integer verification.

Released NOT completed — ACT (formalize D1+D2 then G1) still awaits a build host. The Dirichlet
residue classes per `n mod 8` are deliberately left to a primary source (Serre Ch. IV §1.6) at
formalization time rather than reconstructed from memory.

author: isbak
body:
## Summary

Audited every place Compas calls a Navigate REST endpoint (`navigate_client.py` + the routes/service that feed it) and hardened how untrusted browser input flows into those calls. Compas proxies the browser to Navigate server-side, so the two risks are (a) reflecting untrusted input unsafely and (b) letting input redirect a call to an unintended Navigate endpoint. Both were present.

## Findings & fixes

| # | Severity | Where | Issue → Fix |
|---|----------|-------|-------------|
| 1 | **High** | `relationship_review` route | Raw `action` form value was interpolated **unescaped** into an `HTMLResponse` (reflected XSS), and a fake "success" badge was returned for *any* value. → Allowlist the action (`approve`/`reject`), return 400 otherwise, escape all dynamic output. |
| 2 | Medium | artifact/knowledge/relationship action routes | `NavigateError` text (which can echo user-supplied ids) was interpolated unescaped into badge `HTMLResponse`s. → `markupsafe.escape(...)` all error text. |
| 3 | Medium | `NavigateClient` | Ids and action verbs were f-string-interpolated into Navigate paths with no encoding/validation, so a value with `/`, `?`, `..`, or `%2F` could redirect the call to another endpoint. → URL-encode every path segment (`quote(safe="")`) and allowlist the POST action verbs in the client (defense in depth). |
| 4 | Low | graph JSON helpers | `depth` / `min_confidence` query params were unbounded. → Clamp depth to `1..5` and confidence to `0..1` to bound fan-out across Navigate's `/graph` endpoints. |

The JSON error responses (`/graph/*`) were already safe — values are JSON-encoded, not interpolated into HTML.

## Tests

Added regression tests:
- `test_path_ids_are_url_encoded` — crafted id stays inside its path segment
- `test_action_allowlist_rejects_unknown` — invalid actions never reach Navigate
- `test_relationship_review_rejects_unknown_action` / `test_knowledge_review_rejects_unknown_action` — 400 + no reflection + no Navigate call
- `test_artifact_action_error_is_escaped` — error text is HTML-escaped

All 51 tests pass (`pytest`).

author: zpoint
body:
## Summary

Fixes the nightly `test_skyserve_llm[accelerator0]` failure on the `--aws` smoke-test pipeline (e.g. [build 11262](https://buildkite.com/skypilot-1/smoke-tests/builds/11262)). Root cause is an **upstream FastAPI release**, not SkyPilot code.

- Pin `fastapi<0.137` in `tests/skyserve/llm/service.yaml`'s vLLM install.

## What caused the regression

The test's replica runs `uv pip install vllm==0.10.0`, and **vLLM 0.10.0 leaves `fastapi` unpinned**, so the nightly always installs whatever is latest on PyPI.

**`fastapi==0.137.0` was published 2026-06-14 12:51 UTC** — ~12h before the failing 06-15 nightly — and ships an intentional breaking change: `app.routes` is no longer a flat list of `APIRoute`. Included routers are now kept as a nested tree with intermediate `_IncludedRouter` nodes (FastAPI stopped cloning included routers).

vLLM bundles `prometheus-fastapi-instrumentator`, whose metrics middleware iterates `app.routes` and calls `route.path` on every entry. On the new tree it hits an `_IncludedRouter` node and raises:

```
AttributeError: '_IncludedRouter' object has no attribute 'path'
INFO:  ... "GET /v1/models HTTP/1.1" 500 Internal Server Error
```

So **every** request 500s — including the service's `/v1/models` readiness probe. The replica (Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B on a T4, which itself loaded fine in ~5s) never passes readiness, so after the 1800s initial delay it is marked `FAILED_INITIAL_DELAY`, and the test's `sky serve status` wait-loop exits 1.

This is **deterministic, not a flake** (probe 500s 100% of the time), and reproduces on every run until pinned.

### Pass → fail timeline (reconstructed with `uv pip compile --exclude-newer`)

| nightly | fastapi | starlette | prometheus-fastapi-instrumentator | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 06-11 (build 11214, last green `--aws`) | **0.136.3** | 1.3.0 | 8.0.0 | ✅ passed |
| 06-15 (build 11262) | **0.137.0** | 1.3.1 | 8.0.0 | ❌ failed |

The only material change is `fastapi 0.136.3 → 0.137.0`.

## The fix

`fastapi<0.137` resolves to **fastapi 0.136.3 / starlette 1.3.1 / prometheus-fastapi-instrumentator 8.0.0 / vllm 0.10.0** — i.e. the exact stack the last green AWS nightly (06-11) ran with. It excludes only the broken release (and future 0.138+, since the routing-tree change is permanent) until the bundled instrumentator learns to walk the tree.

## Test plan

- Verified the pin resolves cleanly against current PyPI with `uv pip compile` (vllm 0.10.0 requires `fastapi[standard]>=0.115.0`, so the pin is well within range).
- `/smoke-test -k test_skyserve_llm --aws` on this PR (below).

author: etiennechabert
body:
## What

Adds the **medical consumables** category — 18 items (`category = "medical"`, ids `med_*`) — so the in-hideout **Medical Box** (`CollectionBox_Medical`) can be OCR-scanned like the misc Collection Box, with weight + value shown in the Items DB / weight-budget views.

| Family | Items | Weight | Price (₽) | Rarity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bandages | Gauze / Bandage / Military Bandage | 0.05 | 724 / 1 584 / 4 378 | C / U / R |
| Suturing Tools | Suturing Instrument R1 / R2 / Apex | 0.38 | 3 692 / 11 883 / 48 771 | C / U / R |
| Painkillers | Painkiller L1 / L2 / Military Painkiller | 0.08 | 4 121 / 9 110 / 19 262 | C / U / R |
| Syringes | Civilian / Medical / Military / Advanced | 0.03 | 4 826 … 51 371 | C / U / R / R |
| Stims | Adrenaline / H.C. / KB-22 / P4 / Morphine injector | 0.03 | 45 363 … 159 430 | Epic |

## Provenance (per field)

- **Names** — pak-authoritative (`WFItemsStringTable` `medical.*`). Used over upstream, which flattens all three painkillers to "Painkiller" and drops the injector suffixes; the box-scan reads the *in-game* label, so pak names are required for it to match.
- **Weight / price / rarity** — upstream `exfil-zone-assistant` `public/data/medical.json`, the same source the existing misc prices come from (130 of 133 name-matched misc prices are byte-identical to it). Sell prices aren't in the paks (server-side). The painkiller (`0.08`) and suturing (`0.38`) weights are independently **byte-confirmed in the blueprint base-class CDOs**; the rest live in a C++ base class (not byte-extractable) and keep the upstream value (same posture as the curated misc weights).
- **Icons** — cut from the paks' `ItemIcons/Medicals` textures, mapped by **each blueprint's own icon reference** rather than the texture name: the bandage textures are dev-swapped (`WarfareBandage_lv2` "Bandage" references `icon_Gauze`). **KB-22 has no icon anywhere in the paks**, so it reuses the morphine icon (upstream does too).

## App changes

- New **"Medical"** filter in the Items DB (`CategoryFilter::Medical` + button + the `misc | gunsmith | medical` whitelist).
- **No box-scan code change needed** — `match_item`'s strict pass already resolves every catalog item by name. The existing `box` / `stash` / `gunsmith` OCR gates stay green, so the 18 new names cause no regression.
- New integrity test `medical_items_are_complete_and_unambiguous`: every medical item ships an embedded icon + weight + price, and every medical name is unique across the whole catalog (so a scanned tile can't resolve ambiguously).

## Version

`0.7.1 → 0.7.2` (clears the `v0.7.1` tag).

## Verification

`cargo test --workspace` green (357 unit tests incl. the new one), `clippy -D warnings` clean, `fmt` clean. Icons visually reviewed.

## Follow-up (out of scope)

Scanning works by name today, but adding the Medical Box to the OCR **eval/gate fixtures** needs a real Medical Box screenshot captured in VR — once available, the box's tab/subtitle words (Bandages / Painkillers / Syringes / Stims / Suturing) may need adding to `box_scan::CATEGORY_WORDS`.

body:
### Motivation

- Provide a small, dependency-free scene/event engine to model a branching locked-room mystery and permit embedding in a browser, CLI, or test harness. 
- Represent narrative content as immutable scene metadata and manage runtime progress and reveals through a single `SceneEngine` runtime state. 
- Support staging timed reveals and deterministic ending resolution based on accumulated clues and accusations.

### Description

- Add `src/sceneEngine.js` which defines `SCENES`, `DEFAULT_STATE`, `ENDINGS`, `ENDING_TEXT`, helper functions (`applyStateChanges`, `choiceIsAvailable`, `sceneIsAvailable`, `hasRequiredClues`, `resolveEnding`), staged reveal helpers, and the `SceneEngine` class with `choose`, `getAvailableChoices`, `peekStagedReveals`, `playStagedReveals`, and `playStagedRevealsAsync` methods. 
- Implement a concrete scene set for the mystery (intro, murders, investigations, blackout, final accusation, endings) with choice wiring, stateChanges, transitions, and staged reveals. 
- Add `test/sceneEngine.test.js` to validate scene metadata, a perfect-case playthrough path (including staged reveals), choice/scene gating, and ending resolution logic. 
- Add `package.json` with a `test` script (`node --test test/*.test.js`) and a `README.md` showing basic usage and exported API.

### Testing

- Ran the automated test suite with `node --test test/*.test.js` (the `npm test` script runs the same command) and all tests passed. 
- The tests exercise scene metadata presence, the perfect-case progression including staged reveals, requirement gating via `choiceIsAvailable`/`sceneIsAvailable`, and `resolveEnding` outcomes.

body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

Fill three documentation gaps in `docs/security/how-to-authenticate.md` for the v2 Web UI OIDC login with Keycloak:

1. **Secure context requirement** — A note in the *OAuth Mode* section explaining that Web UI OIDC login uses the Authorization Code flow with PKCE, which depends on the browser Web Crypto API and therefore requires a secure context (HTTPS or `localhost`). Plain HTTP on a non-`localhost` host fails.
2. **Separate client configurations** — A new *Enable Web UI OIDC login with Keycloak* subsection that distinguishes the confidential client (machine/engine flows) from a public client (`Client authentication` off, `Standard flow` on) required by the browser UI, with the matching `oidc`-provider configuration.
3. **Token issuer alignment** — Guidance to set the Keycloak realm Frontend URL so the `iss` claim matches across split-hostname deployments, avoiding `JWT iss claim value rejected`.

### Why are the changes needed?

Users setting up the v2 Web UI with Keycloak OIDC hit undocumented failures: login breaks over plain HTTP, a single confidential client does not work for the browser, and split-hostname setups get token rejections. These were reported in #11716.

Fix: #11716

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No code change. Documentation only.

### How was this patch tested?

Documentation-only change. Verified with the repo docs audit scripts (title/intro/heading/spacing and internal link/anchor checks) — all pass.

author: othinas
body:
# Chapter Edit Flow — Keyboard Save & Flexible Status

## Summary

Two improvements to the inline chapter edit flow, driven by operator feedback that status only updated effectively near "Concluído":

1. **Flexible status** — free movement between any non-paid statuses (Pendente / Em edição / Em revisão / Retake) in any order, with no required fields. Narrator + editor + minutagem (> 0) are required only at the entry edges of **Concluído** and **Pago**. **Pago** stays the sole guarded status: entered only from Concluído, left only to Concluído with explicit reversion confirmation, financial fields immutable while paid.
2. **Keyboard** — `Enter` saves and `Esc` cancels the edit row from any focused control, open-aware (an open Select / Popover / calendar acts first; the Save/Cancel buttons keep native behavior; a submit in flight is not re-triggered).

Full-stack change: the domain state machine (`isValidTransition`) is the source of truth, the service enforces it, and the UI mirrors the topology. It required a **constitution amendment (Principle III → v2.18.0)**, committed with the planning artifacts.

## Changes

**Domain & service**
- `chapter-state-machine.ts`: rewrite `isValidTransition` to the new matrix (free non-paid graph; field guards on completed/paid; narrow paid edges) + compile-time exhaustiveness guard.
- `chapter-service.ts`: single transition path through `assertTransition` (now handles `from === "paid"`); removed `assertReversion`; documented why `status` is excluded from `PAID_LOCKED_FIELDS`.
- `chapter-transitions.ts` / `error-codes/chapter.ts`: reworded PT-BR messages to the "concluir ou pagar" context.

**UI**
- `chapter-status-select.tsx`: `reachableTargets` mirrors topology only (Pago disabled unless current is Concluído).
- `use-chapter-row-edit.ts`: new open-aware `handleRowKeyDown` (Enter → submit / Esc → cancel, no double submit).
- `chapter-row-edit-mode.tsx`: wire `onKeyDown`; `chapter-row-edit-actions.tsx`: `data-row-actions` marker.

**Tests** — TDD throughout (RED → GREEN); pre-existing tests realigned to the new graph.
- Unit: state-machine matrix, transition messages, status-select topology, keyboard hook.
- Integration: free transitions, field guards at the completed/paid edges, paid edges, audit regression (FR-016).
- E2E: free status change, paid-guard visibility, 7 keyboard scenarios.

**Governance/docs**: constitution v2.18.0 + CLAUDE.md mirror; full `specs/036-chapter-edit-flow` artifacts.

## Verification

- `lint` clean · `test:unit` **1337 passed** · `test:integration` **327 passed** · `build` clean.
- `test:e2e` **242/243** — the single failure is a pre-existing flake in `chapters-table-scroll` (layout box measurement under parallel load); it passes in isolation and is unrelated to this change (no status/keyboard surface).
- **Double review (financial model)**: the code-reviewer confirmed no chapter can become `paid` at R$0, `PAID_LOCKED_FIELDS` are intact, and the reversion path is gated by `confirmReversion`; its HIGH finding (restore the exhaustiveness guard) was addressed. Human second review pending at merge per the financial-model rule.

## Evidence

- Spec: `specs/036-chapter-edit-flow/spec.md`
- Plan: `specs/036-chapter-edit-flow/plan.md`
- Constitution (Principle III, v2.18.0): `.specify/memory/constitution.md`

author: vcons002-ship-it
body:
## What

Fixes the keyless stock price feed on desktop.

## Root cause (confirmed with live tests, not a guess)
- `stock_quote` fetched **Stooq's** CSV. Stooq **blocks the desktop proxy's non-browser User-Agent** — the request just **times out** (`curl` exit 28 with the app's UA) — and **rate-limits/IP-blocks** even with a browser UA (returns empty or an HTML "page moved").
- `market_analysis` already uses **Yahoo's** chart endpoint, which **works with the proxy's own UA**. So the model had real indicators (the moving averages/range it cited) but **no live quote**, and reported the feed as "offline / needs an extension or Schwab."

## The fix
Move `stock_quote` onto the same reliable Yahoo source:
- `stocks.ts`: `yahooQuoteUrl` + `parseYahooQuote` (reads the chart `meta` block — price, day high/low, volume, time; session open from the day's bar). The Stooq helpers stay for the browser extension/tests.
- `engine.worker.ts`: `handleStockQuote` and the buddy `stockQuote` dep now fetch Yahoo JSON instead of Stooq CSV.

Both keyless market features now ride one proven endpoint.

## ⚠️ Requires a desktop rebuild
The desktop app bundles `web/dist`, so this only takes effect after `pnpm build:desktop` (or `pnpm dev:desktop`) — a plain `git pull` won't pick it up.

## Verification
`pnpm -r run typecheck` (5 projects), `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm test` (**920 passing**, +3 Yahoo-quote tests), `pnpm --filter @visual-reader/web run build` — all green. Live-verified the Yahoo endpoint returns a usable quote with the app's exact User-Agent.

## Summary (roadmap §6 / H1)
The research and automation harnesses had **no domain workflow prompt** — only the generic coding-agent prompt (`CODING_DISCIPLINE_BLOCK` / `CODING_WORKFLOW_BLOCK`). This adds two lean, **default-OFF** guidance blocks following the exact `prompt_guidance.py` contract (`search_decision_block` etc.): each returns `""` when its flag is off, so prompt assembly stays byte-identical.

- **`<research_methodology>`** (`MAGI_RESEARCH_METHODOLOGY_ENABLED`): ground claims in sources opened this turn, corroborate load-bearing facts across ≥2 independent sources, prefer primary sources, attribute facts, report source conflicts.
- **`<automation_methodology>`** (`MAGI_AUTOMATION_METHODOLOGY_ENABLED`): state the deliverable up front, plan→act→confirm each step, back completion claims with this-turn evidence, report blockers explicitly, no partial-as-complete.

- **Guidance, NOT enforcement** (the roadmap's explicit distinction). Independent env flags.
- Flags parsed in `config/env.py` (allowlisted → no flag-read-budget hit, same as the sibling prompt-guidance flags; not in the `flags.py` registry, so env-reference shows no drift — consistent with siblings).

Closing on "press outside" used a union of the window, text-field and list-item responses and tested `hovered()`/`is_pointer_button_down_on()`. # Summary

- This PR further improves support and interoperability for sidre's Python bindings 
- It improves lifetime management for sidre entities in Python interface.

body:
## Summary

Wires the section editor to the Hocuspocus collab service shipped in Slices 1 + 2a. Editor switches from single-user to real-time multi-user mode automatically when both `NEXT_PUBLIC_COLLAB_ENABLED=1` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_COLLAB_URL` are set in Vercel env. Until then, **the editor falls back to its existing single-user path — byte-identical behavior with pre-Slice-2b deploys.** This PR is safe to merge before Slice 2c deploys the Hocuspocus service.

## What ships

- **`src/lib/collab-user.ts`** — `pickColorForUser(userId)` deterministic palette picker (12 colors tuned for the dark canvas) so each collaborator has a stable cursor color across reconnects + pages.
- **`src/app/(app)/proposals/[id]/sections/SectionsClient.tsx`** — accepts new `currentUser` prop, builds per-section `CollabConfig`, passes to `RichSectionEditor`. `fetchCollabToken` hits the `/api/collab/token` endpoint shipped in Slice 2a.
- **`src/app/(app)/proposals/[id]/sections/page.tsx`** — passes signed-in user (id + display name) into the client component.

## Deliberately deferred to Slice 2d (low priority)

Server-side body_doc projection. In Slice 2b, every editor `onChange` still fires a client-side `saveSectionAction` — fine for 1-5 concurrent users but inefficient (N users = N writes per keystroke). Slice 2d will move persistence to the Hocuspocus `onStoreDocument` hook so only one debounced write fires per doc change regardless of how many editors are open.

## Activation path (Slice 2c — operator)

1. Deploy `services/collab/` to Fly.io (Dockerfile + README ready; see `services/collab/README.md`)
2. Set Hocuspocus env vars on Fly: `AUTH_SECRET` (same as Next app), `DATABASE_URL` (Neon main DB)
3. Route a domain like `collab.forge.app` to the Fly app
4. Add to Vercel env (Production):
   - `NEXT_PUBLIC_COLLAB_ENABLED=1`
   - `NEXT_PUBLIC_COLLAB_URL=wss://collab.forge.app`
5. Redeploy. Two browsers on same section → presence cursors appear.

## Pre-push self-review

| Concern from `docs/PRE_PUSH_CHECKLIST.md` | Status |
|---|---|
| Missing `recordAudit` on tenant mutations | N/A — no new mutations; collab session is read+write to existing `proposal_section` through unchanged `saveSectionAction` |
| Missing `recordRead` on sensitive reads (PDF render, share-link load, USAspending lookup) | N/A — no new reads |
| Subtle isolation issues (`organizationId` referenced but not used in `where`) | addressed: `docName: section/<sectionId>` is verified server-side in `services/collab/src/auth.ts` (Hocuspocus `onAuthenticate` checks the existing `yjs_doc` row's `organization_id` matches the JWT's `orgId`) |
| Session-derived org context (`user.organizationId` used in a query instead of `requireCurrentOrg()` result) | N/A — page already calls `requireCurrentOrg()`; `currentUser` carries only `id` + `displayName`, not org |
| `organizationId` as a server-action parameter (caller-controlled) | N/A — `organizationId` flows server-side through the token endpoint, not from caller |
| Cache invalidation gaps (`revalidatePath("/")` missing on Command-Center-affecting mutations) | N/A — no new mutations |
| Cron handlers without `Authorization: Bearer ${CRON_SECRET}` check | N/A — no cron handlers |
| Schema change without matching `drizzle/[NNNN]_*.sql` content | N/A — no schema change |
| Drizzle index parity gap (SQL migration creates an index that `schema.ts` doesn't declare) | N/A — no migration |
| Constant-condition filter/map callbacks (callback ignores its argument) | N/A — no filter/map |
| Dead-store / unused destructured setters not prefixed with `_` | addressed: every new destructured binding is used |
| New external API call without timeout / error handling | addressed: `fetchCollabToken` throws on non-OK status with the response code; the editor's catch block falls back to single-user behavior silently |
| New file without server-only guard where it touches DB | N/A — `collab-user.ts` is pure (hash + palette lookup), no DB |
| Inbox-parity: any new `in_app` `notification_delivery` write also inserts a matching `notification` row | N/A — no notifications |
| SELECT-then-UPDATE pattern: UPDATE filters by collected IDs (`inArray(id, ...)`), NOT by the same predicate as the SELECT | N/A — no SELECT-then-UPDATE |
| Export completeness: data-export endpoints' projections include every tenant-configured field from the source table (skip large blobs deliberately with a comment) | N/A — no exports |

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean
- [x] `npm run lint` clean
- [x] `npm run check:rsc` clean
- [x] `npm run check:isolation` clean (32/32)
- [ ] After merge to prod (before Slice 2c flag flip): visit `/proposals/[id]/sections` — editor renders as before, no collab attempt, byte-identical UX
- [ ] After Slice 2c deploys + flag flips: open same section in two browsers, verify presence cursors with stable per-user colors

## Risk

**Very low.** Without the env-var flag flip from Slice 2c, this PR is a no-op — `buildCollabConfig` returns `undefined`, editor stays single-user. After Slice 2c, the editor connects to Hocuspocus; if Hocuspocus is unreachable the connection silently fails and the editor continues working (proven by the lazy-init pattern in `RichSectionEditor.tsx` from Slice 2a).

## What's next

- **BL-9 Slice 2c** — operator deploys `services/collab/` to Fly.io + flips flags. ~30 min operator work.
- **BL-17** — Stripe vs Paddle research returning from background agent; will surface recommendation when complete.

author: zmnobug
body:
## Summary

This PR adds an optional radix prefix cache backend for paged KV reuse in PyPTO Serving.

The default behavior remains unchanged: if users do not specify a backend, serving still uses the existing `hash` prefix cache path. The new radix path is enabled only with:

```bash
--prefix-cache-backend radix
```

Related issue: #38

## Motivation

The existing hash prefix cache works by matching full-block hash chains. This PR adds a radix-tree-based backend that can manage shared token prefixes more directly:

- Store page-aligned token prefixes in a compressed radix tree.
- Map matched prefixes to physical KV page IDs.
- Reuse cached KV pages across requests with the same long prefix.
- On a prefix hit, schedule only the unmatched suffix for prefill.
- Keep existing page attention kernels and paged KV storage unchanged.

## Main Changes

- Add `RadixPrefixCache`, a page-aligned compressed radix tree for prefix-to-page mapping.
- Add `--prefix-cache-backend {hash,radix}` to the CLI.
- Thread `prefix_cache_backend` through engine and scheduler config.
- Add model-scoped radix keys to avoid cross-model KV reuse.
- Extend `KvCacheManager` with radix match/insert APIs and explicit request/cache page ref handling.
- Add a scheduler radix path parallel to the existing hash path.
- Lock matched radix nodes while requests use cached prefix pages.
- Insert only completed page-aligned prefixes after execution.
- Evict unlocked radix-owned pages before reporting KV block allocation failure.

## Runtime Behavior

Cold request:

- radix lookup misses;
- full prefill runs;
- completed page-aligned prefix is inserted into radix cache.

Hit request:

- radix lookup finds shared prefix pages;
- scheduler attaches cached page IDs to the request;
- `num_computed_tokens` advances to the matched prefix length;
- only suffix prefill is scheduled.

Miss request:

- radix lookup misses;
- normal full prefill runs;
- the new prefix can be cached for future requests.

## Review Feedback Addressed

Follow-up commit `107db2d` addresses review feedback:

- Evict radix-owned pages before allocation failure.
- Let scheduler allocation go through `KvCacheManager.allocate_blocks()` so radix eviction can run.
- During chunked prefill, insert only completed page-aligned token/page slices.
- Reduce repeated radix eviction scans by evicting from an LRU-sorted candidate batch.
- Keep the HTTP probe script local-only instead of including it in the PR diff.

## Validation

Unit and scheduler tests:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/test_radix_cache.py -q
```

```text
13 passed
```

Full test suite:

```bash
python -m pytest tests -q
```

```text
37 passed
```

Qwen3-14B serving validation with radix enabled:

```text
expected_radix_hit_pages=2
expected_radix_hit_tokens=256
```

Observed radix hit logs:

```text
matched_tokens=256 matched_pages=2
scheduled_prefill_tokens=9 computed_tokens=256 cached_pages=2 allocated_pages=1
```

Latency result from cold / hit / miss probing:

```text
hit_avg=0.398s
miss_avg=1.035s
miss/hit=2.60x
hit_faster_pairs=3/3
```

This confirms that repeated long-prefix requests reuse cached KV pages, skip the matched 256 prefix tokens, and only compute the suffix prefill.

## Compatibility

- Default backend remains `hash`.
- Existing page attention kernels are unchanged.
- Existing paged KV storage format is unchanged.
- Radix entries are model-scoped.
- Radix matching and insertion are page-aligned.

> [!NOTE]
> AI-generated with GitHub Copilot.

## Summary

This PR targets two low-risk steady-state refresh wins and restores `microsoft/vcpkg` to the active fetch set:

- persist `comment_fetch_progress` to committed CSVs so future runs can resume comment fetching durably
- skip `review_fetch_progress` rows already marked `failed` unless `--retry-failed` is explicitly requested
- add `microsoft/vcpkg` back to workflow `REPOS` so the freshness banner remains honest for the displayed repo list

## Details

### Durable comment progress

`fetch_comments.py` already maintains `comment_fetch_progress` in SQLite, but that state was not being exported or restored. That meant each workflow run started the comment scan fresh from the default ~14-month lookback.

This PR wires that table into the existing CSV backup/restore path:

- `backup_csvs.py` now exports `comment_fetch_progress`
- `load_csv.py` now restores it when present, while still tolerating older checkouts where the CSV does not exist yet

I intentionally did **not** pre-seed `data/comment_fetch_progress.csv` in the repo. That would speed up the very first post-merge run, but it also risks hiding any older missing `pr_first_comment` rows if prior history was incomplete. The safer approach is to let the first merged run create the durable progress file naturally.

### Skip known failed review PRs by default

`fetch_reviews.py` previously skipped only `status='complete'`, so PRs that had already exhausted retries with `status='failed'` were retried again on every refresh.

This PR changes the default selection logic to skip both `complete` and `failed` rows. Operators can still opt back into retrying failed rows with `--retry-failed`, which clears those failure markers before fetching.

### Restore vcpkg to the active fetch set

The site still displays `microsoft/vcpkg`, so excluding it from workflow `REPOS` made the freshness banner misleading.

This PR adds `microsoft/vcpkg` back to `REPOS`. It remains excluded from `PUSH_REPOS` and `REVIEW_REPOS`, matching the existing scope of those more expensive side fetches.

## Validation

- `python -m py_compile backup_csvs.py load_csv.py fetch_reviews.py update_html_timestamp.py fetch_comments.py`
- `python load_csv.py --force`
- required local review passes:

Closes #293. Non-protected → standing approval.

The root `vitest.root.config.mjs` (the `scripts/__tests__` suite) set **no `testTimeout`**, so tests that spawn real `eslint`/`tsc` subprocesses and scan the whole repo defaulted to vitest's **5s** and flaked under CPU contention during the full parallel `pnpm test`. Improves CI reliability for **every** future PR (fewer spurious re-run round-trips).

## Summary

Stands up working deployments of the `apps/sandbox` CMS to all three target platforms — AWS Lambda, AWS Fargate, and Vercel — and fixes a real API bug found along the way. Each platform required its own fixes, all documented as runbooks in `docs/deployment/`.
