author: hectorvent
body:
## Summary

Adds phase-1 Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) emulation: a local OpenID Connect provider that replaces the static unsigned-token stub. Issues RS256-signed JWTs from a stable signing key persisted across restarts, serves an OpenID discovery document (`/.well-known/openid-configuration`) and JWKS (`/discovery/v2.0/keys`) derived from the request base URL, and handles the non-interactive **client-credentials** and **ROPC** grants in both v1.0 and v2.0 token shapes. App-only tokens carry `idtyp=app`, every token a unique `uti`, and token-endpoint errors use Azure's shape (`error_codes`, `trace_id`, `correlation_id`, `AADSTS` code). Seeds a default tenant and dev app registration so `ClientSecretCredential` works with zero setup. Enabled by default; incoming-token enforcement (`validate-tokens`) stays opt-in so existing services keep accepting any Bearer token in dev.

Also adds ARM `GET /subscriptions`, `GET /tenants`, and `Microsoft.*/checkNameAvailability` endpoints, plus a new **Azure CLI (`az`) BATS compatibility suite** that registers a custom `az cloud`, logs in via `az login --service-principal` against the Entra token endpoint, and drives `az` against resource group, storage (+blob), Key Vault (+secret), vnet/NIC, ACR, and Redis.

Closes #23 (phase 1). App-registration management, Microsoft Graph CRUD, and interactive flows follow in later phases.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix (`fix:`)
- [x] New feature (`feat:`)
- [ ] Breaking change (`feat!:` or `fix!:`)
- [ ] Docs / chore

## Azure Compatibility

Verified with the new `compat-azcli` suite (real `az` CLI, service-principal login through the Entra token endpoint) and the existing Terraform/OpenTofu suites (token response shape preserved). Entra OIDC checked against `ClientSecretCredential`. Token endpoint API: v1.0 and v2.0 shapes.

## Checklist

- [x] `./mvnw test` passes locally (176/177; the lone failure — `AksDockerTest#getClusterArmShape` — is a pre-existing k3s/Docker environment issue that also fails on `origin/main`, unrelated to this change)

## Summary

Teaches the host launcher (`scripts/run_anvil.py`) to start per-session sidecar
containers, each on a docker network scoped to a single harness session. Until
now the launcher started only long-lived (`shared`) sidecars on the harness's
existing network; this adds the per-session lifecycle and the network isolation
it needs.

## What this does

When a discovered sidecar declares a per-session lifecycle, the launcher now:

- creates a docker network named for the harness container's `--name`, so
  concurrent harness sessions cannot reach each other's sidecars by container
  name;
- starts each per-session sidecar on that network under its canonical
  `--network-alias`, so the name the agent dials is identical across worktrees
  (never the session-suffixed container name);
- connects each network-facing `shared` sidecar to the session network for the
  duration of the session, and disconnects -- but does not stop -- it on exit;
- joins the harness to the session network plus the pre-existing `NETWORK=`
  network.

Because `docker run` attaches only one network at creation, a harness that joins
both networks is created, connected to the extra network, then started attached
(`docker create` -> `docker network connect` -> `docker start --attach`). A new
pure `tongs.to_create_argv` rewrites only the `run` subcommand to `create`,
preserving every other token, so the create path reuses the exact argv the
Makefile built.

On exit -- including Ctrl-C -- the per-session sidecars and the per-session
network are torn down (and the connected `shared` sidecars disconnected) while
the long-lived `shared` sidecars keep running. The per-session connect is made
idempotent with a best-effort disconnect first, so a network left behind by a
hard-killed prior session does not wedge the next launch.

## Structure

The per-session network calls (create / connect / disconnect / remove) and the
create -> connect -> start harness run go through the existing `DockerCLI` seam,
so the whole sequence is unit-tested against an in-process fake: network
create/teardown, per-session sidecar start under its alias, shared-sidecar
connect/disconnect, readiness probing on the session network, Ctrl-C teardown,
the missing-`--name` guard, and the byte-identical passthrough exec.

author: mekenthompson
body:
## Summary

`switchroom update` refreshes the separate-compose singletons (`refresh-hostd`, `refresh-web`) but **never touched hindsight** — which runs as a standalone `docker run` container (managed by `memory setup`, not the agent fleet's compose project) on a floating `:latest` tag that `pull-images` / `--pin` don't touch. So every `update` silently left hindsight on whatever stale `:latest` it last started with.

**This is the exact gap that bit us:** #2412 (stable worker_id + reaper) and #2416 (backups / healthcheck / self-maintenance) were baked into `:latest` weeks ago, but the running hindsight container kept serving the pre-fix image until I recreated it by hand during the v0.15.41 roll. Without this, it would silently drift stale again on the next deploy.

## What

- **`memory setup --recreate`** — pull latest image + recreate the container, **reusing its current published port** so `memory.config.url` never changes under the fleet (a silent port change would point every agent's MCP client at a dead URL). Falls back to `pickHindsightPorts()` when nothing is running.
- **New `refresh-hindsight` step** in the update flow, mirroring `refresh-hostd`/`refresh-web`: invokes `memory setup --recreate`, gated on `memory.backend === "hindsight"`, skipped on `--skip-images`.
- Helpers `pullHindsightImage()` + `getRunningHindsightPorts()` in `src/setup/hindsight.ts`.

After this, `switchroom update` keeps hindsight current like every other component — no separate manual `memory setup` dance.

## Test plan
- [x] `update.test.ts`: `refresh-hindsight` present in the plan (+1 step, count assertions updated); gating verified — active when backend=hindsight, skipped when not / on `--skip-images`.
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean; update + rollout suites green (62 tests).
- Manual: the `memory setup --recreate` path is the same recreate I ran live during the v0.15.41 roll (port-reuse landed on 18888, data intact).

## Scope note
Scoped to `switchroom update` (the reported gap). The separate `rollout` command has the same singleton steps and could get `refresh-hindsight` too — quick follow-up if wanted.

author: thad0ctor
body:
## Summary

Replaces the three mutually-exclusive NVFP4 cross-entropy booleans with a single head-aware option:

```yaml
nvfp4_training:
  lm_head_cross_entropy: off | auto | fp4 | bf16 | fp8   # default: off
```

`auto` inspects the already-swapped `lm_head` and routes to the matching tiled-CE kernel:
- NVFP4-packed store (`quantize_lm_head: true`) → **fp4** kernel
- plain frozen bias-free `nn.Linear` → **bf16** kernel
- otherwise → materialized CE path (with a warning)

`fp8` is never auto-selected (it shares the plain-`nn.Linear` head with bf16 but carries fp8 parity caveats), so it's opt-in only via an explicit `fp8`.

### Why

The old `fused_fp4_cross_entropy` / `bf16_lm_head_cross_entropy` / `fp8_lm_head_cross_entropy` booleans were mutually exclusive and the "correct" one was fully determined by the lm_head dtype — easy to misconfigure. In particular, `fused_fp4_cross_entropy: true` **without** `quantize_lm_head` silently no-op'd back to the materialized path (no error). The unified flag makes the wrong combination unrepresentable and fails fast on the rest.

(Context: the standard liger FLCE / axolotl `cut_cross_entropy` plugins don't work under NVFP4 — they read a dense `lm_head.weight` and collapse under SR grads — which is why these three native kernels exist. This PR just unifies their front-end.)

## Changes

- **New dispatcher** `kernels/lm_head_ce.py` — inspects the head and routes to the existing fp4/bf16/fp8 patchers. `fused_ce_vocab_block` now threads into all three (was fp4-only).
- **Schema** (`schemas/nvfp4.py`) — new `lm_head_cross_entropy` enum + `fused_ce_fp4_matmul` (renamed from `fused_fp4_cross_entropy_fp4_matmul`). An after-validator deprecation-aliases the three old booleans + old matmul name (parse with `DeprecationWarning`); conflicting new+old or two-old configs raise. New `fp4_cross_entropy_active` property.
- **Validators** (`schemas/config.py`, `schemas/validation.py`) — mutual-exclusion is now structural; the `cut_cross_entropy` guard and CE-conflict check read the resolved mode. fp4-without-`quantize_lm_head` and bf16/fp8-with-`quantize_lm_head` now error at config time.
- **patch_manager** — three CE call-sites collapsed to one dispatcher call via helpers that work on both the pydantic model and `DictDefault` test configs. Eval-only `fp8_lm_head` stays separate.
- **Backward compat** — the three old booleans still work (mapped with a deprecation warning).
- **Docs / examples** — `docs/nvfp4_training.qmd` reworked to lead with the unified flag; config-reference table updated (old flags marked deprecated); example configs migrated and de-benchmarked.

## Tests

- New `tests/kernels/test_lm_head_ce.py` — CPU dispatcher routing (off/auto/fp4/bf16/fp8, plain-vs-trainable head, vocab-block threading, env override).
- New unified-flag block in `tests/e2e/test_nvfp4_integration.py` — deprecation mapping, conflict raises, gate validators, auto-resolution.
- **50 non-GPU schema/gate/dispatch tests pass.** GPU kernel-math tests unchanged (kernel function names preserved). All 5 nvfp4 example configs validate.

> Not yet run on GPU — the kernel correctness + e2e training tests need a Blackwell run before merge.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added unified `lm_head_cross_entropy` configuration option for controlling cross-entropy optimization modes.
  * Added `fused_ce_fp4_matmul` and `fused_ce_vocab_block` parameters for fine-tuning cross-entropy behavior.

* **Documentation**
  * Updated configuration reference with new options and long-context training recommendations.
  * Updated example configurations to use the new unified option.

* **Deprecation**
  * Legacy boolean cross-entropy flags now deprecated; automatic mapping to new option with warnings.

* **Tests**
  * Expanded test coverage for new configuration validation and cross-entropy patching behavior.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Migration note

`fused_fp4_cross_entropy: true` with `quantize_lm_head: false` is now a **config-validation error** (the deprecated flag maps to `lm_head_cross_entropy: fp4`, which requires `quantize_lm_head`). Previously this combination silently fell back to materialized CE. Use `lm_head_cross_entropy: bf16` / `auto` for a bf16 head, or add `quantize_lm_head: true`.

author: stateofkate
body:
## What

Reverts the "Route probe claude-code to the direct Anthropic API" change introduced by **#363** (`6cc9cfa`).

This fully removes the change from `main`:
- Restores `_agent_uses_bedrock()` to its original `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=="1"` **OR** `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` logic (it had been narrowed to **bearer-token-only**).
- Removes `_claude_code_forces_direct_api()` and the probe-scoped direct-API routing in `_build_agent_config` / the env-clear at `Job.create`.
- Reverts the accompanying test changes.

After this revert, `oddish/src/oddish/workers/harbor_runner.py` and `tests/test_harbor_runner.py` are byte-identical to their pre-#363 state.

## Why

#363 bundled a **probe-scoped** fix together with a **global** rewrite of `_agent_uses_bedrock()`. The global part narrowed Bedrock detection to require `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`, which can flip **normal (non-probe) claude-code trials** off Bedrock onto the direct Anthropic API on any worker that has `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1` but no bearer token — a new 400 vector. Production 400s began ~7pm, near #363's merge window, so we are rolling it back to a known-good state.

## Notes

- **#366 (`2b4d833`)** has the identical title but is an empty/no-op commit (zero files changed); it contributed nothing, so reverting #363 alone fully removes the change. No separate revert of #366 is needed.
- **#359** (`fix/claude-agent-bedrock-model-id-mismatch`) was never merged to `main`, so nothing to revert there. Its only behavioral change is unreachable in the cloud (workers bake `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1`), so it is not implicated in the prod 400s.
- The legitimate probe claude-code direct-API fix will be re-applied **probe-scoped only** (without the global `_agent_uses_bedrock()` change) in a follow-up PR.

body:
## Summary

Closes the **lone remaining `sorry`** in the Goodman-counterexample discharge for Erdős #1047 (Grunsky's convex-lemniscate question), and **registers** the now-complete certificate so the gallery machine-checks it.

`Proofs/Erdos1047OQ02Certificate.lean` now has **no `sorry`** and proves `goodman_counterexample_proof` — the *exact* statement of the parent's `axiom goodman_counterexample` — with **no new axioms**, via the registered topological bridge `componentContaining_lemniscate_not_convex_of_chord_exits` (`Erdos1047OQ02Reduction.lean`).

## What was closed

`goodmanArc_subset_lemniscate`: the 4-segment polyline `−i → (1−i)/2 → 2 → (1+i)/2 → +i` lies inside `{‖f‖ ≤ c}`, i.e. the four degree-8 inequalities `‖f(z(s))‖ ≤ c` on `s ∈ [0,1]`.

Each is the sympy-verified SOS/Bernstein certificate (`chord_exits_sos_certificate.py`) transcribed:

```
‖f(z(s))‖ ≤ c  ⟸  normSq(f z) ≤ 125/16          (c² = 125/16, via 5^(3/2)=5√5)
               ⟸  Re(s)² + Im(s)²                (Complex.normSq_apply)
               ⟸  125/16 − (Re²+Im²) = (1/16)·SQ·P   (a `ring` identity)
```

with `SQ ∈ {s², (1−s)²}` a perfect square and `P` a degree-6 cofactor with **all-nonnegative Bernstein coefficients**, so the gap is a nonnegative ℚ-combination of `sʲ(1−s)^(8−j)`. `nlinarith` closes each segment from the uniform hint list `mul_nonneg (pow_nonneg hs0 j) (pow_nonneg h1s (8−j))`, `j = 0…8` (the same list covers both `SQ=s²` and `SQ=(1−s)²`).

The pattern was validated on a scratch file (segment 1) before transcribing all four.

## Build

```
docker-build.sh Proofs.Erdos1047OQ02Certificate
⚠ [3060/3060] Built Proofs.Erdos1047OQ02Certificate
Build completed successfully (3060 jobs).
```

0 `sorry`, 0 errors. Only cosmetic `linter.unusedSimpArgs` notes (the shared simp list leaves `neg_re`/`neg_im` unused on the non-negated segments). Registered in `Proofs.lean` after `Erdos1047OQ02`.

## Scope / honesty (axiom integrity)

- `Erdos1047OQ02Certificate.lean`: **verified, 0 sorry, 0 axiom**, registered.
- The parent `axiom goodman_counterexample` and its 4 transitive consumers (`grunskyConjecture_false`, `erdos_1047`, `erdos_1047_counterexample`, `erdos_1047_answer`) plus the registered `Erdos1047OQ02.lean` (which still references the axiom) are **unchanged**. The gallery `meta.json` `axiomCount` therefore stays **1** — honest.
- The **analytic risk is now zero**: flipping `axiomCount` 1→0 is a purely *mechanical* restructure (move the headline theorems + OQ02's usage downstream of the certificate and delete the parent `axiom` — the parent can't import the certificate, circular). author: gertl
body:
Description:

This PR enhances the Python extractor to accurately resolve method calls on typed parameters and local variables across module boundaries.

Changes:
**Two-pass extraction strategy:**

1. Pass 1 builds a global symbol index across all Python files, recording class definitions, inheritance relationships, and method signatures
2. Pass 2 uses this index to resolve types when extracting call edges

**Type resolution improvements:**

1. Adds type inference for function parameters with type annotations
2. Collects local variable types from assignments and annotated assignments within function bodies
3. Resolves variables to qualified type names via importMap and localTypes tracking

**Cross-file call resolution:**

1. When a method is called on a typed object (e.g., logger.write()), the extractor now emits edges to both the abstract/interface type and all concrete implementors
2. Prevents phantom edges for unresolvable receivers without type information

**Symbol index infrastructure:**

1. pySymbolIndex: Central registry tracking all classes and their methods across the project
2. implMap: Maps base class/interface names to their concrete implementors
3. Proper detection of abstract classes via ABC inheritance or @abstractmethod decorators

**Tests:**

1. Added comprehensive tests for typed parameter resolution
2. Added tests for constructor assignment type inference
3. Added tests for abstract class implementation tracking
4. Validates that phantom edges are not created for unresolvable types

 This enables more precise dependency graph construction for Python projects using type hints and object-oriented patterns.

author: ericreid
body:
Follow-up to #11 (already merged). Closes the one residual path behind issue #10.

## The remaining gap
After #11, restored converter **windows** self-close and resumed downloads that re-fire as `interrupted`/`complete` are skipped. But a download the browser *resumes as `in_progress`* on relaunch would still pass the guard, get intercepted, and open a freshly-created popup — matching the issue #10 report of a converter window appearing on browser launch for a `.3mf` the user never clicked.

## The fix
Add a `startTime` guard to `downloads.onCreated`:

```js
const startedAt = Date.parse(downloadItem.startTime || '');
if (!Number.isNaN(startedAt) && Date.now() - startedAt > 60000) return;
```

A user-initiated download fires `onCreated` with `startTime ≈ now`; a download the browser resumes/replays at launch carries its original (old) `startTime`. Skipping items older than 60s stops the popup-on-startup behavior regardless of the reported `state`. Falls through normally when `startTime` is missing/unparseable, so legitimate interception is unaffected.

## Notes
- For maintainer reassurance on the issue: the extension only `fetch`es URLs that surface as `.3mf` download events in the user's own browser profile (with their own cookies) — it has no access to other users' downloads.

author: ronaldmannak
body:
## What & why

Next iWork slice (OCR ✅ → Unicode ✅ → Pages ✅ → Pages real-file ✅ → **Keynote**). Adds first-class support for modern Apple **Keynote** presentations (iWork '13+), **reusing the exact in-module IWA decoder** built and validated for Pages — Snappy + protobuf-wire + `IWAArchive` — so **no Keynote.app, no Apple frameworks, and no new dependencies**.

A `.key` is the same ZIP/IWA container as `.pages`: slides live in `Index/Slide<N>.iwa` (loose, or inside a nested `Index.zip`), alongside `MasterSlide-*.iwa` masters and `Document.iwa` metadata.

## How it works

- **`KeynoteConverter`** — opens the `.key` ZIP, gathers the `.iwa` components, and emits **one section per slide** (`kind: .slide`, `slideNumber`) in slide-number order. Each slide's body text is extracted via the **same `kind == 0` TSWP-storage path** as Pages (`IWAArchive.text`). `MasterSlide*` template text is excluded; if no per-slide text is found, a fallback gathers body text from all non-master components into a single section.
- **Detection** — `.keynote` routed by extension (`.key`), UTType (`com.apple.iwork.keynote.key` / `.sffkey`), and MIME (`application/vnd.apple.keynote` + legacy `application/x-iwork-keynote-sffkey`), confirmed by the IWA layout — mirrors the Pages routing exactly. Registered at specific priority; both Keynote UTIs added to the supported types.

## Testing

Synthetic `.key` packages built from the **shared Pages IWA byte-builders** (no Keynote.app needed):
- per-slide sections in slide-number order,
- `MasterSlide*` exclusion,
- detection by extension and by MIME (extensionless download).

## Scope (v1) & follow-ups

v1 extracts **slide body text**. Speaker notes, per-slide *title vs body* structure, graph-based slide ordering, tables, and inline images are follow-ups — best validated against a **real `.key` fixture** (like the Pages real-file pass; the slide-text `kind` should be re-confirmed there, since v1 assumes the Pages-confirmed `kind == 0` body convention).

> [!NOTE]
> `readEntry` / `normalize` currently mirror `PagesConverter`; factoring a shared iWork helper is a planned cleanup once both converters settle. Kept self-contained here to keep this PR isolated from the just-merged Pages code.

author: eatnug
body:
## What

A running Thread's transcript collapsed to its last-finalized state mid-turn when it was re-hydrated (open / switch / reconnect / restore) — the "messages disappear while it runs" report. The agent process stays alive throughout; this was a view re-sourced from a cache that lags the live stream.

## Why

`content_delta` (live streaming) blocks are emitted to the renderer but deliberately NOT written into `thread.cachedBlocks` (the persisted Agent Session Cache stays finalized-only). `hydrateThread` returned `cachedBlocks` only, and the renderer's `thread.hydrated` handler REPLACES its blocks with the payload — so any re-hydrate during streaming dropped the in-flight content.

## Fix (two-layer model)

- New in-memory `ThreadRecord.streamingBlocks` (never persisted/snapshotted) holds the in-flight tail.
- `content_delta` mirrors each block into the tail via a `ThreadCrudService.recordStreamingBlock` delegate.
- `hydrateThread` returns `cachedBlocks ∪ streamingBlocks` (settled wins on blockId).
- `recordAgentSessionBlock` (finalize) evicts the blockId from the tail; `recordTurnComplete` clears it at settle.
- Renderer unchanged — the payload is now complete, so REPLACE is correct.

Affects **claude + codex** (the `content_delta` path). **ACP (gemini/opencode)** streams via repeated `content_record` straight into `cachedBlocks`, so it never had the bug and is untouched.

## Verification

- Deterministic drive of the real seam (live projector `ingestStructuredProviderEvent` → `hydrateThread`): mid-stream hydrate surfaces the in-flight block; finalize evicts it (one copy); settle clears the orphan tail.
- Code-confirmed delta↔record blockId match for claude and codex (eviction is exact).
- typecheck clean; 1057 backend/behavior tests pass (5 new: union / evict / clear / projector wiring). Live UI eyeball was inconclusive (harness selectors, not a collapse) and skipped to avoid disrupting a live session.

Spec: `docs_v2/specs/hydrate-live-streaming-tail.md`

author: daryn-brown
body:
## What & why

The recursive diagnostic from the last round pinned both live response shapes exactly:

- **Quotes** — `object{data:object{closes_error:string, results:array[30]}, guide:string}`. The 30 quote records live at `data.results` as a **positional array** with no per-record `symbol` field (plus a sibling `closes_error`), so the symbol-keyed parser found nothing → "no usable quotes."
- **Historicals** — `«too many symbols for get_equity_historicals (max …, got …); split your request into smaller batches»`. The single all-symbols call is rejected; it must be **chunked**.

## Changes (read-only, backend only)

- **`parse_quotes_positional`** — when records carry no usable symbol, zip them to the requested symbols in request order. Guarded two ways: only when `records.len() == symbols.len()` (no misaligned labeling), and only for records that actually carry a price (an unknown price key fails loud and surfaces the shape rather than labeling a blank value).
- **`fetch_historicals`** — requests in small batches (`HISTORICAL_BATCH = 5`) and merges the per-batch series, with a single de-duplicated diagnostic so a systemic failure doesn't flood the footer.
- **`enrich_positions`** now counts rows that *actually priced* (not merely matched), so "priced X/Y holdings" is accurate and a partial miss is reported honestly.
- **`shape_of`** recurses one more level (depth 3, keys/types/lengths only) so if anything still can't parse, the footer names the record's own fields.

## Safety

All 11 diagnostic sites re-audited: keys-only `shape_of`, digit-redacted `shape_preview`/`redact_nums`, or plain row counts — no value can leak. Positional zip relies on Robinhood returning `results` in request order (documented behavior) and is length-guarded. Tool selection stays gated to read-only tools.

## Tests

72 Rust unit tests pass (+2: positional zip succeeds on the `data.results` shape; refuses on a length mismatch).

author: rlaope
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes the desktop app's pre-backend binary discovery on macOS when Hermes is launched from Finder, Dock, Spotlight, or Login Items.

Those launch paths often start Electron with a very small `PATH` such as `/usr/bin:/bin`. The backend already expands that environment with Homebrew, Hermes-managed, and standard POSIX paths, but the early desktop resolver still searched only the original process `PATH`. As a result, the app could fail to find `hermes`, `python`, `git`, or shell binaries before the backend process was even spawned.

This PR makes desktop-side executable discovery use the same backend-aligned PATH policy that the backend receives.

## Related Issue

Fixes #48158

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests only

## Changes Made

- Added `apps/desktop/electron/desktop-path-resolver.cjs` for desktop executable lookup with the backend-aligned PATH.
- Exported the backend PATH-building helpers from `backend-env.cjs` so bootstrap discovery and backend launch share one policy.
- Updated `main.cjs` so `findOnPath()` resolves commands through the backend-aligned resolver instead of the raw GUI-launch PATH.
- Preserved Windows `PATHEXT` lookup behavior and the existing WSL binary guard.
- Added regression coverage for:
  - Homebrew paths being available before backend spawn.
  - Windows executable suffix lookup.
  - WSL binaries still being rejected.
  - The desktop resolver matching backend PATH policy intentionally.

## How to Test

```bash
node --test apps/desktop/electron/backend-env.test.cjs apps/desktop/electron/desktop-path-resolver.test.cjs
```

Result: `10/10` tests passed.

```bash
git diff --check
```

Result: passed.

## Checklist

- [x] Reproduces and fixes the reported macOS GUI-launch PATH drift.
- [x] Keeps backend PATH construction in one place.
- [x] Does not add a new dependency.
- [x] Adds regression tests for the affected resolver behavior.
- [x] Leaves labels for maintainers.

## Review Status

- Code review: comment addressed in `test: cover desktop resolver platform cases`.
- Architecture review: `WATCH`; addressed with an explicit resolver trust-boundary comment and policy regression test in `docs: clarify desktop resolver trust boundary`.

author: atlas-from-plumb
body:
## Problem

plumb already rewrites alias parameter names to canonical ones inside the daemon (`internal/mcp/argalias.go`), but the rewrite never ran for the most common case. A host that validates `tools/call` arguments against the advertised `inputSchema` **before transmitting** — Claude Code does, via a Zod schema — rejected an alias-bearing call before it reached the daemon:

```
MCP error -32602: Input validation error: Invalid arguments for tool search_in_files:
  [{ "code":"invalid_type", "expected":"string", "received":"undefined",
     "path":["pattern"], "message":"Required" }]
```

The `-32602`/Zod shape is the host (plumb is Go, can't emit it). The call never reached the daemon, so the alias layer was dead on arrival.

Confirmed empirically against the stats DB (`tool_calls.success/error_msg/input_json`): these were **host-side `required`-check rejections**, distinct from the server-side "did you mean" rejections that *did* reach the daemon. The host enforces `required` but not `additionalProperties`.

## Fix

**`publishSchema`** (new, `internal/mcp/argschema.go`), applied only at the `tools/list` publish seam: top-level and recursively through nested object / array-of-object schemas (`edits[]`, `operations[]`) it (1) drops every **alias-target** field (the union of the alias table's values) from `required`, and (2) relaxes `additionalProperties` to `true`. So a pre-validating host forwards the call.

Crucially, the **daemon keeps validating against the original strict schema** (`parseShape` unchanged): the full `required` set and the unknown-parameter "did you mean" message are still enforced server-side with plumb's good errors, and the alias rewrite still fires. Authoritative validation simply moves server-side — which is what `argguard` was built for. `publishSchema` is pure, **fail-open** (non-object/unparseable schema returned byte-for-byte), and precomputed once per tool at registration.

## Also: broader, evidence-driven alias table

Expanded `paramAliases` from the parameter names agents actually send (mined from the stats DB), each gated by the existing eligibility rule (applied only when the canonical is a real, unset parameter of *that* tool):

`pattern`↔`query` · `name`/`symbol`→`symbol_name`/`query` · `path`→`root` & `root`→`path` · `is_regex`→`use_regex` · `file_paths`→`paths` · `find`/`replace`→`pattern`/`replacement` · `file_pattern`→`glob` · `source`/`destination`→`from`/`to` · `workspace_path`→`workspace`

Deliberately excluded: semantic flips (`include`≠`exclude`, `apply`≠`dry_run`) and any safety-critical guess (no `git` subcommand/`confirm`/`files` inference).

## Plus: position-tool steering

`get_definition` and `find_references` carry the highest *genuine* failure rates in the stats DB (17–35%), almost all from bad hand-computed `line`/`character`. Their schema descriptions now mark the existing `symbol_name` path as PREFERRED and say why. With the new `symbol`/`name`→`symbol_name` aliases, `{uri, symbol: "Foo"}` resolves cleanly.

## Tests

`TestPublishSchema_*` (drops aliased required, keeps non-alias required, recurses into array items, fail-open, preserves property order), `TestAliasTargetSet_CoversCanonicals`, `TestResolveArgs_ExpandedAliases`. Full `make verify` green (build + all tests + lint).

## Verification still pending (needs a daemon restart — a shared singleton side-effect)

Unit/build/lint are green. The definitive end-to-end check — build, `plumb restart`, then call `search_in_files({query, path})` from a real host and confirm the `-32602` is gone and the alias notice appears — is intentionally **not** done here because restarting the shared daemon affects other live sessions.

## Deliberately deferred

Flat-edit auto-wrap for `edit_file`/`transaction_apply` (accept top-level `{old_string,new_string}` → `edits:[…]`). Safe but behaviour-changing, and the stats DB ranks it low (the dominant `edit_file` failures are stale-mtime / dirty-file / snippet-mismatch, not flat-form). Left as a follow-up.

author: fronzec
body:
## Summary

Uploaded plugin definitions stayed `PENDING` under every non-production profile (`local`, `dev`, `test`), so `POST /jobs/definitions/{id}/load` rejected them with HTTP 409 *"must be approved before loading"*. The documented local-run flow could not load plugins without an explicit approve call.

## Root cause

`AutoApproveConfig.approve()` only **mutates the entity in memory** (`setApprovalStatus("APPROVED")`). In `JarUploadService.uploadJar()`, `persistMetadata()` had already `save()`d the entity as `PENDING` and committed, and `uploadJar` is not `@Transactional`, so the in-memory approval was never flushed. The bean is active (`@Profile("!production")`) but its effect was silently lost.

## Fix

Re-save the entity after auto-approving:

```java
autoApproveConfig.ifPresent(
    ac -> {
      ac.approve(entity);
      jobDefinitionRepository.save(entity);
    });
```

### Why not `@Transactional` on `uploadJar`?

A method-level transaction would defer the initial INSERT to commit time, **outside** `persistMetadata`'s `try/catch`. That `catch` relies on `save()` throwing `DataIntegrityViolationException` **synchronously** to convert it into `DuplicateJobDefinitionException` — making the method transactional would break duplicate detection. It would also hold a DB connection across the upfront file I/O and signature verification. The targeted re-save is the minimal, side-effect-free fix; auto-approval only runs in non-production profiles.

## Test

`PluginManagementIntegrationTest.uploadUnderNonProductionProfile_persistsAutoApproval` uploads a JAR via MockMvc, then reads the definition back **from the database** and asserts `approvalStatus == APPROVED`. Verified red→green:

- Before the fix: `expected: "APPROVED" but was: "PENDING"`
- After the fix: 12/12 tests pass

A unit test with a mocked repository would not catch this (the `ArgumentCaptor` would hold the same reference `approve()` later mutates) — hence a behavior-first integration test against H2.

## Also (from a fresh-context review)

- Corrected `AutoApproveConfig` Javadoc: it said *"dev profile"* / *"atomically at persist time"*, now accurately *"non-production profiles"* and notes the caller re-saves.
- Added the missing `@Order(12)` to the new test to honor the class's `@TestMethodOrder` convention.

## Context

Companion to the local-run guide (PR #60, merged). The `load-plugins.sh` helper already approves explicitly, so the local flow works regardless; this fixes the underlying behavior so non-production uploads are auto-approved as intended.

author: alenkadev
body:
## Description

This PR fixes the auto-merge failure in the **Extract Source Translations Files** GitHub workflow.

### Root Cause

The workflow's merge step relies on the `REPO` environment variable when invoking GitHub CLI commands. In commit `6de8513c`, the workflow was refactored to move `COMMIT_COUNT` into a dedicated "compute commit count" step and add support for skipping timestamp-only changes. During that refactor, the following definition was inadvertently removed:

```bash
REPO="${{ github.repository }}"
```

As a result, subsequent GitHub CLI commands were executed without the repository context, causing the workflow to fail during the auto-merge step with errors such as:

```text
no pull requests found for branch "automated/extract-translation-source-files-..."
```

### Fix

Restore the `REPO="${{ github.repository }}"` definition so that GitHub CLI commands execute against the correct repository and can successfully locate and merge the generated pull request.

author: ml12580
body:
> [AI-assisted] Original contribution by @ml12580; maintainer rewrite and validation by @steipete.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw v2026.3.24 enabled Commander's positional-option mode. That made this previously shipped and documented invocation fail during lazy command reparse:

```text
openclaw browser tabs --browser-profile remote
error: unknown option '--browser-profile'
```

`--browser-profile` belongs to the `browser` parent, but the second parse happens only after `tabs` has replaced its lazy placeholder. Positional mode then treats the trailing flag as a `tabs` option. This is Regression 1 of #55563 and breaks existing WSL2/remote-CDP troubleshooting commands. Regression 2 in that issue (`doctor --fix` gateway cycling) is separate and intentionally untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

The contributor patch established the right normalization point. I rewrote it around one invariant: after the real lazy subtree loads, restore parent-option placement only when the selected child path does not own the same flag.

The final parser:

- walks the real Commander hierarchy and consumes ancestor option values, so command-looking values do not confuse path selection;
- moves only options owned by the lazy parent;
- preserves collisions on the selected child, including `browser extension pair --json` and cookie `--url`;
- ignores collisions that exist only on an unselected sibling;
- preserves aliases, option values, missing required values, and the `--` terminator.

Simply disabling positional options on `browser` was rejected: Commander 15 would make the parent steal colliding leaf flags. That would fix the reported command by breaking currently valid child behavior.

## User Impact

Both supported orderings work again:

```text
openclaw browser --browser-profile remote tabs
openclaw browser tabs --browser-profile remote
```

The same repair applies to nested lazy commands such as `browser tab new --browser-profile remote`. Existing child-option ownership remains unchanged. No config, protocol, auth, network, or migration surface changes.

## Evidence

Dependency contract checked directly against Commander 15.0.0 source and types: positional parent options after a subcommand are intentionally disabled, and disabling positional mode would restore parent capture at the cost of child collisions.

Blacksmith Testbox provider/id: `blacksmith-testbox` / `tbx_01kwxpxmb3x1g1prnaa9cs4230`.

- `pnpm test src/cli/program/action-reparse.test.ts src/cli/program/register.subclis.test.ts` — 32 passed.
- `pnpm test extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli.lazy.test.ts extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-extension.test.ts extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-state.option-collisions.test.ts` — 26 passed.

- Black-box built-CLI contract — 7/7 clauses passed: both parent-option orders were observably identical; nested order worked; selected-child collision, sibling collision, terminator, and missing-value behavior were preserved.

### Motivation

- Break the large, single-file `app.js` into focused, testable modules so the app can be loaded as a small set of browser scripts and to make incremental refactors safer. 
- Preserve local-first behavior, keep public APIs and runtime behavior stable for the app and the Node-based tests.

### Description

- Replaced the big `app.js` implementation with a compatibility shim and moved all application logic into `src/` modules, including `src/app-state.js`, `src/bootstrap.js`, `src/main.js`, `src/core/*`, `src/ui/*`, and `src/features/*`. 
- Added `src/core/parser-core.js` as a UMD-style core parsing utility and a Node-compatible shim so tests can `require` the parser core; updated `src/parser-core.js` to re-export the core for backwards compatibility. 
- Introduced `src/main.js` as the modular entry point which sequentially loads the Phase 1 script list in order, and updated `index.html` to load `src/main.js` instead of the old `app.js`.

💡 What: An invisible `aria-live` region has been added to the redirect page's countdown logic to effectively announce timer updates to screen readers. The text format has also been updated to handle singular/plural grammar correctly ("second" vs "seconds").
🎯 Why: Screen readers often struggle to announce rapidly updating countdown timers if the `aria-live` attribute is placed directly on the visual text or if it isn't configured properly. By adding a dedicated, invisible announcer with `aria-live="polite"`, we ensure users with visual impairments are informed of the impending redirect without being overwhelmed. The grammar fix adds an extra touch of visual and functional polish.
♿ Accessibility: Ensures WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value) compliance for the dynamic countdown widget.

author: koic
body:
## Motivation and Context

SEP-2106 (modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol#2106, merged for the 2026-07-28 spec release) makes tool `inputSchema` and `outputSchema` conform to the full JSON Schema 2020-12 vocabulary: an input schema keeps `type: "object"` at the root but may use any 2020-12 keyword below it; an output schema may be ANY valid schema (object, array, primitive, or a root-level composition); and `CallToolResult.structuredContent` widens from an object to any JSON value. The SEP also adds resource bounds: `$ref` resolution is restricted (same-document only in the reference implementation) and composition-heavy documents must be bounded to avoid excessive validation cost.

This follows the TypeScript SDK's reference implementation (typescript-sdk#2249; the Python SDK tracks the same work in python-sdk#2792):

- `Tool::Schema` now validates against the JSON Schema 2020-12 metaschema rather than the draft-04 metaschema. The draft-04 pin was a stopgap from when the SDK used the `json-schema` gem, which did not support 2020-12; `json_schemer` does, so `$defs`/`$ref` and the rest of the 2020-12 vocabulary now resolve natively. This matches the dialect the SDK already advertises in emitted schemas and the Python SDK's behavior, whose `jsonschema.validate` selects the validator from the schema's `$schema`.
- `Tool::Schema` moves root-type defaulting into an overridable `apply_default_root_type!` hook. `InputSchema` keeps the historical `type: "object"` default; `OutputSchema` now applies it only when no root schema keyword (`type`, `$ref`, `oneOf`, `anyOf`, `allOf`, `not`, `if`, `const`, `enum`) is present. The previous unconditional default merged `type: "object"` into root combinators such as `{ oneOf: [...] }`, producing a wrong schema, so that case is a bug fix.
- `Tool::Schema` enforces the TypeScript SDK's schema bounds at construction time: only same-document `$ref`/`$dynamicRef`s (starting with `#`, so schema handling can never trigger network or file access), `MAX_SCHEMA_DEPTH = 64` nesting levels, and `MAX_SUBSCHEMA_COUNT = 10_000` subschema objects, all raising `ArgumentError` on violation.
- `Server#call_tool` mirrors non-object `structuredContent` into `content` as serialized JSON text when the tool provided no content blocks, so pre-SEP clients that only read `content` still receive the data. Object results and explicit content are untouched.

Resolves #377.

## How Has This Been Tested?

- `test/mcp/tool/output_schema_test.rb`: root-level `oneOf`, `$ref`+`$defs`, primitive, and `enum` schemas serialize without an injected `type` and validate results correctly; the `properties`-only shorthand still serializes with `type: "object"` (wire-format regression); explicit `type: "array"` keeps working.
- `test/mcp/tool/input_schema_test.rb`: an input schema using `$defs`, `$ref`, `oneOf`, `if`/`then`, and `allOf` keeps its object root and round-trips all keywords; a draft-04-only boolean `exclusiveMinimum` is rejected under the 2020-12 dialect while the numeric form is accepted.
- `test/mcp/tool/schema_test.rb`: depth and subschema-count bound violations raise `ArgumentError`; non-same-document `$ref`s (remote URI, sibling file) are rejected while `#/$defs/...` is accepted. The previous unbounded-depth caching test is replaced, since the depth bound now rejects such documents by design.
- `test/mcp/server_test.rb`: `tools/call` with array `structuredContent` and no content gains the serialized TextContent fallback; explicit content is not overwritten; object `structuredContent` gets no fallback.

`bundle exec rake` (tests, RuboCop, and conformance baseline, including the `json-schema-2020-12` server scenario) passes.

## Breaking Changes

Three narrow behavior changes, all intentional per the SEP:

- Runtime validation now uses the JSON Schema 2020-12 metaschema instead of draft-04. Schemas that rely on draft-04-only syntax are rejected at construction time. The practical case is the boolean `exclusiveMinimum`/`exclusiveMaximum` form (deprecated since draft-06), which must now be the numeric form; the Python SDK rejects it the same way. Other draft-04 spellings (`definitions`, `id`, `dependencies`) still validate, since 2020-12 tolerates unknown keywords.
- Schemas that exceed the new resource bounds (nesting deeper than 64, more than 10,000 subschema objects) or use a non-same-document `$ref`/`$dynamicRef` now raise `ArgumentError` at construction time. Previously such documents were accepted (external references were already never fetched, only ignored).
- An `OutputSchema` whose root declares a schema keyword other than `type` (e.g. `oneOf`) no longer has  `type: "object"` merged into it. The old output was an invalid hybrid schema, so no conforming consumer could have relied on it.

## Types of changes
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply: -->
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [x] Documentation update

## Checklist
<!-- Go over all the following points, and put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
- [x] I have read the [MCP Documentation](https://modelcontextprotocol.io)
- [x] My code follows the repository's style guidelines
- [x] New and existing tests pass locally
- [x] I have added appropriate error handling
- [x] I have added or updated documentation as needed

## Summary

Implements the four Subsonic "sharing" API methods — `getShares`, `createShare`, `updateShare`, and `deleteShare` — converting the prior HTTP‑501 "Not Implemented" stubs into working, authenticated endpoints. Subsonic‑compatible clients can now create public, shareable links to albums and playlists and manage those shares, with the public links served by Navidrome's pre‑existing unauthenticated `/p/{id}` route.

The feature layers a thin Subsonic protocol surface on top of Navidrome's existing share infrastructure (`model.Share`, `core.Share`, the persistence repository, and the public delivery handler), which already provided nanoid generation, the 365‑day default expiry, and content resolution.

## Scope of Changes (9 files, +526 / −6)

**New files**
- `server/subsonic/sharing.go` (361 lines) — `GetShares`, `CreateShare`, `UpdateShare`, `DeleteShare` on `*Router`, plus helpers `authorizeShareAccess` (IDOR protection), side‑effect‑free `resolveShareTracks`, and `buildShare`.
- `tests/mock_playlist_repo.go` (130 lines) — `MockPlaylistRepo` satisfying the full `model.PlaylistRepository` interface (compile‑time assertion included).

**Modified files**
- `server/subsonic/responses/responses.go` — exported `Share` and `Shares` DTOs + `Shares *Shares` `omitempty` envelope field.
- `server/public/public_endpoints.go` — exported `ShareURL(r *http.Request, id string) string`.
- `server/subsonic/api.go` — removed the four method names from `h501`, registered real handlers, added the `core.Share` dependency (idiomatic DI).
- `cmd/wire_gen.go` — threaded `core.NewShare(dataStore)` into `subsonic.New(...)`.
- 3 existing Subsonic test files — propagated the new `New()` trailing argument.

## Validation

- `make build` → exit 0 (only a pre‑existing, out‑of‑scope C++ TagLib deprecation warning).
- In‑scope tests (race detector): `server/subsonic` 45/45, `server/subsonic/responses` 78/78 (golden snapshots byte‑identical), `server/public` 4/4; full module 31 packages OK, 0 failures, zero data races.
- `make lint` → clean (golangci‑lint v1.50.1; zero findings on in‑scope packages).
- Live end‑to‑end: all four endpoints return HTTP 200; `createShare` yields a 10‑char nanoid id, a public `/p/{id}` URL, owner, and a +365‑day default expiry; missing `id` returns `ErrorMissingParameter` (code 10); XML and JSON both Subsonic‑v1.16.1‑compliant.

## Scope Compliance

No protected files modified (`go.mod`, `go.sum`, `Makefile`, CI config, i18n, `model/share.go`, `core/share.go`, persistence, `ui/**`, `db/migration/**`). No new tests added to existing files; no golden snapshots regenerated.

## Remaining Before Production (~17h, human)

Dedicated handler test suite + golden snapshot, security sign‑off of the authorization/IDOR and unauthenticated‑exposure logic, real Subsonic‑client interop testing, operational enablement of `DevEnableShare`, and a final CI run + code review + merge.

Implements a template-based narrative engine that drives all dynamic UI copy across the dashboard — hero text, sidebar stats, wrapped slides, section labels, streak commentary, and more.

- **441 templates** across 84 narrative keys, covering streaks of 0, 1–2, 3–5, 6–10, and 11+ days plus always-true fallbacks
- Daily UTC seed for stable randomization (same text throughout the day); manual rotation available from Settings
- Specificity-first selection: conditional templates win over `always_true` fallbacks
- **XSS-safe**: no `{@html}` anywhere — `NarrativeText.svelte` splits on `[[...]]` delimiters and renders accent spans as plain text nodes
- **plain/rich API split**: `GET /api/narrative` returns `{ plain: Record<string, string>, rich: Record<string, string> }` — TypeScript consumers must explicitly choose which bucket, making accidental misuse of `NarrativeText` for non-accent keys visible at the call site
- `[[...]]` delimiter (replacing `*`) allows literal asterisks in prose without ambiguity
- All HTML entities in templates replaced with Unicode literals

### Playing-now cover art (bundled fix)

Moved all cover art HTTP work (LB MBID enrichment + CAA Tier 1/2/3) out of the `/api/playing-now` request path into fire-and-forget `asyncio` tasks. Cache miss now returns `null` art immediately (~300ms) and populates the cache for the next poll. Increased `_MAX_ART_ATTEMPTS` from 1→3 so transient LB timeouts no longer permanently suppress art for a session.

https://liferay.atlassian.net/browse/LPD-95233

## What Is Being Fixed

The product menu (site administration side navigation) close button was always
visible. Per the accessibility design gated behind feature flag LPD-57922, the
close button should be visually hidden and surface only when reached via the
keyboard, so it stays operable for keyboard and screen-reader users without
adding visual clutter for everyone else.

## How It Is Being Fixed

The change is layered across Clay and its consumers. First, the clay-core
`SidePanel.Header` gains a `closeButtonProps` pass-through so a consumer can
apply HTML attributes — such as a `className` — to the rendered close button.
Second, clay-css adds a close "sr-only-focusable" utility: the `clay-close`
mixin now emits quoted custom selectors through `clay-map-to-css`, and the
standard, cadmin, and atlas-custom-properties variable sets define a
`&.sr-only-focusable:focus` rule that repositions and sizes the button when it
receives focus. Finally, the consumers gate the `sr-only sr-only-focusable`
classes behind `FeatureFlags['LPD-57922']`: the React `SideNavigation` passes
them via `closeButtonProps`, and the site administration header JSPF appends
them to the `clay:button` `cssClass`.

## Why Are There No Tests?

The changes are presentational clay-css utilities, a clay prop pass-through, and
feature-flag gating of a CSS class — behavior that is not meaningfully
unit-testable and is covered by the existing clay component tests.

Now that did:atp v2 is on `main` (#67), this migrates the downstream verifiers toward v2 with a **backward-compatible verification shim** so legacy Ed25519 signatures keep working throughout the rollout while v2 post-quantum (ML-DSA-65) signatures verify as signers adopt hybrid keys. ## The shim — `@atp/shared` `verifySignatureCompat()` `packages/shared/src/crypto/verify-compat.ts`: verifies a hex signature over a UTF-8 message against whatever key material is available, **auto-selecting the algorithm by signature size**: - 64-byte → **Ed25519** (legacy / classical) - 3309-byte → **ML-DSA-65** (v2, FIPS 204) - inconclusive → tries every supplied key (post-quantum first) Returns `{ valid, algorithm }`. Reuses existing `@noble` primitives — Ed25519 mirrors `crypto/pqc-crypto.ts`, ML-DSA-65 mirrors `security/quantum-safe.ts` (arg order verified correct for `@noble/post-quantum` 0.6.x). **No new cryptography.** ## Verifiers wired through it All preserve current Ed25519 behavior and become v2-capable when a post-quantum key is supplied: | File | Change | |---|---| | `rpc-gateway/src/services/auth.ts` | `verifySignature` → shim; optional `mlDsa65PublicKeyHex` param | | `vc-service/src/services/credential.ts` | `verifySignature` (Ed25519Signature2020 proofs) → shim | | `identity-service/src/utils/crypto.ts` | new `verifyCompat()`; legacy `verify()` left untouched | ## Tests & gate - 10 new shim tests (Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 roundtrip, tamper, wrong key, both-keys selection, malformed input) - Full gate green locally: **770/770** unit tests, lint clean, `tsc --noEmit` clean ## Deferred (with reason) `src/app/api/crypto/verify-signature/route.ts` still uses a placeholder length check. The new `verifySignatureCompat()` function in `@atp/shared` auto-detects signature algorithms by byte length (64 bytes for legacy Ed25519, 3309 bytes for post-quantum ML-DSA-65) and verifies against available key material. Three downstream services (RPC gateway auth, VC service credential verification, and identity service crypto utils) are wired through this compatibility shim, allowing them to handle both legacy Ed25519 signatures and new ML-DSA-65 signatures during the rollout period without breaking existing functionality. ⏱️ Estimated Review Time: 30-90 minutes

The underlying noble crypto calls and argument orders are correct against `@noble/post-quantum` 0.6.x, and the 10 new shim tests cover happy paths, tamper detection, wrong-key rejection, cross-algorithm key-mismatch, and malformed input. - `packages/shared/src/crypto/verify-compat.ts`: new shim with brute-force fallback when signature length is inconclusive or the matching key is missing; all crypto primitives reuse existing `@noble` patterns. - `rpc-gateway/src/services/auth.ts` and `vc-service/src/services/credential.ts`: call sites thread through the shim but do not yet supply `mlDsa65PublicKeyHex`, making the post-quantum path unreachable until key extraction from DID Documents is updated in a follow-up. - `packages/identity-service/src/utils/crypto.ts`: adds `verifyCompat()` as a thin boolean wrapper; legacy `verify()` is preserved unchanged.

body:
Fix bash arithmetic injection vulnerability via input sanitization

Harden bash script against command injection while preserving exact expected byte-parity between Bash and PowerShell ports. Rather than exiting early on non-integer input to arithmetic `((...))` or `$((...))` contexts, variables are validated with a new `is_int` helper and sanitized to `0` prior to arithmetic evaluation. This prevents injection vectors and unbound-variable errors, maintaining byte-identical output to original codebase rendering for non-integers. PowerShell implementation handles fallback-to-0 equivalently using `TryParse` with careful bounds. All temporary/scratch scripts have been fully removed.

author: ghbvf
body:
## Summary

强制 ABAC `EffectAllow` 规则声明非空 `Action`，闭合「空 Action + 空 Conditions 的 allow 规则可对任意 action/subject 无条件 permit、放空整层路由门禁」的漏洞（#1979）。

## Why / 背景

`evaluator.go` 的 `applyRule` 把 `len(rule.Action)==0` 当作「untargeted = 通配全部 action」，叠加 `matchAllConditions([])` 恒真——一条 `{effect:allow, action:[], conditions:[]}` 的租户 policy 即对**任意 action、任意 subject** 无条件 permit，一条误配/恶意规则即可放空所有 permission 的**路由门禁**。

数据访问不受影响（行可见性由 principal 派生的 `RowScope` 独立治理），但路由门禁是数据边界之上的纵深防御外层，不该被一条空规则放空。

**探索期关键发现**：HTTP 契约 `rule.schema.json` 此前 `additionalProperties:false` 且**根本没有 `action` 字段**，converter 也从不映射 Action——即租户经 API 创建的每条 allow 规则都必然空 Action = 通配全部。所以「强制非空 Action」**必须同 PR 给契约补 `action`**，否则租户再也建不了任何 allow 规则。

### 方案：Direction X + 三层 Medium enforcement（强度天花板自审）

本不变式 = 运行时谓词 `len(Action) > 0`，Go 编译期不可表达 → 真 Hard（不可表达）对动态 surface 范畴上不可达；sealed constructor 买不到 Hard（仍是 runtime funnel）却要付 `Rule` 跨包 unexport + accessor 大成本，故**不做重构**。按 surface 打满各自天花板：

| Surface | 性质 | 载体 | 行为 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 租户规则（运行时输入） | 动态谓词 | `abac.Rule.Validate` 写侧 fail-closed | empty-Action allow → `KindInvalid`/422 |
| 漏网/旧持久化规则 | 运行时 | evaluator `applyRule` 读侧 fail-closed | empty-Action allow 视为不适用、永不放行 |
| baseline（静态 Go 值集） | 编译期已知 | archtest `BASELINE-ALLOW-ACTION-NONEMPTY-01`（value-level 同包冻结 + anti-vacuity + RED case） | 每条 baseline allow 必带非空 Action |

空 Action 仅 `EffectDeny` 合法（deny-all，forbid-wins 覆盖全部 action，不变）。对标 XACML 3.0 §5.9 Rule target / AWS Cedar permit-scope（permit 必带 action scope）。

## Refs

Closes #1979 · ADR amendment `docs/architecture/202606121400-1348-adr-pr10a-authz-wiring.md` §"Amendment: #1979"

### 契约扇出矩阵

| 变更 | contract | generated | cell/slice | tests | docs |
|------|----------|-----------|------------|-------|------|
| allow 必带 Action + wire 承载 Action | `shared/v1/rule.schema.json` +`action`（optional，结构真相单源在域层 Validate，沿用 #1977） | `create/update/get/list` `types_gen.go` + TS 重生成（`RequestRulesItem`/`ResponseData*RulesItem.Action`） | `abac.Rule.Validate` / `evaluator.applyRule` / `policymanage.converter`（双向映射） | rule/policy/converter/service/handler/errmap/evaluator/conformance + 新 archtest | `tenancy.md §ABAC` + PR-10a ADR amendment |

PG `policy_codec` 早已 round-trip `Action`（PR-10a #1348），无需 migration / backfill。

## Risk / 兼容性

- **wire 破坏式变更**（pre-GA 窗口允许原地改 active 版本，#api-versioning）：`action` 为新增 optional 字段，对 deny 规则向后兼容；对 allow 规则收紧（必带 action）。全部 in-repo 调用方随本 PR 原子更新。
- **legacy 空-Action allow 行**：读侧 fail-closed（永不放行），无需数据 backfill——这些行正是漏洞本身，停止放行即修复。
- 威胁矩阵已在 ADR amendment 重评：全通配 allow / condition-only blanket allow 向量均闭合；owner→tenant widen 与 cross-tenant 由既有冻结/e2e 覆盖，不受影响。

## Test plan

- [x] `make check-build`（全 32 个 go.work 模块编译通过）
- [x] `make test`（全 32 个模块单测通过，非 integration）
- [x] `go vet -tags=integration` / `-tags=e2e`（corecells / adapters/postgres / tests / cmd/corebundle 编译通过）
- [x] 新增 TDD：rule.Validate empty-action-allow 拒绝（RED→GREEN）、deny-all 仍合法、evaluator empty-action allow inert、converter Action 往返、service 422、baseline archtest
- [x] codegen 确定性（重跑 `generate contract/shared-schema` 无 drift）
- [x] `golangci-lint run` 改动包 0 issues
- [x] `gocell validate` 0 errors

body:
Closes #228

## Summary
Automated implementation of [Cache review verdict by diff-hash + delta-only pre-merge re-review to stop redundant non-deterministic re-reviews](https://github.com/accidental-hedge-fund/agent-pipeline/issues/228).

**Implemented by**: claude
**Plan reviewed by**: codex
**OpenSpec change**: `cache-review-verdict-by-diff-hash`

## Proposal
## Why

The adversarial reviewer is non-deterministic: re-reviewing an identical diff produces different findings each pass. Two pipeline paths invoke the reviewer redundantly on already-evaluated code — override re-entry and ceiling resume re-run review on a frozen diff, minting fresh finding keys that invalidate previously-applied overrides so convergence is impossible; and the pre-merge SHA gate routes back to a full adversarial round whenever any fix commit lands, burning round budget toward the ceiling on code the reviewer already approved.

## What Changes

- Embed a `<!-- verdict-diff-hash: <hash> -->` sentinel in every review comment, keying the verdict to a hash of the PR diff content at review time.
- On re-entering a review stage, compute the current PR diff hash. If it matches the sentinel in the prior review-N comment, return the cached verdict without invoking the reviewer.
- Extend `enforceReviewShaGate` in the pre-merge stage with a diff-hash check: a SHA mismatch where the full diff hash is unchanged reuses the prior verdict (no re-review needed); a mismatch where the diff changed triggers a focused delta review (adversarial review of `last-reviewed-sha...HEAD` only) rather than routing back to a full review-2 round.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `verdict-diff-cache`: Review verdicts are cached per review round keyed by a hash of the PR diff content; re-entering a review stage on an unchanged diff returns the cached verdict without invoking the reviewer.
- `pre-merge-delta-recheck`: When the pre-merge SHA gate detects HEAD moved with non-archive commits, it checks the diff-hash cache first; on a cache hit the verdict is reused; on a miss the unreviewed delta (`last-reviewed-sha...HEAD`) is reviewed adversarially rather than routing back to a full review-2 round.

author: xl-openai
body:
## Why

Plugin-install preflight and the actual OAuth login flow used different discovery implementations. Preflight had a Codex-specific implementation that only queried authorization-server metadata on the MCP host, while login already used the upstream `rmcp` Rust MCP SDK. As a result, servers that advertise a separate authorization server through RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata were classified as OAuth-unsupported during plugin installation, so login was skipped.

## What changed

- delegate plugin-install OAuth discovery to `rmcp::transport::AuthorizationManager`, the same implementation used by the login flow
- let `rmcp` follow Protected Resource Metadata first and perform direct RFC 8414 authorization-server discovery when protected-resource discovery does not yield usable metadata
- retain Codex's existing HTTP headers, timeout, `no_proxy` behavior, and scope normalization around that discovery
- add unit coverage and a pure-MCP plugin-install integration test that proves the protected-resource path reaches OAuth client registration

This only changes shared MCP OAuth discovery. App declarations and `appsNeedingAuth` behavior are unchanged.

## Verification

- `just test -p codex-rmcp-client auth_status`
- `just test -p codex-app-server plugin_install_starts_mcp_oauth`
- real plugin-install smoke test with an isolated `CODEX_HOME`: both DigitalOcean MCP servers started OAuth callback listeners, while Linear continued to start its existing direct-discovery OAuth flow

## Problem (live)
Background `auto` pipes were hard-failing with `400 Invalid tool_calls[0].id: string too long` — Sentry `model=gpt-5.4, error_path=auto_fatal`, **~600/day**. gpt-5.4 (OpenAI) rejects long tool_call IDs that glm-5/Gemini accept, but `runChain` **broke the loop on any non-transient error**, so it never fell back to the working model one line down. Users saw a misleading "may not be enabled on your account" message.

Regression from #4285 (background→gpt-5.4); before, background headed on gemini-flex/glm-5 which accept those IDs.

## Fix
- `runChain` now tries **every** chain entry and only fails when exhausted — a chain exists to fall back. The `transient` flag still gates Sentry noise, not cascade.
- Reworded the 400/404 `friendlyError` to name the real likely cause (unsupported param / malformed tool call) instead of blaming account access.

## Verified
446 tests pass. Deployed to prod (`9445eb19`); interactive (glm-5) + background (gpt-5.4) both healthy post-deploy.

author: junixdev
body:
## What

The 387s hang was sustained by ~9 threads all running git2 working-tree diffs at once, all blocked acquiring libiconv's single global rwlock (libgit2 opens/closes a converter per directory for Unicode path normalization). With 40-50 repos, one `repos-changed` burst refreshed every repo's status simultaneously and the writes serialized into a lock convoy.

## Changes

- Add a git-status `Semaphore` (`GIT_STATUS_CONCURRENCY = 4`) to `AppState`.
- `repo_statuses` and `git_worktree_status` acquire a permit and run the git2 work in `spawn_blocking`, capping concurrent scans.
- Coalesce `repos-changed` bursts in `useGitWatch` (250ms) so one FSEvents storm triggers one invalidation round instead of dozens of refetches.

## Verification

`cargo check` + `tsc` pass.

## Note

Overlaps #88 (both make `git_worktree_status` async). Merge #88 first, then rebase this — the remaining diff is the semaphore plumbing + permit acquisition.

Closes #89

- New request fields: `steering_vectors` / `prefill_steering_vectors` / `decode_steering_vectors` (packed base64 wire format matching the Python OpenAI API), `steering_name`.
- Packed format (`dtype`/`shape`/`layer_indices`/`data`/`scales`) decoded into the inline `SteeringVectorSpec` engine-core resolves (`float32`/`float16`/`bfloat16`/`float64`, per-row scales). Layer keys serialize as integer msgpack keys (Python `dict[int, ...]`). `steering_name` lowers to `steering_module_ref = (name, 1.0)`.

### Named steering modules
- `--steering-modules name=path` loads module JSON at startup and broadcasts to the engine workers (`register_steering_modules` + `pre_materialize_steering_module`).
- Runtime endpoints re-broadcast on change: `GET` / `POST` / `DELETE /v1/steering/modules`. Per-request `steering_name` validated up front (unknown → `invalid_request` / `NotFound`); mutations serialized by a lock.

### Activation capture (end-to-end)
- Request side: `capture` spec accepted on HTTP + gRPC, forwarded verbatim into `SamplingParams.capture`; engine-core's offline admission resolves prefix-cache flags.
- **Output side (the key fix):** Python's `EngineCoreOutput` is an `array_like` tuple with `capture_results` at index 7; the Rust `EngineCoreOutput` predated that field, so capture-enabled outputs misaligned/failed to decode. Added a `CaptureResult` type and inserted `capture_results` at the correct tuple index, threaded it (alongside `kv_transfer_params`) through `llm` → `text` → `chat`, and surfaced it on the non-streaming completion/chat responses and the gRPC `FinishInfo` — coercing each consumer payload to an object (mirror of Python's `_capture_result_to_response_payload`). Streaming responses omit `capture_results`, matching Python (capture still executes; consumers write out of band).
- The `python_compat.py` fixture mirror was updated to include `capture_results`, keeping the Rust↔Python wire-format test faithful; a new wire test pins the index-7 position.

### Frontend tokenizer override (`--tokenizer`)
- New `--tokenizer <path>` flag on `serve` / `frontend` overrides **only** the frontend's backend-file resolution source (`LoadModelBackendsOptions.tokenizer` → `ResolvedModelFiles::new`); `--model` stays the public id and the engine model. Defaults to `--model` when unset.
- Motivation: a `.gguf` has no `tokenizer.json`, and the Rust `tokenizers` crate can't extract the embedded ggml tokenizer (the Python engine reads it from GGUF metadata). The flag lets the frontend tokenizer point at a directory that has one while the engine loads the original model.
- Removed the now-implemented `tokenizer` field from the recognized-but-unsupported engine passthrough args (it was a no-op placeholder and clashed with the real flag).

## Why

The Rust frontend replaces vLLM's Python OpenAI entrypoint; these are the steering/capture surfaces clients rely on. Per-request resolution/admission stays in the engine-core; the frontend decodes the wire format, forwards, manages the named-module registry, and surfaces capture results.

## Validation

Workspace lib tests green, clippy + fmt clean.

End-to-end on **gemma4-31B GGUF** through the Rust HTTP API (engine loads the GGUF; frontend tokenizer via `--tokenizer` pointed at a gemma tokenizer dir):
- **Plain:** `"The capital of France is"` → `" Paris."`.
- **Steering:** zero-vector control reproduces the baseline output; any non-zero packed vector drastically changes generation (decoded → forwarded → applied at the kernel).
- **Capture:** the `filesystem` consumer wrote real activations (`post_mlp` layers 0/30, shape `[1, 5376]` bf16) with correct metadata.

## Notes / deferred
- Capture-spec validation parity: the Python entrypoint's synchronous `_admit_capture` spec validation is deferred to the engine-core here, so a malformed capture spec surfaces as an engine error rather than a `400` up front. Concretely, the frontend forwards the `capture` dict verbatim and does not run `resolve_capture_prefix_flags`, so the `filesystem` consumer currently requires the client to include `request_id` and `tag` in the per-consumer spec.
- Pre-existing, unrelated: completions `logprobs` returns a 500 and poisons the request stream — tracked in RhizoNymph/vllm#189.

See `rust/docs/features/steering_capture.md` for the full data flow (incl. the capture return path), file map, and invariants.

author: key4ng
body:
## Description

### Problem

The nightly BFCL A/B (`scripts/bfcl/`) — the parser-parity comparison of pure vLLM vs SMG→vLLM gRPC — only exercised a single model (`Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B`) on one `4-gpu-h100` node. We want coverage of the mid-2026 target SKUs (Kimi K2.6, DeepSeek V4, MiniMax M2.7, gpt-oss-120b) and the ability to run the large models on Blackwell (B300) hardware.

### Solution

Convert the single A/B job into a **5-model matrix**, each leg on its own runner with its own parser config. Because the A/B isolates the *parser frontend* (model size is irrelevant — a smaller same-family checkpoint exercises the identical parse path), the large legs use flash/int4 checkpoints that fit half a B300 node at TP=4, so every leg runs both arms concurrently with no perf tuning. gpt-oss needs no SMG tool-call-parser — SMG's `HarmonyDetector` auto-routes it through the harmony pipeline — so `launch_arm.sh` now omits the flag when unset.

| leg | runner | TP/arm | vLLM tool/reason | SMG tool/reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| qwen3.6 | `4-gpu-h100` | 2 | `qwen3_xml`/`qwen3` | `qwen_xml`/`qwen3` |
| gpt-oss | `4-gpu-h100` | 2 | `openai`/— | _(none → harmony auto)_/— |
| deepseek-v4 (Flash) | `blackwell` | 4 | `deepseek_v4`/`deepseek_v4` | `deepseek_v4`/`deepseek_v31`† |
| minimax-m2.7 | `blackwell` | 4 | `minimax_m2`/`minimax_m2` | `minimax_m2`/`minimax` |
| kimi-k2.6 (int4) | `blackwell` | 4 | `kimi_k2`/`kimi_k2` | `kimik2`/`kimi_k25`† |

## Changes

- `scripts/bfcl/launch_arm.sh`: make the SMG arm's `--tool-call-parser` conditional (omit when `BFCL_SMG_TOOL_PARSER` is empty → gpt-oss harmony auto-detect).
- `.github/workflows/nightly-bfcl.yml`: convert `bfcl-ab` to a 5-leg matrix on per-model runners (`4-gpu-h100`, `blackwell`); leg filtering (dispatch `only`, PR-runs-H100-only) lives in a new `setup` job that emits the matrix as JSON, since the `matrix` context isn't allowed in a job-level `if`.
- `scripts/bfcl/README.md`: per-model parser table + matrix/runner docs.
- `run_ab.py` is unchanged — it already loops over both arms.

**† To confirm on the first nightly:** SMG has no exact `deepseek_v4`/`kimi_k2` *reasoning* parser yet (using closest `deepseek_v31`/`kimi_k25`, marked `TODO(confirm)`); the new model IDs and the int4 Kimi invocation should be verified against the installed vLLM build.

## Test Plan

- `shellcheck scripts/bfcl/launch_arm.sh` passes; behavioral check confirms the SMG tool-call-parser is omitted when empty and included when set.
- `actionlint .github/workflows/nightly-bfcl.yml` clean (only pre-existing custom-runner-label warnings); matrix parses to the 5 expected legs; `setup` filter logic verified for schedule / PR / dispatch-`only` / unknown-leg (guarded) cases.
- PR trigger runs the quick non-live subset on the `4-gpu-h100` legs only as an end-to-end pipeline sanity check; full validation is the scheduled nightly on real runners.

<details>
<summary>Checklist</summary>

- [ ] `cargo +nightly fmt` passes
- [ ] `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` passes
- [ ] (Optional) Documentation updated
- [ ] (Optional) Please join us on Slack [#sig-smg](https://slack.lightseek.org) to discuss, review, and merge PRs

</details>

author: dayartcrew-web
body:
## What

Local/stdio mode (`masday mcp`) created tasks — and the plans they reference — **only in SQLite**. PostgreSQL never learned a task existed, so:

- the API/dashboard showed workflows as **empty** after local task creation, and
- the per-task DONE sync shipped in **#46 (C2.13)** was a **no-op** — there was no PG task row to update.

This is the next scoped slice of **leverage #5 (SQLite↔PG sync gaps, C2.12–C2.17)**, off `master` (`ec271ba`). It **unblocks the rest of C2.13** (per-task completion sync now has a row to update).

## Changes

- **`direct_pg::plan_create`** + **`direct_pg::task_create`** (new). Both: no-op when no PG pool, 5s timeout, `ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE` upsert — mirroring the existing `workflow_create`/`workflow_status` pattern.
- **`direct.rs::workflow_add_task`**: after the SQLite INSERT succeeds, fire **one** fire-and-forget task that syncs the **plan first** (plans are otherwise absent from PG and are referenced by `tasks.plan_id`, a `NOT NULL REFERENCES plans(id)` FK), **then** the task. The plan row (status/summary/content/version/created_by_agent) is read from SQLite for faithful PG data.

## Why plan-before-task ordering

`tasks.plan_id` is `NOT NULL REFERENCES plans(id)` (migration `001`). Plans are never otherwise synced to PG in local mode, so the plan must land first or the task INSERT violates the FK. Both inserts run inside a single spawned task (sequential `await`), guaranteeing order — two independent spawns would race.

## Safety

- **Strictly additive.** SQLite write path is unchanged; the sync spawns only after a successful SQLite INSERT and no-ops without a PG pool.
- **Not unit-testable** (no live PG in the test env; spawn no-ops) — matches the **#46** convention for fire-and-forget PG syncs. Existing add_task tests cover the SQLite behavior.
- Re-verified live against `master` `ec271ba` before implementing (audit is point-in-time).

## Verification

- `cargo build -p masday-mcp` ✓
- `cargo fmt --check` ✓
- `cargo clippy -p masday-mcp --all-targets -- -D warnings` ✓
- `cargo test -p masday-mcp --lib` → **187 passed, 0 failed**

## Next slice

Per-task DONE sync (the rest of C2.13): add `direct_pg::task_status` + spawn it in `workflow_complete_task` so a locally-completed task flips to DONE in PG. Now unblocked by this PR.

author: mishamanevich
body:
## What

Adds a code-driven generator (`icehouse-panels/generate_panels.py`) that produces IceHouse panel cut-layout sheets for increasing **depth** while the **width stays fixed at 8' (96")** — modeled on the reference *IceHouse 8' x 8'* drawing.

Generates a sheet for each requested size: **8×10, 8×12, 8×14, 8×16** — both `.svg` (vector source of truth) and `.png` (preview) in `icehouse-panels/output/`.

## How depth scales

Width (the door wall) never changes. Each wall run is `12" corner + N×24" panel + 12" corner`:

| Footprint | Depth | Depth-side run | Floor strips |
|-----------|-------|----------------|--------------|
| 8×10 | 120" | 12 + 24×4 + 12 | 5 |
| 8×12 | 144" | 12 + 24×5 + 12 | 6 |
| 8×14 | 168" | 12 + 24×6 + 12 | 7 |
| 8×16 | 192" | 12 + 24×7 + 12 | 8 |

Each sheet keeps the three reference sections: **Wall Panels** (top-down ring with hatched corner posts), **Ceiling/Floor Panels** (24" strips), and **All Swing Door** (34"×76" door + cam-locks, unchanged since it sits on the fixed 96" wall).

## Why code instead of an image

Per the request — it's parametric and editable: change a constant or call `build_sheet(depth)` to add any new size (e.g. `build_sheet(216)` → 8×18). SVG generation is pure Python with no dependencies; `cairosvg` is only used to rasterize the PNG previews.

author: jfournier-evsm
body:
Makes the on-map hover/tap label actionable: **tap (or click) the label to add that node to the sequence**.

### Flow
- **Mobile**: tap a named node → its label appears (as today) now with a **"＋ tap to add to plan"** hint; tap the label → it's added to your sequence.
- **Desktop**: hover a node → label shows; move onto it and click → added. The hover is kept alive while the pointer is over the label (the keep-region bridges the small gap between the node and its label, so it doesn't vanish as you move toward it).

### How it works
- `drawAttrLabel` now records the label's screen rectangle (`labelHit`) each frame and appends the hint line (shows "✓ in plan — tap to add again" if it's already in the sequence).
- A canvas `click` handler adds the attraction when the click falls inside that rect. Adding re-runs `refresh()`, so the timeline updates immediately.
- Cleared at the start of each `draw()`, so it only triggers while a label is actually shown. Map clicks are otherwise unused in normal mode (panning only happens in Align-Map mode), so there's no conflict.

Duplicates are allowed (consistent with the picker — tapping again adds another visit). If you'd rather it not re-add when already in the plan, easy to gate.

author: clearmyrecord
body:
### Motivation
- AI-generated Ad Studio campaigns must be publishable even when `advertiserId` or `publisherId` are missing or do not exist to avoid foreign key errors on `Ad` creation. 
- The existing publish flow should be preserved (create Ad, upsert slots, update history, mark previous ads SUPERSEDED, and revalidate pages) while relaxing party requirements. 
- Admins need an immediate way to download generated ad images without publishing first. 

### Description
- In `app/api/ad-studio/campaigns/route.ts` validate `advertiserId` and `publisherId` before `prisma.ad.create()` by attempting `prisma.advertiser.findUnique()` and `prisma.publisher.findUnique()` and resolving to `null` when missing or not found, then use `advertiser?.id ?? null` and `publisher?.id ?? null` when creating the `Ad` and when writing campaign history. 
- Made `Ad.publisherId` and `Ad.advertiserId` nullable in `prisma/schema.prisma` and added a migration `prisma/migrations/20260619000000_nullable_ai_ad_publish_parties/migration.sql` to drop NOT NULL and recreate the FKs with `ON DELETE SET NULL` so generated ads can be created without party records. 
- Kept all existing publish logic (create `Ad`, `upsert` `IssueAdSlot`, `upsert` `StalltalkAdSlot`, update `StalltalkCampaignHistory`, supersede previous ads, and revalidate homepage/issue/admin paths) and updated the publish response to return `{ ok: true, message: "Campaign published successfully." }`. 
- Added immediate image download support in `components/AdStudioAgency.tsx` including a `Download Image` button next to `Use This Version`, `Publish This Version`, and `Regenerate`, a blob-download attempt for fetched image URLs with a fallback of `window.open()` for CORS failures, and the filename format `pottyfavor-generated-ad-{businessName}-{campaignId}.png`. 
- Tolerated nullable advertiser/publisher IDs across admin surfaces by applying small UI/server-side guards so pages do not crash when those relations are null. 

### Testing
- Ran `npx prisma generate` successfully to refresh the client. 
- Ran `npx tsc --noEmit` and fixed type issues, with the final typecheck succeeding. 
- Ran `npx prisma validate` which reported the schema is valid.
