author: robak503
body:
**Walt · WALT-TOKEN-ABIL slice 1** — the first slice of the ability-carrying-token lane: tokens minted **with a mana ability**, plus the false-positive that lives right alongside it.

## What this does

**1. Models token-borne MANA abilities (additive).** A created token whose printed ability is a clean, self-contained mana ability now carries that ability as its real `oracle`, so the mana model drives it exactly like Treasure/Gold — zero new enforcement:
- Eldrazi **Scion/Spawn** `"Sacrifice this token: Add {C}"`, Elf/Monk dorks `"{T}: Add {G}"`, any-color rocks `"Add one mana of any color"`.
- Two oracle shapes handled: `…token with "<ability>"` and `…token[ named N]. It has "<ability>"` (normalized to `with`).
- **Riders/restrictions route to the Arbiter** (CREED all-or-nothing): Powerstone "can't be spent on a nonartifact spell", "you gain 2 life", "spend only to cast a planeswalker spell", a different-color two-pip concat (`Add {W}{U}` — would mis-resolve), and any non-mana inline ability.

**2. Kills a pre-existing false positive in this lane (correctness).** A card's OWN mana was being fabricated from a **token's** ability stated in main text — `manaProduction(Blisterpod)` returned a sac-for-`{C}` source, so the engine would offer **"sacrifice Blisterpod for {C}"** (a fabricated ability; Blisterpod isn't a mana source — its Spawn is). `stripCreatedTokenAbilities` removes a created-token's quoted ability before own-mana detection, **mirrored** across `manaProduction` (runtime) and `coverage.hasManaAbility` (classifier) so they can't drift. **Scoped to create-token context**, so a self-granting lord (Gemhide Sliver) and a mana-grant anthem (Cryptolith Rite) are correctly left intact.

**3. CR 302.6 fidelity.** A summoning-sick creature whose mana ability needs no `{T}` (a sac-for-mana Eldrazi Spawn) is usable the turn it enters — so a freshly-made Spawn ramps immediately.

## Corpus impact (honest)

| | |
|---|---|
| **+2** | spells flip native: **Growth Spasm**, **Spawning Breath** (fully modeled, no dropped clause) |
| **−34** | false `native-mana` removed — token-makers (Eldrazi tribal, Svella, Llanowar Mentor, Kibo…) that were mis-read as fake mana sources |
| **net** | 17.20% → **17.11%** native — a deliberate **correctness** change (deletes fabricated mana sources) |

The −34 is the metric becoming honest. Those Eldrazi **permanents** are now correctly `body-only`/Arbiter; they'll flip **native-trigger** (with the Spawn carrying its real ability) once the trigger compiler captures a quoted token ability inside a trigger effect — see the handoff below.

## 🔗 Handoff to Cindy (TRIG lane) — the passive lift

The ~30 Eldrazi ETB/dies/upkeep makers stay body-only **only** because `detectTriggers` drops the token's `It has "…"` ability: `isFollowupSentence` excludes any sentence with a `:` (the ability's colon), and the line-300 trigger-effect regex `([^.]+)\.` truncates at the ability's internal period. Once a trigger's effect can carry a quoted token ability (`Doomed Traveler` already proves inline-ability create-token triggers are native), **all ~30 flip to native-trigger for free** — the atom is already in place. This is squarely the trigger compiler's lane, not mine.

## Verification

author: jduhking
body:
## Summary
Builds Relay's execution spine in `apps/server`: the **runtime coordinator (orchestrator)** plus all the **session control endpoints**. This connects the previously-shipped building blocks (session manager, adapters, process runner, broadcaster) into a working Claude → handoff → Codex → verify flow driven over HTTP.

## What's included
- **`orchestrator.ts`** — the coordinator. `startClaude → sendInput → buildHandoff → startCodex → verify`, driving the session state machine and fanning every `RelayEvent` to the event store and the broadcaster. Defines the injected `EventStore` interface + an `InMemoryEventStore` fallback and a deterministic placeholder `createHandoff`.
- **`evidence-collector.ts`** — read-only git evidence (branch/status/diff/changed files) → `EvidenceBundle`; `git` via `execFileSync` (no shell), with timeouts and non-git handling. Consolidated from the root `extract.ts`/`evidence-collector.ts` prototype.
- **`verifier.ts`** — runs the stored verification command via the process runner; **pass/fail comes from the exit code only** (never agent prose); emits `test.passed`/`test.failed`; returns `VerificationResult`.
- **`routes/control.ts`** — `POST claude/start`, `input`, `handoff`, `codex/start`, `verify`; `GET diff`, `events` — each delegating to the orchestrator.
- **Wiring** — `createApp` constructs the orchestrator (real Claude/Codex adapters + in-memory store + broadcaster sink); the router dispatches control routes; `SessionNotFoundError → 404`, `InvalidTransitionError → 409`.

Every route in the spec now exists except the optional Sentry trio (`WS /ws/sessions/:id` was already wired).

## Verification
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; **full server suite 74 pass / 0 fail / 0 skipped** (17 new); root engine suite still green.
- Orchestrator e2e (the Prompt 12 DoD): full state machine with fake adapters.
- Control routes over HTTP: create→start→input→handoff→codex→verify→diff→events, plus 400/404/405 mappings.
- Live smoke of the wired server: boots, creates a session, `/diff` returns real git facts, graceful shutdown.

## Reviewer notes — injected seams (swappable, no rework)
- **Michael — event store:** the orchestrator depends on `EventStore` (`appendEvent`/`readEvents`/`saveHandoff`/`loadHandoff`); his Redis `event-store.ts` should implement it, then drop `InMemoryEventStore`.
- **Michael — handoff builder:** `createHandoff(evidence, meta)` is injected; `fallbackCreateHandoff` is a deterministic placeholder to replace with `packages/context` `createFallbackHandoff`.
- **Syed — shared contracts:** `VerificationResult` is defined locally (proposed for promotion to `packages/shared`, like `RelaySession`).

## Consolidation note (not done here, on purpose)
The git-evidence *logic* moved into `apps/server`, but the **root engine** (`orchestrator.ts`, `contracts.ts`, `compressor.ts`, `extract.ts`, root `adapters/`) was left in place — it's still imported by the root `tests/` suite and Michael's compressor, so deleting it now would break CI and reach into his domain. `apps/server` is now the canonical runtime; retiring the root engine should be a coordinated follow-up cleanup.

author: aedanpope
body:
## What (step 7a — DB layer)

Separates the **teacher** from the **class** so one teacher code unlocks many classes. Owner mints teachers; teachers then self-serve classes and codes. This PR is the **database + client layer only**; the class-aware dashboard UI is the next PR. Backward-compat shims keep the current dashboard working in the meantime, so `main` is never broken.

## `0003_teachers.sql` (re-runnable)

- New `teachers` table (RLS-locked). `classes` gains `teacher_id`, **backfilled** from the old per-class `teacher_code_hash` (guarded, so re-runs are no-ops), then the per-class hash column is dropped. The teacher code is unchanged, so existing `pgp_sym`-encrypted student codes still decrypt. All current data is under `test-teacher-code-foxtrot-abacus`, which backfills to a single teacher owning the existing class.
- New RPCs: `teacher_classes`, `create_class` (capped at 100/teacher), `add_students_bulk` (mints N **anonymous, no-name** students from client-generated codes, skipping hash collisions and returning the codes added so the client can top up any shortfall), owner-only `mint_teacher` (replaces `mint_class`).
- Class-scoped `append_student` / `teacher_roster` / `reprint_codes` (now take `class_id` + verify ownership) and re-scoped `mark_complete`. Single-arg compat shims resolve the teacher's earliest class and delegate, so the pre-multi-class dashboard keeps working.

## Client + tests

- `supabase-client.js`: `teacherClasses`, `createClass`, `addStudentsBulk` wrappers (existing wrappers unchanged, hitting the compat shims).
- `supabase-itest.py`: extended to exercise `teacher_classes`, `create_class`, `add_students_bulk`, class-scoped roster + ownership rejection, and to clean up its throwaway class.

## How "no names in the DB" works

`add_students_bulk` inserts students with `display_name = null`. The cover sheet already renders nameless students as "My Pixel Game", and the teacher pairs the printed codes to their paper class list off-system.

## You need to

1. **Apply `0003_teachers.sql`** in the Supabase SQL editor (re-runnable). The existing test teacher/class backfills automatically, no action needed for it.
2. To create a **new** teacher later: `select mint_teacher('School', 'Teacher Name', '<teacher-code>');` (service role).
3. Re-run `supabase-itest.py` to validate against the live DB.

## Verification

- `0003` parsed with `pglast`; `supabase-client.js` syntax-checked + `supabase-client-test.js` 19/19 in V8; `supabase-itest.py` compiles. Full `npm run test:all` runs on CI. The live-DB behavior is validated by `supabase-itest.py`, which you run.

body: ## Summary Adds a new de-personalized, cross-platform **`ultimate-browsing`** shared skill: the escalation path the agent reaches for when a normal browse/fetch is blocked (WAF / 403 / Cloudflare / JS-only render / login-gated, or a platform a generic fetcher cannot read). It is a tiered web-access router vendored from a local browsing skill, with all personal context stripped, license-clean attribution, and a frozen de-personalization gate guarding it. - **Tier 1 — insane-search**: the user-original headless fetch engine (curl_cffi TLS impersonation, WAF detection, yt-dlp, Jina, public APIs, Playwright real-Chrome fallback), vendored at `engine/` and invoked as `python3 -m engine ""`. - **Tier 1.5 — agent-reach**: platform-native readers for Chinese + social platforms (Xiaohongshu, Douyin, Weibo, Bilibili, V2EX, WeChat, Twitter/Reddit/LinkedIn/GitHub), de-personalized to public/zero-config channels. - **Tier 2 — Chrome stealth**: CloakBrowser (MIT, runtime `pip`) + agent-browser (Apache-2.0, runtime `npm`) over CDP, documented as runtime dependencies (no source vendored), plus cross-platform cookie extraction. ## Changes (atomic commits, todos 6-12) 1. **scaffold + register** — `SKILL.md` de-personalized router; registered in the codex `expectedSkills` whitelist after `teammode`, before `ultraresearch` (the natural RED gate: the sync deepEqual fails until registered). 2. **vendor insane-search engine** — explicit file whitelist; `__pycache__`/`*.pyc`/`.DS_Store`/`test_smoke.py` excluded (the codex sync filter only drops `*.test.ts`, so a vendored `.py` smoke test would otherwise ship to npm + the public lazycodex repo). 3. **vendor + de-personalize tier-1/1.5 refs** — strip `~/.agent-reach` home paths, the literal `TWITTER_AUTH_TOKEN`/`TWITTER_CT0`/`xsec_token` names, and the personal browser choice; keep every zero-config public channel. 4. **de-personalization deny-list gate** — a NEW frozen gate (Node + bun:test) scanning `ultimate-browsing/**` + `ultraresearch/**` for PERSONAL IDENTITY + CREDENTIAL leakage only. It does NOT deny the kept tier name `agent-reach`, and is separate from the engine's `bias_check.py` no-site-name scanner. It immediately caught a leftover `TWITTER_*` literal in the scaffold env block. 5. **tier-2 chrome stealth doc** — condensed, cross-platform, version-pinned (cloakbrowser 0.3.28, agent-browser 0.27.1), no `aside`. 6. **cross-platform cookie extraction** — the macOS-only module rewritten into pure, testable functions split by responsibility (`cookie_paths`, `cookie_crypto`, `extract_cookies`) with the OS-keyring read as an injected boundary; synthetic-fixture tests for macOS/Linux/Windows (fake SQLite, known AES-CBC/GCM keys, injected keyring) — 13 tests pass, no live browser. 7. **ATTRIBUTION + finalize** — cloakbrowser MIT + agent-browser Apache-2.0 (incl. §4(b) notice) as runtime deps; engine + agent-reach refs declared project-original. Plus an inventory-test update classifying the synced ultimate-browsing Python files. ## Verification All evidence under `.omo/evidence/20260621-ultimate-browsing/`. - **Loader discovery** — OpenCode `discoverSharedSkills()` finds `ultimate-browsing` (`loader-discovery.txt`, `final-loader-discovery.txt`). - **Sync + whitelist** — `node --test sync-skills.test.mjs` 14 pass; deepEqual includes `ultimate-browsing` (`todo6-sync-test.txt`). - **Engine** — runs end-to-end against example.com producing JSON verdict/trace; no junk; import-clean (`engine-run.json`, `no-junk.txt`). - **De-personalization** — gate green on the cleaned tree, fails on a planted `jobdori` token (`depersonalization-gate.txt`, `depersonalization-gate-negative.txt`); refs grep returns nothing (`refs-depersonalized.txt`). - **Cookies** — 13 synthetic-fixture tests pass across macOS/Linux/Windows path resolution + CBC/GCM decrypt + injected keyring (`cookie-fixture-tests.txt`); unsupported platform/browser raises cleanly (`cookie-unsupported.txt`). - **Chrome stealth** — version pins present, no `aside` (`chrome-stealth-pins.txt`, `no-aside.txt`). - **Cross-harness landing** — codex `install-verify` lands `skills/ultimate-browsing/**` in an isolated `CODEX_HOME`; real `~/.codex/config.toml` SHA unchanged before/after (`codex-install-landing.txt`). - **Pre-push gates** — `bun run typecheck` clean, `bun test` 10091 pass / 0 fail, `bun run build` materializes the skill into `dist/skills`, `bun run test:codex` 360 pass / 0 fail (`pre-push-gates.txt`). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Adds a de-personalized, cross-platform `ultimate-browsing` shared skill that escalates web access when normal fetch/browse is blocked (WAF/403/Cloudflare/JS-only/login-gated). Includes a vendored Tier‑1 engine, platform readers, Tier‑2 Chrome stealth docs, a depersonalization gate, and cross-platform cookie extraction. - **New Features** - New `ultimate-browsing` skill registered in Codex; loader discovery and sync tests updated. - Tier 1: vendored `engine/**` (curl_cffi TLS impersonation, WAF detection, Playwright real‑Chrome fallback) runnable via `python3 -m engine ""`. - Tier 1.5: de‑personalized platform readers (Chinese + social) restricted to public/zero‑config paths. - Tier 2: Chrome stealth reference and cookie‑login flow; no source vendored. - Frozen depersonalization gate (`depersonalization-gate.*`) scanning `ultimate-browsing/**` + `ultraresearch/**` for identity/credential leakage, with tests. - Cross‑platform cookie extraction (`cookie_paths.py`, `cookie_crypto.py`, `extract_cookies.py`) with synthetic macOS/Linux/Windows fixtures. - **Dependencies** - Runtime pins for Tier 2: `cloakbrowser==0.3.28` (`pip`) and `agent-browser@0.27.1` (`npm`); attribution added, tools installed on demand. Adds a proptest harness for the three signal syscalls (`rt_sigprocmask`, `rt_sigpending`, `rt_sigaction`), which previously had unit tests but no property sweep.

Invariants asserted over arbitrary `how`, signal numbers, and pointers:
- **Never panic** — a bad guest pointer yields `SigError::Fault`, never an out-of-bounds host access.
- **SIGKILL/SIGSTOP are inescapable** — no `SETMASK` can block them and no `rt_sigaction` can install a disposition for them, matching the kernel.
- **Round-trip** — a well-formed mask written to a valid pointer comes back identical through `SIG_SETMASK`; a raised pending set round-trips through `rt_sigpending`.

Wires `proptest` as a dev-dependency of `prisma-session`. Validated: 5/5 tests pass, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` clean, fmt clean. No production code touched — conflict-free with the in-flight dispatcher PR.

body: ## Problem The public `/s/:slug/add-name` page showed "submission unavailable" even after an admin enabled public name submission in settings. The toggle appeared to save (success toast), but `publicSubmission.enabled` often stayed `false` in the database. ## Root cause - The enable checkbox is hidden with `display: none` inside a custom toggle, so its value was not always included in the settings form POST. - When the checkbox was missing, the server treated it as unchecked and persisted `enabled: false`. - Settings still redirected with `?saved=1` even when no fields were written, which made the failure look like success. - The optional donation URL used `type="url"`, which could block the entire settings form in the browser when the value was not a fully valid URL. ## Fix - Add a hidden `publicSubmissionEnabled=0` fallback and parse duplicate/array checkbox values reliably. - Persist public submission settings whenever those fields are present in the POST body. - Only show the saved confirmation after a successful DB update. - Change the donation URL field to `type="text"` (server still normalizes URLs). - Improve disabled/error messaging on the add-name page in Hebrew, English, and Russian. ## How to enable add-name 1. Log in to admin → Settings 2. Scroll to **הוספת שם ציבורית** / Public name submission 3. Enable the toggle and click Save 4. Share `/s/{slug}/add-name` with visitors ## Test plan - [x] Enable toggle via admin settings → `publicSubmission.enabled` becomes `true` in MongoDB - [x] Uncheck toggle and save → value becomes `false` - [x] `/s/novosibirsk/add-name?lang=he` shows the form when enabled - [x] POST submission adds a person and redirects to success page - [x] Disabled page shows clearer admin instructions

author: zengwen-dt
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Upgrading OpenClaw 2026.6.8 → 2026.6.9 corrupts the external ClawMail `email`
channel config. The doctor migration `maybeRepairGroupAllowFromFallback` injects
a `groupAllowFrom` key into `channels.email.accounts.default`, which the email
plugin's schema rejects, so the Gateway fails to start:

```
Config validation failed: channels.email.accounts.default: invalid config for plugin email: must not have additional properties: "groupAllowFrom"
```

Fixes #95515. (Supersedes #95518, which was auto-closed for the author's active-PR
queue limit, not on merit.)

## Why This Change Was Made

`generatedSchemaAllowsGroupAllowFrom` defaulted to **permissive** (`!schema || …`)
when a channel had no entry in the bundled channel-config metadata. `email` is an
external plugin (ClawMail) — it is not in this repo and is absent from
`GENERATED_BUNDLED_CHANNEL_CONFIG_METADATA` — so core cannot verify its schema and
must not write keys into it. Per the owner boundary in `AGENTS.md`
("plugin-owned config repairs live in that plugin's doctor contract"), external
plugin config repair belongs to that plugin's own doctor, not core.

The schema guard is the correct, minimal fix: it now **fails closed** when core
cannot confirm the target schema accepts the key. The capability default stays
permissive for warnings; only actual config *writes* are now schema-verified. This
is the only place core can fix this, since the email plugin lives outside the repo.

## User Impact

- Bundled channels (e.g. `feishu`) still migrate exactly as before — no regression.
- External channels with no bundled schema are left untouched on upgrade, so the
  Gateway no longer crash-loops after 2026.6.8 → 2026.6.9.

## Evidence

real-behavior proof — drove the actual `maybeRepairGroupAllowFromFallback` with the
exact config from the issue (external `email` account alongside a bundled `feishu`
channel), comparing current `main` behavior against the fix:

BEFORE (fix reverted, current `main` behavior) — reproduces the bug:
```
[repro95515] email.account after: {"allowFrom":["*"],"groupAllowFrom":["*"]}
[repro95515] changes: [
  "channels.feishu.groupAllowFrom: copied 1 sender entry ...",
  "channels.email.accounts.default.groupAllowFrom: copied 1 sender entry ..."
]
```

AFTER (this fix) — email untouched, feishu still migrated (no regression):
```
[repro95515] email.account after: {"allowFrom":["*"]}
[repro95515] changes: [
  "channels.feishu.groupAllowFrom: copied 1 sender entry ..."
]
```

Unit tests: `allowfrom-fallback-migration.test.ts` 7/7 pass (adds a case asserting
external schemaless channels are skipped). Format (`oxfmt --check`) and lint
(`oxlint`) clean on the changed files.

author: ancongui
body:
## Summary

A framework-wide audit (6 parallel lenses — provider-agnosticism, cost, cohesion, design-quality, test-coverage, streaming/structured — synthesized and **adversarially verified**) found the framework architecturally sound but **not yet rock-solid across any provider**. All **nine confirmed P0/P1 findings** are addressed here and validated against a **live Anthropic model**.

### Provider-agnosticism
- **`Model`-object provider identity** (`model_utils`): read the provider from `_provider.name`, so `OpenAIResponsesModel`/`GoogleModel`/`XaiModel`/`OpenRouterModel`/Azure/DeepSeek resolve correctly instead of dropping the provider (which corrupted cost lookup, quota keys, usage grouping).
- **Family detection**: match on the model *name* only — fixes `ollama:…`/`groq:…` misclassified as `meta` (substring `llama` ⊂ `ollama`); adds `grok`→`xai`; multi-vendor proxies → `unknown`.
- **`default_temperature`** wired **provider-safely** (`None` default = provider's own default, so `o1`/`o3` aren't forced a temperature they reject).

### Cohesion / correctness
- **Middleware error hook** (`on_error`) wired into `run`/`run_sync`/`run_stream` — the **CircuitBreaker can now open** and the **OTel span no longer leaks** on a failed run (`resilience/` was effectively orphaned).
- **Reasoning runs through `FireflyAgent`** — structured calls inherit middleware/429-retry/usage instead of a bare `pydantic_ai.Agent`; normalised the recorded model id (`str(Model)` repr → `provider:model`).
- **Structured-output streaming no longer crashes** — `text()` falls back to `stream_output()` snapshots; `stream_tokens()` raises a clear `AgentError`.
- **`cost_strict` honoured on every path** — workflow + agent paths stop swallowing `UnknownModelCostError`; `budget_limit_usd` docstring corrected.
- **`retryable()`** wraps `_execute`, so retries cover the pydantic-ai handler path and `RunContext`-aware tools.

### Testing (the biggest gap)
- New **live e2e suite** (`tests/integration/test_real_anthropic_e2e.py`, `@pytest.mark.nightly`, skips without a real key): agent+tools, structured output, streaming, multi-turn memory, reasoning, pipeline, a workflow (`FireflyAgentRunner` + `using=`), cost tracking — **8/8 pass against real Anthropic haiku**. Previously every provider-facing behaviour was validated only against mocks; `tests/README.md` corrected.

## Validation
- `ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .` clean, **pyright 0**, **pre-commit clean** (incl. gitleaks).
- **1434 PR-gate tests pass** (+ new unit tests per fix: model-object provider extraction, structured streaming, middleware error hook / circuit breaker / span, reasoning routing, retryable handler path).
- **Live e2e: 8/8** against real Anthropic, re-run green after every fix.

## Deferred (documented follow-ups, lower priority)
COST-001 (provider-aware reasoning-token pricing — Gemini `thoughts_tokens` undercount; largely mitigated by the reasoning→FireflyAgent routing) and the remaining audit P2s (per-provider prompt-cache for Bedrock/OpenRouter, Gemini strict-schema for `dict[str, Any]` tool params, single-flight caching, orphaned `storage/`, strategy thread-safety). Version → 26.06.6.

author: cooperlees
body:
## What & why

The Simple/Index API already exposes the hash of each file's [Core Metadata](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/core-metadata/) (the `.metadata` file served alongside a distribution) via the `core-metadata` key, as standardized by [PEP 658] and [PEP 714]. For example, [`/simple/black/`](https://pypi.org/simple/black/) carries it today.

The legacy JSON API (`/pypi/<project>/json`) does **not**, which means consumers that mirror PyPI — notably [bandersnatch](https://github.com/pypa/bandersnatch) — cannot discover and serve PEP 658/714 Core Metadata from the JSON API and have to fall back to the Simple API. This then adds an extra PyPI call to get the simple API adding load on PyPI and more network calls for clients we'd love to not need to do.

This PR adds a `core-metadata` key to every file object returned by both JSON routes:

- `GET /pypi/<project>/json` (under `urls` and `releases`)
- `GET /pypi/<project>/<version>/json` (under `urls`)

## Format

It mirrors the Simple/Index API format exactly so it can be passed straight through by mirrors:

- `false` when no metadata file is available
- `{"sha256": "<hex>"}` when it is

```json
{
  "filename": "black-...-py3-none-any.whl",
  "digests": { "md5": "...", "sha256": "...", "blake2b_256": "..." },
  "core-metadata": { "sha256": "..." },
  ...
}
```

The hyphenated key name `core-metadata` is intentional: it matches the PEP 714 standardized field name and the existing Simple/Index API key, rather than the JSON API's usual snake_case, so mirrors can reuse it without translation.

## Tests & docs

- Updated `tests/unit/legacy/api/test_json.py` to assert the new key, covering both the populated (`{"sha256": ...}`) and absent (`false`) branches. `warehouse/legacy/api/json.py` remains at 100% coverage.
- Updated the user-facing JSON API docs (`docs/user/api/json.md`) with a description of the field and example payloads.

Refs https://github.com/pypa/bandersnatch/issues/1124

[PEP 658]: https://peps.python.org/pep-0658/
[PEP 714]: https://peps.python.org/pep-0714/

Plan PR C (see `TODO/refactor-plan.md`). Adds the capability to mark a chapter as an optional **bonus**.

## Behavior
A chapter with `bonus = true` in `.chapter.toml` is:
- **hidden** from the table of contents and the chapter picker
- **excluded** from progress totals and the next-chapter CTA (which now skips it)
- rendered **without a number** ("Bonus chapter" eyebrow + ★ badge)
- still **reachable** by direct URL

## How
- `ChapterDirectives.bonus` + `Exercise::is_bonus()`.
- Chapter display numbers are assigned in `scan_dir` as a running **ordinal over non-bonus chapters**, so hiding a bonus leaves **no gap**. Bonus chapters get `0`. (Backward-compatible: with no bonus chapters the numbers are identical to the old `prefix + 1`.)
- `is_bonus` threaded through `ProgressDot`/`ExerciseProgress`; bonus excluded from `completable_total`, both dashboards, and the per-page progress + next-CTA.
- Templates: `chapter_list.html` and the `exercise.html` picker skip bonus rows; the header/label render "Bonus".
- Marked the two bonus chapters (`smart_pointers`, `password_validator`) via `.chapter.toml` **at their current locations** — PR D will relocate them.
- Forward mentions added to the word-frequencies and traits wrap-ups so the bonus chapters stay discoverable (also fixed a stale "Chapter 15" cross-ref).

## Validation
- New regression test `bonus_chapters_are_unnumbered_and_excluded_from_the_sequence` (numbers are 1..=N gap-free; bonus = 0).
- `fmt`, `clippy -D warnings`, lib+bin tests (15 pass), `check-examples.sh`, `REQUIRE_COMPLETE=1 check-solutions.sh` all green.
- **Runtime smoke test:** booted the server and confirmed bonus chapters are hidden from the homepage TOC + picker, the bonus page renders a "Bonus chapter" eyebrow, and the word-frequencies next-CTA skips the bonus chapter.

The dashboard TOC shows numbers one higher than exercise pages (`ExerciseProgress.number = ex.number + 1`). This predates the PR; I preserved it to keep scope tight. Worth a separate fix.

body:
# Motivation

Sunmmio target handling was mixed into the generic lowering and optimization pipelines, making the control flow harder to follow and increasing the risk of applying non-Sunmmio passes to Sunmmio modules. Tests also needed a lightweight way to run code under a resolved TVM target context without repeating target setup logic.

# Solution

This PR separates Sunmmio-specific phase handling into dedicated pipeline functions:

- Add `LowerAndLegalizeSunmmio` for Sunmmio lowering and legalization.
- Add `OptimizeForSunmmio` for Sunmmio optimization, pipeline planning, synchronization injection, host/device splitting, packed API generation, and kernel launch lowering.

author: rjwalters
body:
Closes #337

## Summary

Adds configurable **graded / non-uniform radial mesh strategies** to the 2D mesh generators in `crates/geode-core/src/waveguide_modes.rs`, so callers can concentrate triangle density where a problem needs it instead of being limited to uniform-per-region spacing.

## Grading spec

New public `RadialGrading` enum (Copy, default `Uniform`) controlling how the `n_radial` ring radii are distributed *within* a single region `[r_inner, r_outer]`:

- **`Uniform`** — current behavior (default).
- **`Geometric { ratio }`** — adjacent ring steps scale by a constant factor (`ratio > 1` clusters toward the inner edge, `< 1` toward the outer).
- **`Linear { ratio }`** — ring step grows/shrinks linearly; last step is `ratio×` the first.
- **`InterfaceClustered { strength }`** — densifies toward the region edge nearest the core–cladding interface `r = a` (from both sides: core densifies toward its outer edge, cladding/PML toward their inner edge); larger `strength` ⇒ tighter clustering.

Grading only redistributes rings **within** a region; the region-boundary rings (`core_radius`, `cladding_outer`, `outer_radius`) stay fixed, so the conforming-ring structure, the centroid-radius region tagging, and the geometry-keyed boundary/interior-DOF masks (`disk_boundary_nodes`, `disk_pec_interior_dofs2`, etc.) all keep working under any grading.

## Generators (which take the spec)

- `disk_tri_mesh_graded(core_grading, cladding_grading)`
- `disk_tri_mesh_pml_graded(core_grading, cladding_grading, pml_grading)` — **per-band grading**, the variant the downstream graded-fiber experiment needs.
- `rect_tri_mesh_graded(x_grading, y_grading)` — axial x/y grading for the rectangular generator.
- `*_graded_checked(..., aspect_bound)` — checked constructors that **reject** sliver-producing configs (return `Err`).

The existing un-graded `disk_tri_mesh` / `disk_tri_mesh_pml` now delegate to the graded path with `Uniform` (single triangulation code path in a shared `build_disk_mesh` helper); `rect_tri_mesh` is untouched.

## Mesh-quality guard

`worst_aspect_ratio(&mesh) -> f64` exposes the worst triangle aspect ratio (`longest_edge / 2·inradius`, matching the existing disk-mesh quality metric). The `*_checked` constructors reject any config whose worst aspect ratio exceeds `ASPECT_RATIO_SLIVER_BOUND` (= 25.0).

## Tests (all green)

- **Uniform bit-for-bit reproduction (load-bearing):** `disk_tri_mesh_graded` / `disk_tri_mesh_pml_graded` / `rect_tri_mesh_graded` with `Uniform` produce **exactly** the same nodes, triangles, and tags as the un-graded generators (exact `f64` equality; the disk core/cladding/PML bands reuse the original arithmetic forms so there is no FP drift).
- **Density concentration asserted:** geometric — ratio of adjacent radial steps ≈ configured factor; linear — last/first step ratio ≈ configured factor and monotone; interface-clustered — min step is the one adjacent to `r = a` (verified for both core-outer-edge and cladding-inner-edge cases).
- **Validity / tags under grading:** every strategy yields a connected, CCW, non-degenerate mesh; core area fraction still matches `(a/R)²` to ~2%; tags agree with the centroid-radius band; boundary node set is still exactly the outer ring; p=2 interior-DOF mask still builds.
- **Aspect-ratio guard:** mild grading passes the checked constructor; a deliberately pathological geometric config is rejected.

## Verification

- `cargo build -p geode-core` — clean (default + `--no-default-features --features ndarray`).
- `cargo test -p geode-core` — 237 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored (pre-existing); all integration binaries pass. No regression in the disk-mesh / waveguide tests.
- `cargo clippy -p geode-core --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.
- No new dependencies.

## Non-goal (per the issue)

This is **general mesh infrastructure**, **NOT** a fix for the SMF-28 weakly-guiding fiber spectral-pollution problem (#330/#333) — a prior diagnostic proved that problem is not mesh-resolution-limited.

author: urisland
body:
## What

Mila already detects when you join a Zoom meeting and **prompts to start** recording. This adds the inverse: when a tracked meeting goes **inactive while Mila is actively recording**, a floating prompt asks whether to **stop**:

> **Zoom meeting ended** — Stop recording now?  [Stop recording] [Keep recording]

It fires regardless of how the recording was started (auto-prompt or manual), and is gated on the same Settings → Meetings toggle as the start prompt.

## How

- **`MeetingDetector`** now emits a debounced `meetingEnded` subject on the active→inactive transition (the inverse of `meetingStarted`). To avoid false positives when Zoom momentarily drops the mic (mute/unmute, device switch), the falling edge requires `endConfirmationPolls` consecutive inactive polls (default **2** → ~6s at the 3s poll). The transition core is factored into `processActiveMeetings(_:)`, fed by either the real Core Audio poll or a `simulatePollForTesting(activeBundleIDs:)` test seam.
- **`MeetingPromptCoordinator`** subscribes to `meetingEnded` and presents the stop prompt. The overlay (`MeetingPromptView`) is generalized with a `Kind` (`.start` / `.stop`) that drives the copy, the primary button, and the accessibility identifiers (`meetingPrompt.*` vs `meetingStopPrompt.*`).
- The show/no-show decision is a **pure, injectable** `MeetingPromptCoordinator.shouldShowStopPrompt(detectionEnabled:appSilenced:isRecording:promptAlreadyShowing:)` — easy to unit-test without a real Zoom.
- Stopping routes through `QuickActionsController.stopRecording()`.
- Settings → Meetings copy updated to mention both directions.

## Tests

- **Unit** (`MilaTests/MeetingStopPromptTests.swift`):
  - decision logic — recording + meeting ended → prompt; not recording → none; feature disabled → none; app silenced → none; prompt already showing → none.
  - detector transition — a brief drop+recover does **not** fire; sustained inactivity fires exactly once; never-active never fires; rejoin-then-end fires again.
- **UI** (`MilaUITests/MeetingStopPromptUITests.swift`, optional): launches with `--ui-test-simulate-meeting-ended`, which starts a fake recording and fires `meetingEnded`, then asserts the `meetingStopPrompt.*` panel appears. Exercises the real presentation path; only the trigger is faked.

## Verification

- `xcodebuild ... build-for-testing` — **TEST BUILD SUCCEEDED** (app + both test targets compile).
- Ran `MilaTests/MeetingStopPromptTests` — **9/9 passed**.

## What a human should check

- **Real Zoom end-of-meeting behavior**: confirm leaving/ending an actual Zoom call while recording surfaces the stop prompt within a few seconds, and that ordinary mid-call mic mute/unmute does **not** trip it (the debounce should absorb it). The ~6s debounce window may want tuning against real Zoom mic-release timing.

author: verzog
body:
## Summary

Addresses a batch of review comments on the **session** and **shared-server isolation** diagnostics. Each was checked for validity and whether it was already included; the valid, not-yet-included ones are fixed here. All changes are read-only/best-effort and keep the plugin's "always unconfirmed" tone.

## Review comments addressed

1. **Use the resolved session handler before warning** — When `$CFG->session_handler_class` is empty, core does **not** always default to file: `\core\session\manager` selects the **database** handler when `$CFG->dbsessions` is enabled (and the DB supports session locking). `get_session_info()` now resolves the effective handler the same way, so a database-session site is no longer mislabelled "defaults to file" and no longer triggers the Redis-inactive / file-session warning. The "not set" label now reports the resolved default (`file` / `database`).

2. **Do not use script owner as the process UID** — `current_euid()` dropped the `getmyuid()` fallback. `getmyuid()` returns the owner of the PHP *script file*, not the worker's effective UID; on hosts without POSIX it would compare `/proc` owners against the wrong identity. The `/proc` visibility check is now skipped unless a true effective UID is available.

3. **Do not infer hidepid when no foreign process is present** — `get_proc_visibility()` now tracks foreign-owned processes *sampled* separately from *readable* ones. The panel only claims `hidepid` is active when foreign processes were seen but hidden; when none were running it reports an inconclusive note instead of a false hardened signal.

4. **Treat unavailable account lookups as incomplete** — When neither `/etc/passwd` is readable nor `posix_getpwnam()` is available, a failed pool-user lookup is now classified `unresolved` (undetermined) rather than the hard `nouser` failure, so such hosts report an *Incomplete* audit instead of a *Weak* verdict.

5. **Preserve incomplete verdicts when pool users are unresolved** — `assess_isolation()` no longer returns the site-centric *Partial* ("on its own dedicated pool") result when another pool's config is undetermined (e.g. user set in an `include`) **and** the current request's pool was not positively matched as clean. Such hosts now report *Incomplete*. The deliberate #26 behaviour (dedicated current + unreadable-but-not-undetermined other pools → Partial + caveat) is preserved.

### Already included (no change needed)
- **Flag cron that has never run** — already handled: `get_cron_health()` leaves `age` null when `MAX(lastruntime)` is falsy, and `render_cron_health()` renders the never-run warning for that case (it does not suppress the section).

## Testing

Validated via a reflection harness (stubbed `block_base`/`get_string`) exercising the private methods directly:
- Session type resolves to `file` / `database` per `dbsessions` + `session_lock_supported()`, explicit handlers still detected; the "not set (defaults to database)" label renders and database sessions are flagged info (not the file warning).
- `/proc` render produces leak / hidden / inconclusive states correctly.
- Pool issue is `nouser` when resolution is available and `unresolved` (undetermined severity) when not.
- Verdict matrix: preserved #26 cases (other-pool hard → Partial, own-pool hard → Weak, generic + unreadable → Partial) and the new #6 case (hard + undetermined, current pool unmatched → Incomplete; matched-clean → Partial).

`php -l` clean on changed files; `block_servermon.php` stays within the 132-char limit. Version bumped to `1.9.1` (`2026062100`); README and CHANGELOG updated.

author: jbeshir
body:
## Problem

The three widget pipeline skills (`build-widget`, `widget-frontend-tutorial`, `widget-design-tutorial`) branched from the **mounted HEAD** and landed by **switching the single shared `beshir-widgets` working tree** (`switch main` / `pull` on prep; `switch -c … FETCH_HEAD` + `commit --amend --reset-author` on land).

That made the one host checkout a serialization point: you had to let one widget fully land and switch the tree back to `main` before safely launching the next — concrete symptom was *lots of waiting on other widget tasks*. It also let a build branch off whatever HEAD the previous widget left checked out, contaminating its base.

The demesne side was never the issue — sandbox mounts are read-only and outputs are UUID-keyed, so concurrent pipelines are already isolated in-sandbox. The whole problem was host-side git on one mutable working tree.

## Change

Make host-prep and host-landing **checkout-free** across all three skills:

- **Host-prep:** `git fetch origin main` only (no `switch`/`pull`); capture the host commit identity to hand to the orchestrator.
- **In-sandbox finalize:** branch from `origin/main` (tutorials: or `origin/<headRef>` when appended to an open widget PR), commit **authored as the host** — so the host needs no re-author.
- **Host-landing:** create the branch ref via a fetch refspec (`+<branch>:refs/heads/<branch>`) and push; the open-PR tutorial case fast-forwards onto `<headRef>` via `push origin <branch>:<headRef>`. The working tree is **never switched**.

Net: concurrent widget builds and tutorials can run and land in any order without blocking on the shared checkout, and the base-contamination path is closed.

Patch bump to **0.2.15** so `/plugin` re-syncs the cache.

## Not touched

The four code-landing demesne skills (`sandbox-feature-work`, `-quality-improvement`, `-migration-sweep`, `-test-gen-from-spec`) use a deliberately different model — `fetch` + `merge --ff-only` to *integrate the change into the host's local `main`*. That ff-merge moves the working tree on purpose (you end up with the change checked out), and integrating into one `main` is inherently sequential. They don't have the branch-and-PR-while-leaving-the-tree-alone shape, so they're correct as-is.

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|

- **다운로드 URL 발급 전략**: 사진은 목록에서 즉시 발급, 동영상은 다운로드 시점에만 발급 (레거시 동일, 목록 대량 발급 회피)

author: matthew-demidoff
body:
## Severity: MEDIUM ×2 (from external review)

Both in the grace-period deletion purge (`worker.js sweepPendingDeletions`):

1. **TOCTOU** — the sweep SELECTed due accounts then `delete from users where id = $1` with no re-check. A user who **cancelled** their deletion by signing in (which clears `deletion_requested_at`) between the scan and the delete was still irreversibly purged.
2. **PII retention** — `security_events.user_id` is `ON DELETE SET NULL`, so a purged user's audit rows survived carrying **IP / user-agent / country / metadata** (including raw Telegram id + username) until the 90-day retention sweep — undercutting the erasure the user asked for.

## Fix

Each purge now runs in **its own transaction**:
- Re-selects the row `FOR UPDATE` with the same deletion-window predicate. A cancelled (or no-longer-eligible) account doesn't match and is skipped — closing the race atomically.
- **Scrubs** `ip` / `user_agent` / `country` / `metadata` on that user's `security_events` rows *before* the delete (while `user_id` still resolves), leaving only user-less event shells (type / result / timestamp) for audit integrity.
- Then reserves the Telegram-id ban, writes the `account_purged` audit row, and deletes the user — all-or-nothing.

## Verification

- `node --check worker.js`; `tsc` clean; unit suite 155 passed.
- Post-merge: deploy **worker** and live-test on throwaway users — an over-grace account is purged with its audit PII scrubbed, while a within-grace account is left untouched.

**Deploy note:** needs the **worker** rebuilt (not `app`).

body:
## 요약
[BE2] 검색 평가 **지표 타당성(construct validity) 검토** — nDCG/rel("재사용 안전")이 실제 "답변 초안 생성 도움"을 재는지 점검. (#464 후속, 분석 단계 — 운영 코드 미변경)

## 핵심 발견
- **천장 효과**: BE3 실제 답변 범위(grounding top-5, 프롬프트 2~3)로 재계산하니 **Success@3=1.0 · MRR≈0.99 · hit@5≈3.6** → 검색 시스템 변별이 거의 없음. 형태소 hybrid=dense 동률은 top-5/3에서도 유지.
- **천장 정체**: query↔top-1 유사도 평균 0.825(>0.95 0%, >0.90 5%), top-1 관련율 97% → **near-dup/self-retrieval 아님, 검색이 실제로 잘 찾는 게 맞음**(평가가 복붙으로 부풀려진 게 아님).
- **최대 validity gap(미해결)**: 평가 rel은 문서 전체(2000자)로 채점했는데 답변엔 snippet(120~200자)만 들어감.

## 결론
- 검색 ranking은 이미 천장(실제 실력) → **검색 nDCG를 더 올릴 여지 적음**. nDCG는 의사결정 지표에서 내려놓고 보조로.
- 진짜 개선 여지 = **query 대표성**(운영 사용자 질문은 더 어려움) · **snippet utility** · **BE3 답변 생성**.
- **최대 함정**: "검색 rel 포화 = RAG 품질 포화" 착각(BE3는 snippet이 좌우).

## 산출물
- `scripts/eval_topk_validity.py` — BE3 범위(top-5/3) 정렬 지표(nDCG@5/3·Success·hit·MRR)
- `scripts/diag_self_retrieval.py` — 천장 정체(self-retrieval/near-dup) 진단
- `reports/retrieval/v3/ndcg_eval_civil.md` — "지표 타당성 검토" 절 추가

## 검증
독립 AI 4차 교차검토 수용. 다음(ROI): 사람 spot-check(top-5 snippet 충분/부족/위험) > snippet 재평가 > query 대표성 > 형태소 운영 튜닝 > end-to-end.

author: gnanam1990
body:
## Summary

Adds an **Agent Client Protocol (ACP)** surface so ZERO can run as an **editor backend**: editors that speak ACP (Zed, JetBrains, Neovim, …) spawn `zero acp` and drive ZERO's agent over JSON-RPC 2.0 on stdio. This is one more surface on ZERO's surface-agnostic core — alongside the TUI, headless `exec`, the MCP server, and cron — reusing the same `agent.Run`, tool registry, permission model, and session store. **Provider, model, and API keys stay owned by ZERO (BYOK); the editor only hosts the conversation thread.**

## Provenance

Derived **solely from the public, Apache-licensed ACP specification** (agentclientprotocol.com schema/v1 and the `agent-client-protocol` repository). Method names and message shapes come from the spec; all logic is written originally against ZERO's own interfaces. **No third-party agent's ACP implementation was read, copied, or paraphrased.** No new dependencies — standard library only.

## What's implemented (`internal/acp/` + `zero acp`)

- **Transport** — a bidirectional JSON-RPC 2.0 peer over newline-delimited JSON. It serves inbound requests/notifications and issues outbound calls (needed for the client-directed `session/request_permission`). Handlers run concurrently so a long-running `session/prompt` never blocks `session/cancel` or a permission response; in-flight handlers are drained on stream close so piped/finite input never drops a reply.
- **Methods** — `initialize` (capability + protocol-version negotiation), `session/new`, `session/load` (replays stored history so resume has context), `session/prompt` (drives a real `agent.Run` turn), `session/cancel`, `session/set_mode` (permission/autonomy mode), model selection via `session/set_config_option` (plus a vendor `_zero/set_model` alias), and the agent→client `session/request_permission`.
- **Event streaming** — ZERO's agent events are translated to `session/update` notifications: assistant text → `agent_message_chunk`, reasoning → `agent_thought_chunk`, tool calls → `tool_call` / `tool_call_update` (with content and changed-file locations), and plan items → `plan`.
- **Permission mapping** — ZERO's permission prompts map to ACP `PermissionOption`s (the option id carries the ZERO decision verbatim for a lossless round trip); the client's outcome maps back to a ZERO decision and **fails closed to deny** on anything unrecognized.
- **Capabilities** — advertises only what ZERO supports: `loadSession`, `promptCapabilities.image`, and session resume/load. ZERO executes tools locally, so client `fs/*` / `terminal/*` delegation is intentionally not required; clients that offer them still interoperate. ZERO-specific extras are vendor-prefixed (`_zero/…`) so clients that don't support them degrade cleanly.
- **`zero acp` subcommand** — registered in the CLI dispatch and help. It reuses config resolution, provider construction, the core tool registry, and the session store, so behavior matches the other surfaces.

## Commits (staged, one concern each)

1. JSON-RPC 2.0 ndjson transport
2. ACP wire types (from the public spec)
3. event → `session/update` translation
4. permission prompt ↔ `session/request_permission` mapping
5. the ACP Agent server driving `agent.Run`
6. the `zero acp` subcommand
7. drain in-flight handlers on stream close

## Test plan

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, **`go test ./... -race` — all green** (adds the `internal/acp` package).
- Unit tests: transport (request/response, notifications, errors, and a mid-handler callback that mirrors `session/prompt` → `session/request_permission`), event→update translation, and permission mapping.
- **Integration test**: drives `initialize` + `session/new` + `session/prompt` over in-memory pipes through the **real `agent.Run`** with a fake provider and asserts the streamed updates and stop reason.
- Verified against the built binary: the handshake and a full streamed turn — `tool_call` → `tool_call_update` → streamed answer → `stopReason: end_turn`.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- **Submit ZERO to the ACP Registry** so it's installable as an agent in Zed / JetBrains (manual step).
- Advertise the user's *configured* providers' models in the model picker (currently it lists the model-registry defaults).
- Optional client-hosted `fs/*` + `terminal/*` for editors that prefer to own file access and the terminal.

Do not merge — opening for review.

  * Introduced a JSON-RPC transport with request/notification handling and robust stream parsing.
  * Implemented end-to-end ACP agent session flow: initialize, create/load sessions, run prompt turns, stream message/thought updates, and handle cancellation.
  * Added permission request forwarding with fail-closed option handling, plus per-session mode/model selection.

author: copilot
body:
Two final web-companion polish items: in dark mode only the cards changed colour while the page background stayed white (most visible in demo mode), and the layout used a single mobile column on desktop/widescreen, wasting horizontal space.

### Dark-mode page background
- The `body` rule folded the colour and gradient into one shorthand:
  ```css
  /* before — invalid, silently dropped */
  background: var(--bg) var(--bg-grad) fixed;
  ```
  `--bg-grad` is a **two-layer** gradient, so the colour was no longer on the last layer — the whole declaration was invalid and discarded, leaving the page transparent over the white canvas while only `--card` tiles re-themed.
- Split into separate `background-color` / `background-image` / `background-attachment` so the page background tracks the theme.

### Demo-mode width
- Demo was wrapped in the centred `.screen` grid (meant for setup/unlock), which shrink-wrapped the dashboard to its content width and overflowed horizontally, including on phones. It now renders in normal full-width flow (`.demo-shell`) like the live app.

### Widescreen layout
- Mobile-first single column is unchanged — same markup, same source order, additive `min-width` queries only.
- At ≥64rem, `.content` becomes a dashboard grid: hero beside the return horizons, KPIs as a full-width strip, holdings as the main column with the allocation panel as a sidebar. Wider content + sidebar at ≥100rem.

### Docs
- `web/README.md` updated to describe the desktop multi-column enhancement.

body:
## Track 4 — Versioning Phase-2: auto-tag on milestone close

The standing repo automation behind the owner's **"complete a milestone → tag/release"**. Built **conservatively as a DRAFT, dry-run-by-default, never auto-enabled on prod without validation.**

### What's here (4 new files, fully additive — no existing file touched)
| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `.github/workflows/release-on-milestone-close.yml` | trigger → gate → (dry-run print \| real tag+release) |
| `qa/release_gate_check.py` | the **unit-tested**, READ-ONLY gate decision |
| `qa/test_release_gate_check.py` | 15 tests + a workflow-YAML structural lint |
| `docs/roadmap/release-automation.md` | marker convention + dry-run→live promotion |

### The gate design — solving "GitHub milestones don't support labels"
GitHub milestones can't carry labels, so the "ready-for-release" opt-in is an explicit **`[release-ready]` marker** in the milestone **title or description** (case-insensitive, literal brackets so prose can't trip it). The full gate (all must hold for a GO):
1. **`[release-ready]` marker** present — else NO-GO (a development milestone closing must NOT auto-tag).
2. **Clean `vX.Y.Z[-rcN]` title → tag** — `Sprint 12`, `v1.0`, `v1.0.5 (final)` are refused.
3. **Tag does not already exist** — never clobber/re-cut.
4. **Version consistency** — milestone base `X.Y.Z` must equal `VERSION` **and** `servers/engine/__version__.py`.
5. **STATUS: RELEASE** — `generate_release_notes.py` / the per-gate verdict reports **all 11 RRI gates PASSED**. `DEVELOPMENT` (any gate SKIPPED/FAILED/MISSING/UNKNOWN) ⇒ NO-GO. A `-rcN` pre-release may opt in to ship on DEVELOPMENT via `allow_prerelease_dev`; a GA **always** requires RELEASE.

The decision lives in `qa/release_gate_check.py` (extracted from YAML) so it's **unit-tested** rather than ad-hoc shell. It reuses `generate_release_notes`' DEVELOPMENT/RELEASE logic so there is ONE definition of the flag.

### Dry-run safety (why merging this is safe)
- `dry_run` **defaults to `true`**. A real `milestone: closed` event has no input → dry-run, unless the owner sets repo var `RELEASE_AUTOMATION_LIVE=true`.
- Dry-run runs the **full** resolution + notes and prints **exactly what it would tag/release** — creates **nothing**.
- Only an explicit dispatch `dry_run=false` **or** the live repo-var reaches `git tag` + `gh release create`. The real step re-confirms the tag is free immediately before cutting (defense-in-depth).
- Minimal `permissions: contents: write`. No gameplay/heavy job; reads the scores ledger READ-ONLY; **never touches Eva or any gateway**.

> The RELEASE status comes from a real per-gate RRI artifact (`--verdict-json`/`--rri-json`). None is committed, so a bare run falls back to **ledger-inference, which can never certify RELEASE** (honesty guard) — a GO requires real release evidence, not merely a closed milestone.

### Validation
- `qa/test_release_gate_check.py`: **15 passed** (the four load-bearing cases + edges).
- Combined with the Phase-1 deps (`test_generate_release_notes.py`, `test_version_consistency.py`): **30 passed**.
- `actionlint` on the new workflow: **clean (exit 0)**.
- `scripts/license_check.py`: passed. `scores.db`/ledger: untouched.

### Promoting from dry-run to live (needs owner sign-off)
1. One successful **dry-run on a real closed `[release-ready]` milestone** (title == bumped VERSION, all-PASS RRI artifact wired in).
2. Go live either **per-cut** (`gh workflow run "release-on-milestone-close.yml" -f milestone=vX.Y.Z -f dry_run=false`) or **standing** (`gh variable set RELEASE_AUTOMATION_LIVE --body true`).
3. Verify the tag + `gh release` (pre-release iff `-rc`) and the generated notes body.

Kept DRAFT per the conservative scope — flipping to real mode needs owner sign-off + one successful dry-run.

body:
## Why

Role promotion was SQL-only (`docs/authz.md` documented the hand-run `INSERT INTO role_bindings`). That was a wave-1 shortcut and does not scale past the pilot: every change is a DBA ticket with no in-product audit. This is the second half of the SSO + RBAC story (#66), following the SSO config UI (#375) and service-account auth (#376), reusing the same admin-settings shell. Closes #135.

## What changed

Scope (wave-2, confirmed with the maintainer): manage existing users, single role per user. New operators still arrive via OIDC JIT or break-glass.

**Server**
- New `user.manage` authz action (admin-scoped; listing stays on `user.read`), registered in `actions.json` + `roles.json` with the parity test green.
- `rbac` store: `AllLiveBindings`, `LiveGlobalRoles`, transactional `SetUserRole` (single-global-binding replace), `CountActiveAdmins`. `users` store: admin `List`, `GetAdmin`, `SetStatus`.
- New `useradmin` handler behind the chokepoint: `GET /api/settings/users`, `PUT /api/settings/users/{id}/role`, `PUT /api/settings/users/{id}/status`.
- Guardrails: last admin cannot be demoted/disabled, no self-management, break-glass immutable, `super_admin` grantable only by a `super_admin`.
- Audit `authz.role_binding.{create,update,delete}` and `user.{disabled,enabled}` on every applied mutation; a no-op succeeds without an audit row.

**UI**
- Users page under `/admin/settings/users`: per-user role selector + enable/disable, gated via `useCan(user.read/user.manage)`. `super_admin` and break-glass rows render read-only.
- API client (`listUsers` / `setUserRole` / `setUserStatus`), permission constants, settings nav entry.

**Spec/docs**: `openspec/changes/user-role-management/` (proposal + design + tasks + `server-identity-authorization` and `web-ui` deltas). `docs/authz.md` reframes the SQL pattern as the break-glass alternative.

No migration: the `users` (status) and `role_bindings` (expires_at) columns already exist.

## Out of scope (deferred)

Invite-new-user, multi-tenant / host-group scope, custom roles, OIDC group-to-role mapping (#136). All converge on the same `role_bindings` table additively.

## Testing

- Go: real-DB integration tests in `server/identity/internal/tests` covering list, set-role (replace + audit), disable/enable, and every guardrail, with `spec:` markers for the new scenarios.
- UI: vitest for the Users page (list, role change, read-only rows, gating, errors), the api client, and the settings nav.
- Gates green locally: `go test ./server/...`, golangci-lint (custom), dash lint, `spectrace check --strict` (423/423, 0 invalid refs), `openspec validate --strict`, `cd ui && npm test` (320 tests) + eslint + tsc, prettier/markdownlint.
- Manual QA on `task dev:server` (Chrome + API): list renders with correct permission gating, a role change round-trips through the React dropdown -> fetch/CSRF -> server -> DB, and the audit row is written.

author: edwinjhlee
body:
macvision wraps Apple's `Vision` framework in a tiny Swift binary — the "sight" layer of the ljh-sh agent IO stack (`macli`=system, `maclisten`=hearing, `macvision`=sight, `macmlx`=reason). All output is compact JSON for pipes and agents.

## What's in v0.1.0

8 subcommands, all verified on arm64 / macOS 26.5.1 / Swift 6.3:

| cmd | Vision request | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ocr` | `VNRecognizeTextRequest` | multi-language (`--lang zh-Hans,en-US`), confidence + bbox |
| `classify` | `VNClassifyImageRequest` / `VNRecognizeAnimalsRequest` | `--animals` |
| `detect` | faces / rects / barcodes / text-regions / horizon | single pass |
| `document` | `VNDetectDocumentSegmentationRequest` | outline for crop/deskew |
| `salient` | saliency request | attention/objectness heatmap PNG |
| `feature` | `VNGenerateImageFeaturePrintRequest` | vector; `--compare` distance |
| `daemon` | — | long-lived FIFO daemon, NDJSON IPC |
| `doctor` | — | environment + capability matrix |

Image input: file path · `-` stdin base64 · `--clipboard` · `--screen`.

## Design decisions

- **Zero external Swift deps.** Hand-rolled `Cmd` framework, mirroring maclisten (the shipping reference). `Vision`/`CoreGraphics`/`CoreImage`/`CoreVideo`/`AppKit` are all system frameworks — no model download.
- **Bounding boxes = pixel `[x,y,w,h]`, top-left origin** (the convention agents map to screen coords), plus a normalized `norm` copy.
- **No `NSApplication` run loop** for image work — `Vision.perform(_:)` is synchronous (unlike audio tools).
- **`daemon` IPC = FIFO + NDJSON, not HTTP** — x-cmd-style, shell-native (`echo > req.fifo; cat res.fifo`).

## Verification

- ✅ `swift build -c release` and `swift build`
- ✅ `swift test` — **7/7 pass** (geometry flip, parser, daemon encode/error paths, doctor)
- ✅ Real scenario: rendered a CN+EN test image → `macvision ocr --lang zh-Hans,en-US` recovered all 6 lines, **Chinese accuracy >90%**
- ✅ FIFO daemon served `doctor` + `ocr` end-to-end
- ✅ `feature a.jpg --compare a.jpg` → distance `0`

```
$ macvision ocr /tmp/macvision-test.png --lang zh-Hans,en-US | jq -r '.texts[].text'
GitHub:ljh-sh/macvision 2026-06-21
macvision OCR测试
Vision framework 中文识别准确率
The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
你好，世界！这是一段用于验证OCR 的中文文字。
错误代码：ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED（0×2AF7）
```

## Repo surface

Mirrors maclisten's layout: README (cn + en), `docs/` Jekyll site, CI/release/CodeQL/Scorecard/Pages workflows, `.x-cmd` release scripts with reproducible-build + no-leak verification.

## Out of scope (tracked in ROADMAP)

v0.2 = hardening + Homebrew formula + signed releases; v0.3 = face landmarks, pose, PDF input, per-language OCR matrix; later = video tracking, camera input.

author: danieljtrujillo
body:
feat(edit): real-time psychoacoustic FX rack, granular morph, spatializer

Add a context-agnostic insert-effect engine (rackEffects.ts) that builds the
same node subgraph for live preview and the offline bounce: crossfeed,
missing-fundamental bass, true M/S widening, aural excitation, HRTF
spatialization, and an equal-loudness contour. Master-bus and per-track FX
chains route through liveMixer with a topology-signature reconcile, so param
moves push into the running nodes without a rebuild and only the editor mix is
processed (library/DJ/sequencer audio is untouched).

Add the granular identity-bleed morph (Phase M): donor A is indexed into a
grain corpus and host B's onsets drive grain selection inside
granular-morph.worklet.js, controlled from MetamorphPanel via morphEngine.
Add SpatializerPad with onset-sliced Teleport motion backed by the FFT-free,
time-domain analysis in audioAnalysis.ts. editorStore carries the master and
per-track chain state; wavEncode renders a morph pass back into a timeline clip.

fix(media): build large blobs from arrayBuffer; readable instrument dropdown

fetchRetry now constructs the Blob from an in-memory ArrayBuffer rather than
res.blob(). On a large body Chrome materializes res.blob() into its disk-backed
Blob store, and when the disk is constrained that write fails with
net::ERR_FAILED after a 200, surfacing here as "Failed to fetch". Verified live:
a 66 MB WAV fails every time via res.blob() and succeeds every time via
new Blob([arrayBuffer]).

Also restyle the MIDI InstrumentPicker dropdown for a dark color scheme so the
native option list stays legible.

author: washka20
body:
Срез S5 эпика aa-improvements (follow-up #706). Добавляет фильтр "Ночь" во вкладку "Доступные мне" охранника.

## Что
- BE: фильтр `night=true` поверх инварианта видимости мест. Ночь = окно въезда `[entry_time_from, entry_time_to]` пересекает `[22:00, 06:00)` (22:00 включительно, 06:00 нет). При активном поиске не применяется (показывает оба, как `completed`).
- FE: тоггл "Ночь" рядом с "Завершённые" (тот же паттерн: state, buildParams/syncUrl/hasActiveFilters/reset, URL `?night=1`).

## Как считается ночь (SQL)
`entry_time_from/to` - `varchar(20)`, формат непоследовательный (`HH:MM` и `HH:MM:SS`). Предикат берёт `substr(...,1,5)` -> нормализует к `HH:MM`; зеро-паддинг часа делает лексикографическое сравнение хронологическим - без `::time`-каста, который упал бы (500) на нечисловом мусоре в колонке. Окно non-wrap (from<=to) - ночь, если конец `>= 22:00` или начало `< 06:00`; окно через полночь (from>to) всегда ночь (содержит 00:00). Пустые/NULL-времена не ночь.

## Тесты
- `TestAvailableAttachments_FilterByNight` - граничные времена (22:00 вкл, 06:00 искл, смешанный формат, wrap через полночь, NULL-окно).
- `TestAvailableAttachments_NightIgnoredDuringSearch` - поиск отменяет ночной предикат.
- `TestAvailableAttachments_NightDoesNotBypassPlaceGate` - ночное вложение на чужом месте скрыто.
- `TestAvailableAttachments_NightAndCompletedCombined` - оба тоггла -> только ночные завершённые.
- FE-спека тоггла "Ночь" (включение/снятие/диплинк).

## Ревью
code-reviewer: GO, блокеров нет. Жёлтые учтены: добавлены swagger `@Param night`/`completed`, тест place-gate для night, тест комбо. Полный `go test ./...` локально ловит коллизию ОБЩЕЙ тест-БД с параллельной сессией (`internal/database` partition-тест, не связан с диффом); `internal/handlers` изолированно зелёный - SQL исполняется.

Генерируемые `docs/swagger.*` не регенерил (их сейчас правит другая сессия; `completed` тоже исторически без регена).

author: lorecajp
body:
## 症状
えみの給与取込で、**年末調整の還付**がある明細（2025年12月分・支給日2026/01/31）で `差引支給額（¥112,163）と計算値（¥106,933）が一致しません` の警告が出る。

## 原因（実データで特定）
PDFのテキスト構造:
```
支給合計 → 106,933        (総支給)
控除
  年調過不足税額 → -5,230
控除合計 → -5,230          (マイナス＝還付)
振込支給額 → 112,163       (= 106,933 − (−5,230))
```
`parse.ts` の数値判定 `/^[\d,，]+$/` が**マイナス符号を許可していない**ため、`控除合計 = -5,230` を拾えず控除0件に。結果、計算 net＝総支給106,933のまま → 明細の振込112,163と食い違い → **警告は正しい**が、このまま確定すると**還付5,230が記録から漏れる**（収入だけ登録され振込額と不一致）。

## 修正
- **parse.ts**: 数値判定を符号付き（`- − ▲ △`）に対応。マイナスの `控除合計` も拾い、`年末調整還付` という1行の控除として保持。
- **PayslipImport `save()`**: マイナス控除は還付なので、**金額を正にして収入（type=income）として登録**（控除＝支出のまま負数にすると `amount>0` 制約に反するため）。これで計算 net＝総支給−控除合計＝**振込支給額に一致 → 警告も消える**。収入はカテゴリ未指定でも年間ビューの「収入」行に集計される（人タグ=えみは保持）。
- **レビュー画面**: マイナス行は「還付＝収入として記録」と明示。
- **CLAUDE.md §6** にこのケースを追記。

## 記録のされ方（このPR適用後・1月分の例）
- 収入: 106,933（えみ給料）
- 収入: 5,230（メモ「年末調整還付」／未分類・人=えみ）
- → 月の収入 112,163、税の支出は計上なし、収支 +112,163（振込額と一致）

## 検証
- 1月分（還付）: `控除合計 -5,230` を取得、計算 net 112,163＝振込 → 警告なし ✅
- 5月分（控除なしの通常月）: `控除合計 0`、控除0件・警告なし（**回帰なし**）✅
- `npm run check` エラー0 / `npm run build` 成功。

## 注意
取込は**必ずレビュー画面で確認してから確定**なので、デプロイ後も勝手に保存はされません。還付の扱いを「専用カテゴリにしたい」等あればレビュー画面で変更可、または方針変更します。

author: dscho
body:
Currently, `/deploy` spawns _two_ workflow runs for regular MINGW packages: one that builds the `clangarm64` variant of the package, and one that combines the `mingw32` and `mingw64` builds.

(Exceptions: `git-credential-manager`, `git-lfs` and `wintoast`, where the executables are not actually built using the MINGW toolchains provided by the MSYS2 project.)

With the currently ongoing [migration](https://github.com/git-for-windows/git-sdk-64/pull/117) from MINGW64 to UCRT64, it is as good a time as any to split that combined build, and simply trigger separate workflow runs for all the separate MINGW flavors (`MINGW_ARCH` in MSYS2 parlance).

This _also_ prepares for dramatically restricting the set of packages to be updated in the 32-bit builds of Git for Windows: Even though Git for Windows promises to provide MinGit 32-bit builds [until 2029](https://gitforwindows.org/32-bit#until-2029-mingit-only-32-bit-support), the uphill battle to maintain 32-bit support requires making concessions by focusing on an even smaller set of components that _must_ be updated for that architecture. I am thinking about cURL, OpenSSL and OpenSSH, and stopping to update, say, PCRE2 and xpdf-tools for 32-bit. Bash, for example, is [no longer updated](https://github.com/git-for-windows/gfw-helper-github-app/pull/192) for 32-bit at all.

## Summary

Full implementation of all backlog items identified in the project audit. Builds on the previous critical/high/medium fixes already in this branch.

### Security Hardening
- **CSRF token rotation**: Token rotated after each successful mutation; `X-New-CSRF-Token` header sent back; `csrf-handler.js` updated to capture it immediately
- **SecurityAuditService wired up**: Login failures, CSRF violations, and rate limit hits now all log to `audit_logs` via `SecurityAuditService::log()`
- **Redis for RateLimiter**: Optional Redis backend via `REDIS_HOST`/`REDIS_PORT`/`REDIS_PASSWORD` env vars; falls back to file-based on any error
- **2FA enforcement for admin**: Admin login blocked with 403 if TOTP not yet configured; returns `totp_setup_required: true` in JSON

### Password Reset Flow
- New `password_reset_tokens` table (auto-migrated in `db.php`)
- `POST /api/auth.php?action=forgot_password`: generates 64-char token, enqueues reset email, rate-limited (5/15min per IP), no user enumeration
- `POST /api/auth.php?action=reset_password`: validates token, updates hash, marks token used
- `login.html`: "Забыли пароль?" link, forgot form, reset form (shown when URL has `?action=reset&token=...`)

### PHPMailer
- Added `phpmailer/phpmailer ^6.9` to `composer.json`
- `EmailService::sendSmtp()` now delegates to PHPMailer when available; falls back to raw socket
- PHPMailer handles proper TLS cert verification, STARTTLS/SMTPS, AUTH, UTF-8

### Telegram Bot Enhancements
- `TelegramService::notifyLetterAssignment()`: sends Telegram DM to users linked to assigned members when a letter is created/updated
- `LetterPersistenceService::syncLetterMembers()`: detects newly assigned members and triggers notification

### User Profile Page
- New `api/profile.php`: GET (fetch profile), PUT (update name/email/password with current-password verify), POST `?action=photo` (upload with finfo MIME check), DELETE `?action=photo`

### Bulk Operations

### SRI Hashes
- New `scripts/generate_sri.sh`: computes sha384 hashes for Bootstrap CSS/JS and Icons CSS via curl + openssl
- Run at deployment time; CDN blocked in CI environment so hashes can't be pre-embedded

### Security Tests
- New `tests/SecurityTest.php`: 21 tests covering CSRF generation/rotation/bypass/enforcement, rate limiter allow/block/per-identifier, file upload MIME detection, password hashing

author: fkiene
body:
## What

Adds the interactive cost-breakdown dashboard to `llmtrim status`. On a terminal,
`status` opens a tabbed TUI (Overview / Sessions / Detail) showing what you saved,
what you paid, the daily trend, per-model and per-session breakdowns, and where each
session's tokens went. Piped or redirected output keeps the plain snapshot, so scripts
are unaffected.

## How it's built

- **`llmtrim-core`**: a per-source token attribution engine maps each request's tokens to
  its blocks (system prompt, tool schemas, tool results, MCP servers/tools, messages, output).
- **Ledger**: a breakdown turn/block schema, recorded per proxied request in `serve`, with a
  read-only open path (`query_only`, no prune) and a single-pass window query for sessions.
- **`monitor`**: cost view-models and one shared `overview_data()` that the binary and the
  asset generator both call, so the numeric derivation can't drift.
- **TUI**: ratatui, refreshed on a background thread so the UI never blocks on SQLite.
  Selectable Catppuccin themes (persisted), update/repair affordances when relevant.
- **Assets**: `assets/status-watch-{dark,light}.svg` are rendered from the real TUI buffers by
  a gated `#[cfg(test)]` generator (bars/gauges as vector graphics, real sanitized ledger
  numbers), embedded in the README.

## Review

Four reviewers ran (three code, one architecture). Fixes applied: removed the duplicated
Overview derivation (now shared in `monitor::overview_data`), dropped tracked `tmp/` scratch
docs, logged the refresh-thread panic and a JSON parse failure, released the idle read-write
ledger handle during the TUI, reconciled the cost tree's un-named direct rows, and tightened
several comments. The branch history was reshaped into seven logical commits, and an unrelated
bench-snapshot deletion that had been bundled in was excluded.

## Coverage

Logic layers are well covered (monitor 86%, tracking 92%, attribution 85%, config 92%,
db 98%, export 89%). `app.rs` (41%) and `palette.rs` (38%) are lower by design: the real
terminal `run()` loop, interactive key handlers, the env-gated SVG generator, and the
per-flavor color accessors don't run under `cargo test`; the render logic is covered via a
headless `TestBackend`.

## Notes

The architecture reviewer suggested splitting the SVG asset work into a second PR; left as one
here for review, happy to split if preferred.

author: raphaelvigee
body:
## What

`heph.core.pkg()` is documented as returning the **current package path**, but the example value included a leading `//`:

- `website/docs/plugins/buildfile.md` → `"//tools/build"`
- `plugins/heph-expert/skills/heph/references/authoring.md` → `//tools/build`

## Why

The Addresses reference (`website/docs/reference/addresses.md`) defines the terms precisely:

```
//lib/auth:lib
  └──┬──┘ └┬┘
  package  name
```

- **package** — the workspace-relative directory, *after the `//`* (root package is the empty string, written `//:name`).
- An **address** is the whole `//`-prefixed `//package:name` string.

So the `//` marks an *address*, not a *package path*. A package path is `tools/build` (or `""` for root), never `//tools/build`. The example contradicted the repo's own definition.

This updates both the docs page and its reference twin together, per the reference-drift rule in `CLAUDE.md`.

## Note

This fix is based on the repo's own internal definitions of "package" vs "address" — I wasn't able to reach the heph engine source from this environment to confirm the builtin's exact runtime string. If `pkg()` is actually intended to return the `//`-prefixed form, the wording "current package path" would be the thing to fix instead.

## Summary

This PR sets up [CodSpeed](https://codspeed.io) to continuously measure the performance of Sury in CI, so performance regressions are caught automatically on every pull request.

The repository already had a benchmark.js suite in `packages/e2e` (`Benchmark.res`). This integration reuses that suite directly rather than introducing a parallel one.

## Changes

- **Benchmark harness**: Wrapped the existing benchmark.js `Suite` with `withCodSpeed` from `@codspeed/benchmark.js-plugin`. The change is applied to both the ReScript source (`Benchmark.res`) and its committed generated output (`Benchmark.res.mjs`) so they stay in sync. When not running under CodSpeed, the suite behaves exactly as before.
- **Dependency**: Added `@codspeed/benchmark.js-plugin` as a dev dependency of `packages/e2e` (lockfile updated).
- **CI workflow**: Added `.github/workflows/codspeed.yml`. It installs dependencies with pnpm and runs the benchmarks through `CodSpeedHQ/action@v4` in `simulation` mode, using OIDC authentication. It triggers on pushes to `main`, on pull requests, and via `workflow_dispatch` (to let CodSpeed generate baseline data).
- **README**: Added the CodSpeed badge.

## Validation

The setup was verified locally with the CodSpeed CLI:

```
codspeed run --mode simulation -- node ./src/benchmark/Benchmark.res.mjs
```

All 19 benchmarks were measured and reported successfully under CPU simulation.

## Notes

- The benchmarks run on the standard `ubuntu-24.04` GitHub-hosted runner, consistent with the existing CI. Simulation mode is hardware-agnostic, so no specialized runners are required.
- Once this is merged and CodSpeed has baseline data, performance reports will appear directly on pull requests.

## Next steps

- Merge this PR so CodSpeed can collect a performance baseline from `main`.
- Review subsequent PRs for the automatic CodSpeed performance report.

## Wave-1 cheap fidelity applies — faq (audit/145) + legal trio (audit/146)

Per E's recon (`audit/145-faq-fidelity-recon`, `audit/146-legal-trio-fidelity-recon`). Both screens were already near-fidelity; this closes the **buildable LAYOUT/COMP gaps only** (colour/chrome settled by audit/126 + 127). FROZEN: none.

### audit/145 — FAQ (`399bae4e`)
- **F3 — "Email" mailto CTA.** The contact-support card gains an `Email` button (`mailto:info@bookbed.io`), mirroring the existing `url_launcher` precedent in `about_screen` / `profile_screen`.
- **F2 — accordion active-state.** Each FAQ row is now a small stateful `_FaqExpansionCard`; its leading category disc flips to **filled-primary with a white icon** while expanded (handoff active-state), via `ExpansionTile.onExpansionChanged`.
- **Breakpoint hygiene.** The body-column width gates are named `_kFaqDesktopColMin` (1024) / `_kFaqTabletColMin` (600). They read the layout box (content-fit reflow) → **intentionally NOT migrated to 1200**.
- **Data-honest omissions (kept):** helpful-vote (D1) and live-chat "Razgovor uživo" (D2) — no backend, not faked.

### audit/146 — Legal trio (`a9a29cbd`)
- **LG1 option B — box-driven 2-col breakpoint.** Applied uniformly to terms / privacy / cookies: keep the two-column-reader threshold at **900** (named `_kLegalTwoColMin`) and convert the decision from `MediaQuery.of(context).size.width` (device width) to a `LayoutBuilder` `constraints.maxWidth` read (the layout box).
- **Why kept at 900, not 1200:** sidebar(240) + gap(48) + doc column fit inside the existing `980` clamp from 900px up — a content-fit reflow, not a device-class pivot. Migrating to 1200 would drop the premium 2-col reader across the **1024–1199 band including iPad-landscape**.
- The `LegalTabsRow` `pushReplacement` nav contract (pre-auth + post-auth) is untouched. **"Preuzmi PDF" stays omitted** (D1) — no PDF generator, data-honest.

### Gates (verified locally at tip)
- `flutter analyze`: 0 errors / 0 warnings; **0 net-new** infos (97 pre-existing, none in the 4 touched files).
- `flutter test`: **all 1583 pass** (incl. the existing `faq_screen` smoke test).
- `flutter build web --no-tree-shake-icons`: clean.
- `dart format`: clean (pre-commit hook).

### Render eyeball (auth-free, real `AppTheme` + fonts)
faq + legal rendered at mobile(390) / tablet(768) / desktop(1024–1100) × light/dark. Confirmed: Email CTA present (mobile+desktop+dark); accordion disc flips to filled-primary/white when expanded; legal **stacked < 900 / 2-col ≥ 900** boundary preserved (2-col intact at 1024), across terms + privacy + cookies, light + dark.

### ⚠️ Golden note (P6 dependency)
The recon flow calls for `flutter test --tags golden` → faq golden RED → `--update-goldens` → commit re-blessed baseline. **P6 (golden net) is not on `main` yet** (no `matchesGoldenFile` / `golden`-tagged tests / baselines on `origin/main`), so that step cannot run on a main-based branch and **is not in this PR** (committing baselines here would entangle it with P6). The render eyeball above was done with a temporary local harness (deleted, not committed). **Once P6 merges, faq's golden baseline will need a re-bless** (rebase this branch onto post-P6 main + `--update-goldens` faq, or re-bless after both land).

author: indyjonesnl
body:
## What

Two more instances of the skipped-validation-on-update gap (cf.
EndpointSlice #1359, Ingress #1360, NetworkPolicy #1361):

- **LimitRange** (core/v1) — upstream update strategy re-runs
  `ValidateLimitRange` on the new object.
- **PodDisruptionBudget** (policy/v1) — upstream `ValidateUpdate` re-runs
  `ValidatePodDisruptionBudget` (no spec immutability;
  `pkg/registry/policy/poddisruptionbudget/strategy.go:112`).

rusternetes validated on **create** but both **update** handlers
persisted PUTs unchecked, so an invalid spec (duplicate limit type;
`minAvailable`+`maxUnavailable` both set; …) could be written via update.

## How

- `crates/api-server/src/handlers/limitrange.rs`: run `validate_limit_range`
  on update before persisting.
- `crates/api-server/src/handlers/poddisruptionbudget.rs`: run
  `validate_pod_disruption_budget` on update before persisting.

## Test

`crates/api-server/tests/limitrange_pdb_update_validation_test.rs` —
in-process `TestApiServer`: for each, create valid → PUT invalid rejected
(422) → valid PUT succeeds (200). Both pass.

author: sebakwie
body:
## Make local setup judge-ready (`SETUP.md` + remove the inconveniences)

Adds a complete local setup guide **and fixes the things that made local eval annoying**,
so a judge can go zero-to-dashboard with no manual surgery.

### Fixes (so the quick start is genuinely one-shot)
- **Demo login now works out of the box.** `seed.sql`'s auth fix-up `UPDATE` only
  targeted `tester@solar.test`, so the demo user `demo-api@solar.test` was left with null
  GoTrue token fields → `invalid_credentials`. Now applied to **both** users, and dropped
  `phone = ''` (it collided on `users_phone_key` when set on two rows). **Verified:** after
  `db reset`, both users return an `access_token` with **no manual repair**.
- **`apps/web/.env.local.example` added** so `setup.sh` auto-creates the env file Next
  actually reads (`apps/web/.env.local`) — removing the env-location gotcha for the
  scripted path. Local Supabase defaults only; **no secrets**.

### `SETUP.md`
- **"For evaluators / judges" section** up top: there's **no hosted demo** → run locally
  (~10 min), the demo login, **what you can evaluate with no API keys** vs. what needs
  `OPENAI_API_KEY` / ElevenLabs, and a table mapping each thing to judge → where to click.
- One-shot quick start (`setup.sh` then `pnpm web#dev`), env reference, DB reset/seed/types,
  ports, first-look click-through of the 5 seed leads, quality gates, troubleshooting, repo map.
- The old manual login repair is demoted to a collapsed fallback for older checkouts.
- Linked from `README.md`.
